articles.summary_zh: 文：查尔斯·加德纳（Charles Gardner）——在第二次世界大战南太平洋的一场海战中，一名日本水兵所在的驱逐舰被美国人击沉，他的大多数战友都淹死了。令人惊奇的是，尽管鱼雷官新谷通晴与其他人一起被卷入波涛之下，随着战舰的沉没，但他却奇迹般地在这场1942年的灾难中幸存下来。（只有18名……）  这篇文章《二战日本战俘在战俘营中找到“自由”》最初发表在《上帝报道》上。
articles.title_zh: 二战日本战俘在战俘营中找到“自由”
articles.content: By Charles Gardner — When a Japanese sailor’s destroyer was sunk by the Americans in a World War II South Pacific battle, most of his companions drowned. Amazingly, even though he was sucked underneath the waves with others as the ship went down, torpedo officer Michiharu Shinya somehow survived this 1942 disaster. (Only 18 of the 200-strong crew did). But he would rather have died at that point as his people had been indoctrinated to believe that it was shameful to be captured. Nevertheless, he was badly wounded but nursed back to health by medics. In time, he was picked up and eventually taken to a Prisoner-of-War camp at Featherston, near Wellington, in New Zealand, where he was to spend the next three years, as Don Stephens records in his inspirational book War and Grace (Evangelical Press, an imprint of 10Publishing). Shinya and his fellow inmates were treated with much kindness (in sharp contrast to the torture often experienced by Allied prisoners at the hands of the Japanese). Being showered with gifts at Christmas, a feast he knew nothing about, seemed especially strange. However, he was determined not to be ‘taken in’ by the Christian teaching offered after some of the prisoners requested spiritual help and a Japanese Bible was made available. That is until he chanced upon an article entitled ‘Sorrow in Victory’ in which the author quoted a ‘Hebrew prophet’ as saying: “Those who hope in the Lord will renew their strength. They shall soar on wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary; they will walk and not be faint.” It made a deep impression on him, and he was determined to find out where it came from. Assuming it was from the Old Testament, he began reading the Bible, starting at Genesis chapter 1. Eventually, to his joy, he discovered that the profound words were from the Book of the prophet Isaiah (chapter 40, verse 31). After flagging somewhat in his search, he found himself hospitalised with malaria when a friend brought him a booklet called The Reason Why explaining the way to salvation. It so happened that the camp’s chaplain, Pastor Hessell Troughton, had been a missionary to Japan and spoke the language. Shinya joined others in his Bible studies and came to know and love Jesus as his Saviour. So much did this “complete freedom” now rule his life that prison had morphed into what he described as “a unique paradise on earth”. He never looked back after that and became convinced that his post-war calling would be in service of his Lord. When he finally returned home, his family were shocked to see him alive for he had been reported as killed in action. He had also given a false name to his captors because of the supposed shame of falling into enemy hands. Shinya subsequently became a pastor and prolific writer and translator following years of theological study both in Tokyo and the US. The Old Testament, he came to believe, demonstrated that sin is “the ultimate problem of mankind” and clearly pointed to Christ as the answer. On seeking to understand why so few Japanese became Christians, he felt it was partly due to their pride borne of believing they were a superior race. As for those three Christmases he spent in New Zealand, author Don Stephens writes: “Of all the gifts he received, the one he valued most was ‘the boundless and deep grace and peace of God in the Lord Jesus Christ’.” The post WWII Japanese POW found ‘freedom’ in camp first appeared on God Reports .
articles.content_zh:
查尔斯·加德纳编著: 当一艘日本水手的驱逐舰在二战南太平洋战役中被美国人击沉时,大部分同伴溺毙. 令人惊奇的是,尽管随着船只的下沉,他与其他人一起被吸在海浪下,但鱼雷军官Michiharu Shinya却不知何故幸免于1942年的灾难。 (200人的船员中只有18人这样做).

但他宁愿死在那个时候,因为他的族人被灌输相信被俘虏是可耻的. 然而,他受了重伤,但被医护人员喂养。

在时间上,他被接了起来,最终被带到新西兰惠灵顿附近的费瑟斯顿(Featherston)的战俘营,在那里他将度过接下来的三年,正如唐·斯蒂芬斯在他的励志书"战争与格蕾丝"(福音出版社,10Publishing的印记)中记载的那样.

信也和同狱囚犯受到很大程度的善待(与盟军囚犯经常在日本人手中遭受的酷刑形成鲜明对比). 在圣诞节用礼物淋浴 一个他一无所知的宴会 看起来特别奇怪

然而,在一些囚犯要求精神帮助和提供日本圣经后,他决心不再接受基督教教义的 " 接纳 " 。 直到他看到一篇题为“为胜利而悲伤”的文章,作者在文章中引用了一位“赫布鲁先知”的话:“那些希望主复活的人。 他们将像鹰一样飞翔,

他们将奔驰,而不会疲倦,他们将走路,而不会晕倒。 这给他留下了深刻的印象,他下定决心要找出它来自何处. 假设它来自旧约,他开始阅读圣经,从创世纪第一章开始. 最终,在他的喜悦中,他发现深刻的文字来自先知以赛亚的经典(第40章第31节).

在搜索中略微浮出水面后,他发现自己患上了疟疾,一位朋友给他带了一本小册子,名为《原因》,解释救世之路。 难民营的牧师Hessell Troughton牧师曾是日本的传教士, 信也加入了其他人的圣经研究,来到了了解和热爱耶稣作为他的救世主.

这种“完全自由”现在统治了他的生活,监狱变成了他所称的“地球上独一无二的天堂”。 他从此之后再也没有回头看,并且确信他的战后召唤将会为他的主服务. 当他最终回家时,家人震惊地看到他活着,因为他被报道为阵亡.

他还给抓捕者取了一个假名,因为被假定是落入敌人手中的耻辱。 在东京和美国多年的神学研究之后,信也后来成为一名牧师和多产作家和翻译。 他逐渐相信,《旧约》表明了罪恶是“人类的最终问题”,并明确指出基督是答案。

在试图理解为什么如此少的日本人成为基督徒时,他感到部分是由于他们的自豪感,因为他们相信他们是优越的种族。

至于他在新西兰度过的三个圣诞节,作者Don Stephens写道:"在他收到的所有礼物中,他最珍视的一件是`上帝在耶稣基督中无限和深厚的恩惠与和平 ' 。 日本战俘在营地发现「自由」,

articles.title_zh: 在西部明星的阴影下：格罗弗·刘易斯、拉里·麦克默特里和文字的胜利
articles.content: With The Grover Lewis Reader: Splendor in the Short Grass and Western Star , the newest biography of Larry McMurtry, in hand, I load my truck and head toward Archer City, Texas, accompanied by my wife, Melanie, and our friend Eliott. Archer City is, of course, McMurtry country, a small Texas town made famous through the literary imagination of one of America’s most celebrated novelists. Having written about McMurtry’s faith—or lack thereof—in a previous article , following an earlier visit to Archer City, I’m returning with a somewhat different interest. This time, my attention turns to Grover Lewis, the gifted journalist, critic, and poet whose life intersected with McMurtry’s during their college years. Lewis’ story, however, begins not with literary achievement but with almost unimaginable tragedy. As a child, he experienced the devastating loss of both parents when his father murdered his mother and was subsequently shot with the same gun, either by his dying wife or another person present. Lewis was only eight years old. It is difficult to imagine a more horrific beginning. Yet rather than allowing that tragedy to become the entirety of his story, Lewis eventually found a voice through literature. Perhaps the cards life dealt him gave him plenty to write about. Or perhaps writing became his way of making sense of a world that had revealed its cruelty far too early. In his autobiographical poem “Hillbilly Song,” Lewis writes: “You asked me once, Ann/Over coffee gone cold with talk/In your mother’s rain-drowsy/House, who they were, how it/Was with them in their breathless/Time in the wilds of years.” For Lewis, those early years were indeed wild. But they were also the soil from which his literary imagination would eventually grow. A Life in Words Born in Texas in 1934, Grover Lewis emerged as a distinctive voice in American journalism, particularly through his cultural criticism and reporting on the rapidly changing landscape of the 1960s and 1970s. He became known for his sharp observations, literary flair, and ability to capture the personalities and contradictions of American culture, even if he occasionally stretched the truth in the telling. His work appeared in prominent publications, including Rolling Stone , where his reporting helped establish his reputation as an insightful, sometimes cutting observer of popular culture. Lewis was more than a journalist, however. He was a poet and literary craftsman, someone who understood that words could do more than convey information. They could illuminate the human condition, expose its contradictions, and perhaps even provide a measure of healing. Grover Lewis (ChatPGT) Continuing “Hillbilly Song,” Lewis ponders: “At last, breathless and dry-mouthed/With private desire in the blue,/Swollen dark, we all lie down together—/My mother, my father, their perishing/Dreams, and I this unborn prisoner son…” There is something haunting about these lines. The dead remain present. The past refuses to disappear. And the poet, even as an adult, seems to wrestle with the circumstances that shaped his entrance into the world. Yet the very act of writing suggests something else: a refusal to remain silent. Two Texans, Two Literary Paths Lewis and Larry McMurtry crossed paths as students at North Texas State College, now the University of North Texas, during the 1950s. Both were young Texans drawn to literature and the possibilities of the written word. Their friendship developed within a shared intellectual environment, one that encouraged reading, conversation, and the pursuit of literary ambitions. Although their careers eventually followed different paths—McMurtry toward novels, screenplays, and literary fame, Lewis toward journalism, poetry, and cultural criticism—they shared an interest in the complexities of American life. 与《格罗弗·刘易斯读者:短草中的辉煌与西部之星》,拉里·麦克默特里的最新传记, 手持,我装载我的卡车并前往德克萨斯州阿彻城, 由我的妻子梅兰妮和我们的朋友埃利奥特陪同。 阿彻城当然是麦克默特里国家,一个通过美国最著名的小说家之一的文学想象而成名的德克萨斯小镇.

在之前访问Archer城后, 我对McMurtry的信仰(或缺乏信仰)有一番兴趣, 这一次,我转而关注有天赋的记者、评论家和诗人格罗弗·刘易斯,他在大学时代的生活与麦克默特里的生活交织在一起。

然而,刘易斯的故事并非从文学成就开始,而是从几乎难以想象的悲剧开始. 他从小就经历了父母的惨痛损失,当时他的父亲谋杀了他的母亲,随后被他即将死亡的妻子或在场的其他人用同一把枪射杀。 刘易斯才八岁 很难想象一个更可怕的开端。

然而,刘易斯最终没有让这场悲剧成为他的全部故事,而是通过文学找到了声音. 也许他命中注定的卡片 给他写了很多东西 或写作成为他理解世界的方式, 这个世界已经揭示了它的残酷性,还为时过早。

刘易斯在自传诗“Hillbilly Song”中写道 : “ 你曾经问过我,Ann/Over咖啡随着谈话而变得冷淡,在你妈妈的雨滴/住所里,他们是谁,他们在无气息的年代/在野外时如何。 ” 对刘易斯来说,那些早年的确很狂野. 但它们也是他的文学想象最终会成长的土壤.

1934年出生于德克萨斯州的"言语生活"(A Life in Words Born in Texas),格罗弗·刘易斯(Grover Lewis)成为美国新闻业中一个有特色的代言人,特别是通过他对1960年代和1970年代迅速变化的地貌的文化批评和报道.

他以尖锐的观察,文学的才华,以及能够捕捉美国文化的个性和矛盾而闻名,即使他偶尔在讲述中伸张真理. 他的作品出现在包括滚石公司在内的著名出版物中,他的报道帮助他树立了自己作为有见地,有时剪切流行文化观察者的声誉.

然而,刘易斯不只是一名记者。 他是一位诗人和文学家,一个懂得文字可以比传递信息更有用的人. 它们可以揭示人类的状况,暴露其矛盾,甚至可能提供某种治疗方法。

Grover Lewis (ChatPGT) 继续“Hillbilly Song,” 刘易斯思考道:“最后,无气息和干燥的嘴唇/在蓝色的暗处私欲下,我们都躺在一起——/我的母亲、父亲、他们的死亡/梦想,我这个未出生的囚犯儿子......” 这些台词有些困扰。 死者仍然在场。 过去拒绝消失。

而诗人,即使作为一个成年人,似乎也与塑造他进入世界的环境相搏. 然而,写作本身就暗示了另一种情况:拒绝保持沉默。 两德克萨斯州立大学,两条文学道路刘易斯州立大学和拉里·麦克默特里(英语:Larry McMurtry)在1950年代作为北德克萨斯州立学院,即现在的北德克萨斯大学的学生跨过道路.

两人都是年轻的德克萨斯人,被吸引到文学和写字的可能性. 他们的友谊是在共同的知识环境中发展起来的,这种环境鼓励阅读,对话,追求文学野心.

尽管他们的职业生涯最终走的是不同的道路——小说、剧本和文学名人、刘易斯新闻、诗歌和文化批评——但他们对美国生活的复杂性有着共同的兴趣。 麦克默特里和刘易斯在大学期间(ChatGPT)都拥有超越德克萨斯州和美国西部神话的能力,认识到孤独,凝视

articles.summary_zh: 文：查尔斯·加德纳（Charles Gardner）——一位犹太籍陆军外科医生对一名年轻士兵的勇气感到惊叹，这名士兵在美国内战（1861-65）的葛底斯堡战役中身受重伤。为了挽救这个男孩的生命，马克斯·罗斯瓦利（Max Rossvally）博士不得不截肢，截掉了他的一条腿和一条胳膊。但这改变了他自己……  这篇题为《犹太军医在目睹病人的勇气后归向耶稣》的文章  最初发表在《上帝报道》上。
articles.title_zh: 犹太军医在目睹病人的勇气后归信耶稣
articles.content: Pastor Peter Colon portraying Major Rossvally in the movie of his story By Charles Gardner — A Jewish army surgeon was amazed by the courage of a young soldier badly wounded in the Battle of Gettysburg during the American Civil War (1861-65). Dr Max Rossvally was forced to amputate both a leg and arm in a bid to save the boy’s life. But it changed his own life. For the 17-year-old Drummer Boy – too young for frontline duty – refused chloroform or brandy to dull the pain. Charlie Coulson chose instead to trust in Jesus, his Lord and Saviour. The doctor – an army major and Orthodox Jew – was understandably stunned by the boy’s bravery, as well as his boldness in declaring his faith in Christ and imploring the officer (whom he knew to be Jewish) to put his own trust in Jesus, since he was also the Jewish Messiah. Max, however, was shaken rigid, and in a great dilemma, as he had always been taught to hate Jesus. For his people had largely rejected him as an ‘impostor’ and false Messiah. Charlie died just days later, apparently more concerned for the doctor’s eternal destiny than for his own painful exit from this life. Ten years later, Max found himself in a barber’s chair in New York once more being urged to trust in Jesus. Having explained the gospel, the barber promised to pray for him and said that, whenever he came in contact with a Jew, he felt it his duty to introduce him to the one who came for “the lost sheep of Israel” (Matthew 10:6). The surgeon subsequently boarded a train for a business meeting in Washington, where a newspaper advertisement drew him to a ‘revival’ service where the preacher echoed the messages he had heard from the barber and the boy soldier, leaving him in tears. He agonised at home in prayer for some time afterwards, struggling most of all with the thought that, if he accepted Christ, he would be going against all the advice and teaching he had known, not to mention the Jewish community as a whole. But he finally became convinced that Jesus was indeed the fulfilment of Old Testament prophecies (in particular, Genesis 49:10, Micah 5:2 and Isaiah 7:14). So he prayed: “O Lord God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. You know I am sincere in this thing. If Jesus Christ is the Son of God, reveal him to me this night, and I will accept him as my Messiah.” A long battle ensued, but his doubts were eventually replaced by joy and happiness as he praised God that he had found the true Shiloh, Ruler of Israel and Emmanuel. He was to pay a high price, however, as do all who follow Christ. His wife walked out on him; his parents disowned him. But he never gave up hope as he constantly prayed and reached out to his family. After 54 days, his wife joined him as a disciple of Jesus and, in time, his daughter also became a believer. But his son disowned him for many years until he was eventually reconciled both with his earthly and heavenly Father. In an extraordinary sequel some 18 months after he came to Christ, Max met up with Mrs Coulson, the mother of his dying young patient all those years earlier on the battlefield. With great joy, he was able to share how her son had set him on the path to a glorious future in Christ, which was to touch lives across the world, including my home county of Yorkshire in England. In fact, he came to live in Leeds to reach out to the Jewish community there and is buried at Lawnswood Cemetery in the city. An Irish friend of mine, Colin Nevin, has visited the grave, which includes an excerpt from one of the doctor’s hymns, I am Coming Soon, and was able to give a copy of Max’s story to a caretaker, so continuing the evangelist’s legacy more than a century after his death in 1892, aged 64. A 54-minute movie – Rossvally: From the Synagogue to the Saviour – has been produced on DVD and can apparently be ordered online. articles.content_zh:
牧师彼得·科隆在他的故事电影"查尔斯·加德纳"(By Charles Gardner)中描绘了罗斯瓦利少校——一位犹太军队外科医生对美国内战期间格底斯堡战役(1861-65)中一名年轻士兵严重受伤的勇气感到惊讶. Max Rossvally医生被迫截肢, 但这改变了他自己的生活。

对于17岁的Drummer Boy — — 年龄太小,无法承担前线任务 — — 拒绝氯仿或白兰地来消磨疼痛。 查理·科尔森选择了信任耶稣,他的主和救世主.

这位医生是一名陆军少校和正统犹太人,对男孩的勇敢以及他大胆地宣布对基督的信仰,恳求军官(他知道是犹太人)相信耶稣是可以理解的,因为他也是犹太弥赛亚。 然而,马克思被动摇僵硬,陷入了巨大的困境,因为他一直被教导要憎恨耶稣.

他的宗族曾否认他是一个 " 骗子 " 和假的弥赛亚。 Charlie在几天后就去世了,显然更关心医生的永恒命运,而不是他自己痛苦地离开这一生。 10年后,马克思发现自己在纽约的理发师座椅上再次被敦促信任耶稣.

在解释了福音之后,理发师答应为他祈祷,并说每当他与一个犹太人接触时,他觉得有义务将他介绍给前来寻找“迷失的以色列羊”的人(Matthew 10:6)。

外科医生随后登上火车在华盛顿举行商务会议,报纸的广告将他引向 " 复活 " 服务,传教士重复了他从理发师和男孩士兵那里听到的信息,使他流泪。

他在家里苦苦地祈祷了一段时间,他首先想到,如果他接受基督,他将反对他所知道的所有建议和教导,更不用说整个犹太社区了。 但他最终确信耶稣确实是"旧约预言"的实现(特别是创世纪49:10,米迦5:2和以赛亚7:14).

他就祈祷说:易卜拉欣、易司哈格、叶尔孤白的主啊! 你知道我对这件事很真诚 如果耶稣基督是上帝之子,那么今晚把他告诉我,我将接受他为我的弥赛亚。” 一场漫长的战斗随之而来,但他的疑虑最终被欢乐和幸福所取代,因为他称赞上帝找到了真正的希洛,以色列统治者和埃马纽埃尔.

但他要付出高昂的代价,跟随基督的所有人一样。 他的妻子抛弃了他;他的父母抛弃了他。 但是,他从未放弃过希望,因为他不断祈祷和联系家人。 在54天后,他的妻子作为耶稣的门徒加入了他,在时间上,他的女儿也成为了信徒.

但他的儿子与他断绝关系多年,直到他最终与他的大地父和天父都和解. 在他来到基督的大约18个月之后的一段非凡续集中,马克思在战场上遇见了那些年前他死去的年轻病人的母亲科尔森夫人.

他怀着极大的喜悦,得以分享她儿子如何使他踏上基督辉煌未来的道路,这就是触摸世界各地的生活,包括我的家乡英格兰约克郡. 事实上,他来到利兹居住,向那里的犹太社区伸出援手,并被埋在城内的草坪林墓地.

我的一个爱尔兰朋友科林·内文参观了这个坟墓,其中包括医生颂歌"I am Coming Soon"的节录,并且能够把马克思的故事复制给看守人,因此在1892年去世后一个多世纪的福音派传承下来,享年64岁.

一部54分钟的电影 — — Rossvally: 从Synagogue到救世主 — 已经在DVD上制作,显然可以在网上订购. 在目睹病人的勇气首次出现在上帝的报告之后,

articles.title_zh: 两只卡车轮胎和一只白鸽教会了我信靠上帝
articles.content: By Mike Shreve — Tent meeting in the 80s Evangelism has been my focus for 55 years, ministering throughout the United States and in 14 other nations. God mercifully saved me during the Jesus Revolution (1970), out of a hippie lifestyle and a passionate, though misguided pursuit of truth through far eastern religious practices (yoga and meditation). Shortly after encountering Jesus and being delivered, along with another brother in the Lord, I began hitchhiking around the country, preaching the Gospel on street corners and college campuses. That developed through the years into ministry in churches, auditoriums, conferences, and tent crusades. Supernatural provision and divine intervention has always carried me, through every phase of this five-and-a-half-decade-long adventure. However, the following story is a classic. For about 25 years I carried big Gospel tents around the country. At the time of this “miracle,” I was transporting a 60’ x 90’ tent from one city to the next in an old, dilapidated bus that kept introducing new challenges to our amateur mechanic skills (putting it mildly). One day, on our way to Tampa, Florida—unfortunately—we hit a large pothole in the road that put a serious dent in the rear left rim on which a large truck tire was mounted. From that point, the inner tube would not retain air, making it necessary to stop every thirty miles or so to fill it up again . . . and again . . . and again . . . making the trip painfully slow. Adding to the problem, the other rear tire was bald, and we had no spare (couldn’t afford one). So, a flat would have brought us to a complete standstill. Sometimes, I think back on those days (when our zeal for the Kingdom outran any wisdom we might have possessed), and I marvel at the many times God took care of us anyway (like the loving heavenly Father that He is). Thousands of pounds of equipment were packed into that groaning, creaking, rusty, decrepit bus — heavy canvas tent sections, metal poles, stakes, platform, and 300 chairs—and only a few days allowed in between cities for transit and setup. No, we really could not afford any setbacks. And yes, a lot of “faith prayers” were uttered during every trip (or were they “presumptive proclamations”—not sure—maybe a mix of the two). An old split rim tire mounted on an old bus Once we got to Tampa, attempting to be frugal, I visited the junkyards hoping to find a used replacement rim. As if they had conspired to dissuade me, every junkyard owner/manager shot down my hopes with a similar assessment, “Fella, you won’t find one of them old split-rims anywhere. They’re dangerous. When you try to mount a tire on one, they can snap open and injure somebody real bad, cutting off a hand, even killing a person. We melted ‘em all down as scrap metal.” (Go ahead, look them up online—they were even called “widow-makers.”) It was the same story everywhere I went. Nobody could help. Then three weeks passed and we had to pack the bus and head to our next location—Bessemer City, North Carolina. It was a college-level, biblically-sound course on developing long-suffering and patience: stopping every thirty miles or so to air up that unpredictable tire, pleading with God to somehow supernaturally assist us in our journey by making sure none of the tires blew. Somehow, we made it—around 600 miles—stopping about 25 times. Then an incredible miracle happened! God did it and I still feel awestruck, just writing about it. As we turned into the fairgrounds area, right in the middle of the entrance were two brand new, neatly-stacked truck tires (unclaimed), exactly the size we used on the bus—mounted (you guessed it!) on the very same split rims our bus required. Talk about worshiping God—we launched into a praise session right then and there! What were the odds? We all knew it had to be God. Jehovah-Jireh (the Lord our provider) had fulfilled His amazing promise to do “exceedingly, abundantly above all” we could ask or think (Ephesians 3:20). Then li
articles.content_zh:
麦克史瑞夫 80年代的帐篷会议是我55年来的焦点,在美国和14个其他国家担任部长。 上帝在耶稣革命期间(1970年)从嬉皮的生活方式和热情中怜悯地拯救了我,尽管通过远东宗教实践(瑜伽和冥想)错误地追求真理.

在遇到耶稣和被送走后不久,我与上帝的另一个兄弟一起,开始搭便车到全国各地,在街角和大学校园传福音. 多年来,这在教堂、礼堂、会议和帐篷十字军中发展成部。

超自然的供给和神的干预 总是让我在五年半的历险历程中 然而,以下的故事是一个经典的故事. 大约25年来,我在全国各地搭载着大型福音帐篷。

在这个“奇迹”发生时,我正用一辆老旧、破旧的公交车将60×90的帐篷从一个城市运送到另一个城市,这辆公交车不断给我们的业余技工技能带来新的挑战(轻轻地推开)。 有一天,在前往佛罗里达州坦帕的路上——不幸地——我们撞上了路边的一个大坑洞,在后左侧竖起一个大型卡车轮胎,后侧有严重的凹痕。

从此,内管不会保留空气,使得每30英里左右必须停一次才能再次填充. . . 再加上问题, 另一台后轮胎是秃头, 因此,一个公寓会 使我们完全停顿。

有时,我想起那些时候(那时我们对王国的热情超越了我们可能拥有的任何智慧),我惊讶地看到,无论怎样,上帝总是照顾我们(就像他那慈爱的天父)。

数千磅的设备被装进那辆呻吟、颤抖、生锈、破烂的巴士——重型帆布帐篷路段、金属杆、木桩、平台和300张椅子——而且只有几天时间允许在城市之间过境和布置。 不,我们真的无法承受任何挫折。

在每次旅行中都发表了许多“信仰祷告”(或它们是否“假定的宣告”——不确定——可能是两者的混合)。 一辆旧公共汽车上挂着一个旧的分叉轮圈轮胎 一旦我们到了坦帕, 试图节俭, 我参观了垃圾场 希望找到一个旧的替代轮圈。

就像他们密谋劝阻我一样, 每个垃圾场老板/经理都用类似的评估来击落我的希望, “伙计, 他们很危险。 当你试图安装一个轮胎, 他们可以撕开和伤害一个人 真正的坏,切断一只手,甚至杀死一个人。

我们把它们都融化成废金属。” 他们甚至被称为“寡妇制造者”。 我去过的地方都一样 没人能帮上忙 然后三个星期过去了,我们不得不收拾公交车 并前往下一个地点——北卡罗莱纳州的贝瑟默市。

这是一个关于发展长期痛苦和耐心的大学级、圣经般的教程:每隔30英里左右就停下来吹吹那个不可预测的轮胎,恳求上帝以某种超自然的方式协助我们的旅程,确保没有轮胎爆炸。 不知何故,我们大约在600英里的距离里,停了25次。 奇迹发生了!

上帝做到了,我仍然感觉 西车,只是写它。 当我们变成广场时, 就在入口的中间, 两个全新的, 整洁的卡车轮胎(无人认领), 说到崇拜上帝——我们发起了一次赞美会议,

什么机会? 我们都知道那是真主。耶和华已满足了。 他令人惊奇地承诺“超越一切, 然后说

articles.title: Rejoice in the Lamb: Benjamin Britten, Christopher Smart, and the Poetry of Faith
articles.summary: When music meets poetry, the result can be more than art, it can become an expression of spiritual wonder. The last time I heard Professor Bruce Redford speak about the eccentric British clergyman and poet Christopher Smart (1722–1771), I was so inspired that I included a substantial portion of Smart’s extraordinary poem, Jubilate Agno, in […]  The post  Rejoice in the Lamb: Benjamin Britten, Christopher Smart, and the Poetry of Faith  first appeared on  God Reports .
articles.summary_zh:
当音乐与诗歌相遇时,结果可以超越艺术,成为精神奇迹的体现.

上次我听到布鲁斯·雷德福德教授 谈到古怪的英国神职人员和诗人克里斯托弗·斯马特(1722–1771)时,我受到很大启发,在[.]中包含了一大部分斯马特非凡的诗歌,大庆阿格诺. 以及《信仰之诗》,
articles.title_zh: 喜悦羔羊：本杰明·布里顿、克里斯托弗·斯马特和信仰的诗歌
articles.content: When music meets poetry, the result can be more than art, it can become an expression of spiritual wonder. Christopher Smart The last time I heard Professor Bruce Redford speak about the eccentric British clergyman and poet Christopher Smart (1722–1771), I was so inspired that I included a substantial portion of Smart’s extraordinary poem, Jubilate Agno , in my book Beauty (And the Banana) . I described Smart as a theopoet , someone whose deep religious convictions found expression through a distinctive and imaginative poetic vision. Smart was no ordinary poet. His writings moved freely between the sacred and the seemingly mundane, finding divine significance in everything from biblical figures to animals and the natural world. His poetry was exuberant, unconventional, and, at times, wonderfully strange. For Smart, creation itself was a chorus of praise, and every living thing had a part to play. Recently, I had another opportunity to hear Redford explore Smart’s remarkable literary legacy, this time through the music of British composer Benjamin Britten (1913–1976). As part of an All Saints’ Day concert at the Cathedral of St. John in Albuquerque, New Mexico, celebrating Britten’s music, Redford delivered a pre-concert lecture focusing on the composer’s Rejoice in the Lamb , a choral masterpiece that brings Smart’s unusual poetry to life. The evening offered a fascinating intersection of literature, music, theology, and history, demonstrating how two artists separated by nearly two centuries could share a common vision of wonder. The Musical Imagination of Benjamin Britten Benjamin Britten. Photo: Public Domain. Redford, a former professor at Boston University who was living in England when Britten died in 1976, identified three defining characteristics of the composer’s work. First, Britten’s music is distinguished by “passion and variety.” His compositions resist easy categorization, moving between emotional intensity, dramatic storytelling, and moments of remarkable spiritual intimacy. Redford described Britten’s approach as creating a kind of musical parable, pointing to Curlew River , one of Britten’s church parables, as a particularly compelling example. Second, Britten demonstrated an extraordinary ability to balance “economy and scope.” Redford compared this quality to the novels of Jane Austen, whose carefully constructed narratives reveal entire worlds through seemingly modest details. Similarly, Britten could communicate profound emotional and spiritual truths through restrained musical means. Nothing was wasted; every note served a purpose. Third, and perhaps most important for the evening’s performance, Britten possessed an exceptional “sensitivity to words.” Redford described him as an “inspired” interpreter of literary texts, a composer who understood that music should not merely accompany poetry but illuminate its deeper meaning. It was this third characteristic that led Redford to Christopher Smart. When an Eccentric Poet Meets a Brilliant Composer In 1943, Britten composed Rejoice in the Lamb (Op. 30), a festival cantata scored for four soloists, SATB choir, and organ. The composition draws its text from Smart’s Jubilate Agno , a work of religious poetry that remained largely unknown for nearly two centuries. Christopher Smart Smart wrote much of the poem during his confinement in a private madhouse in eighteenth-century London. Its unconventional structure, biblical references, exuberant language, and seemingly spontaneous declarations of praise made it unlike almost anything else in English religious literature. The manuscript remained unpublished until W. F. Stead brought it to public attention in 1939. Soon afterward, the poet W. H. Auden introduced Britten to Smart’s newly published work while the composer was living in the United States. The connection proved fruitful. Britten recognized something remarkable in Smart’s poetry: an unrestrained celebration of creation that could be translated into music.
articles.content_zh:
当音乐与诗歌相遇时,结果可以超越艺术,成为精神奇迹的体现. 克里斯托弗·聪明 上次我听到布鲁斯·雷德福德教授谈到古怪的英国神职人员和诗人克里斯托弗·斯马特(1722–1771)时,我深受启发,在我的书《美人(和香蕉)》中包含了一大部分斯马特非凡的诗集《阿格诺大庆》。

我形容Smart是一位戏剧家, 聪明不是普通诗人 他的著作在圣人和看似庸俗的人之间自由移动,在从圣经人物到动物和自然世界的一切事物中都发现了神圣的意义.

他的诗歌充满了活力,与众不同,有时也非常奇怪. 对于Smart来说,创作本身是赞美的合唱,每一个活物都有角色可以扮演. 最近,我又有机会听到雷德福德探索Smart杰出的文学遗产,这次是通过英国作曲家本杰明·布里顿的音乐(1913–1976).

作为新墨西哥州阿尔布开克圣约翰大教堂庆祝布列顿音乐的全圣人节音乐会的一部分,雷德福德发表了一场音乐会前演讲,重点讲述了作曲家在羊羔中的欢乐,这是一部将斯马特不寻常的诗歌带给人生的奇特杰作.

晚上提供了文学、音乐、神学和历史的奇妙交汇点,展示了两个艺术家如何在将近两个世纪的时间里分开,可以分享一个共同的奇观。 本杰明·布林顿·本杰明·布林顿的音乐想象. 图片:公共域名.

雷德福德(Redford)是波士顿大学前教授,1976年布里顿逝世时居住在英国,他确定了作曲家作品的三个决定性特征. 首先,布列顿的音乐以“热情和多样性”来区分。 他的构思抵制轻松的分类,在情感的强度,戏剧性的故事性,以及非凡的精神亲密的时刻之间移动.

Redford将布列顿的做法描述为创造了一种音乐比喻,指向了布列顿教堂比喻之一的Curlew River,作为特别有说服力的例子.

第二,Britten表现出了平衡“经济和范围”的非凡能力。 雷德福德将这种品质与简·奥斯汀的小说相比较,他精心构建的叙事通过看似微小的细节揭示了整个世界. 同样,布列顿可以通过受约束的音乐手段传达深刻的情感和精神真理. 没有浪费任何东西;每张纸条都有作用。

第三,或许对晚间演出来说最重要的,布列顿拥有一种非凡的“言语敏感性 ” 。 Redford将他描述为文学文本的“受启发的”解释者,他是一个作曲家,他明白音乐不应仅仅伴随着诗歌,而应阐明其更深层次的意义。 正是这第三个特征导致雷德福找到克里斯托弗·斯马特.

1943年,当一位爱心诗人遇到一位杰出的作曲家时,布列顿在"羔羊"(Op. 30)中编曲了"欢乐"(Rejoice in the Lamb (Op. 30)),一个节日的Cantata为四位独奏家,SATB合唱团和管风琴打分. 内容来自Smart's Jubilate Agno, 一部宗教诗歌作品,

克里斯托弗·斯马特(Christopher Smart Smart)在18世纪伦敦一个私人疯人院禁闭期间写下了这首诗的大部分内容. 它的非常规结构,圣经的参考文献,兴旺的语言,以及看似自发的赞美宣言,使得它几乎不同于英国宗教文献中的其他任何内容. 手稿直到W. F.

施泰德在1939年引起了公众的注意. 不久之后,诗人W·H·奥登(W. H. Auden)在作曲家在美国居住期间,向布里顿介绍了斯马特新出版的作品. 这种联系证明是富有成果的。 Britten在Smart的诗歌中承认了一些令人瞩目的事物:一种可以被翻译成音乐的无限制的创作庆典.

articles.summary_zh: 文：查尔斯·加德纳（Charles Gardner）——在希特勒企图迫害我们的时期，这位德国人却来祝福我们！大屠杀幸存者维尔纳·西蒙森（Werner Simonson）在第二次世界大战爆发前夕逃离德国，后来成为英国国教的牧师。他有犹太血统，被……解除了法官职务。这篇题为《犹太难民成为牧师》的文章最初发表在《上帝报道》上。
articles.title_zh: 犹太难民成为副牧师
articles.content: Werner Simonson By Charles Gardner — At a time when Hitler aimed to harm us, here was a German who came to bless us! Holocaust survivor Werner Simonson escaped from Germany just before the outbreak of World War II, only to become a Church of England vicar. Of Jewish heritage, he was sacked as a judge by the Nazis and had to endure long years of separation from his non-Jewish wife and son before being reunited after the war. Like John Wesley who was rescued as a child from a rectory fire, Werner was also ‘a brand plucked from the burning’. He was about to be executed in a World War I battle with France when he and his colleagues were wrongly accused of shooting French prisoners. But just in time, one of the latter told the firing squad how Werner had treated him with kindness, even sharing his rations with him. The German soldier was thus spared but spent the next five years as a prisoner of the French, his POW status only ending in 1920 after being put to work restoring war damage in northern France. When finally released, it was a case of ‘from the frying pan into the fire’ as Germany was plunged into despair and division following their ignominious defeat. Despite this, however, Werner quickly rose to the status of high court judge before being dismissed from his post by the Nazis when they discovered his Jewish heritage. The fact that he had fought for Germany and had won the coveted Iron Cross for gallantry counted for nothing. And the increasing pressure of anticipating arrest led to a breakdown of his health. But while attending his niece’s confirmation at a Lutheran church, feeling at the end of his rope, it was as if the preacher was speaking directly into his desperate situation. He opened his heart to Christ and found new life and hope. “In the utter darkness which had engulfed my life I saw a new light,” he recalled.(1) He became associated with the Confessing Church opposing the Nazis’ antisemitic policies and was advised to escape which he managed to do with the help of the Bishop of Chichester Dr George Bell. Werner’s wife Leonie and son Juergen stayed behind but were able to join him after the war. Being German, he was initially interned with others on the Isle of Man where he led fellow Jews to faith in Christ. But tragic news followed, hearing of his father’s death, his mother being murdered in a concentration camp and his sister Ilse gassed in Auschwitz. Werner knew little English when he arrived on these shores but attracted much interest by being ordained at St Paul’s Cathedral when Britain was in the middle of a war with his fatherland. He was subsequently offered back the post of judge in the new West Germany along with a pension for the job from which he had been previously dismissed by the Nazis. But he turned down the generous offer. “I could not exchange service in the ministry of God for service in administering man-made law; accepting this offer would have meant abandoning God’s call to me, and this I could not do.” But this humble and self-effacing man was to make a significant impact in succeeding years as he proclaimed the gospel in three separate London parishes, ending up at St Luke’s, Hampstead, where (from 1956-1965) he helped yet more Jewish people to a knowledge of their Messiah. He continued passionately preaching Christ almost till his final breath in 1991, aged 101. 1 With grateful thanks to War and Grace by Don Stephens (Evangelical Press 2005), an imprint of 10Publishing. The post Jewish refugee became vicar first appeared on God Reports .
articles.content_zh:
维纳·西蒙森 查尔斯·加德纳 当希特勒想伤害我们的时候 有个德国人来祝福我们! 大屠杀幸存者维尔纳·西蒙森(Werner Simonson)在二战爆发前刚从德国逃出,只是成为英国牧师教堂.

由于犹太人的遗产,他被纳粹解雇为法官,不得不忍受与他非犹太妻子和儿子多年的分离,战争结束后才重新团聚. 就像小时候被救出来的约翰·卫斯理(John Wesley),

他在第一次世界大战与法国的战斗中即将被处决,当时他和他的同事被错误地指责射杀法国囚犯. 但就在时间上,后者之一告诉行刑队,沃纳如何以善意对待他,甚至与他分享他的口粮.

德国士兵因此幸免于难,但作为法国人的俘虏度过了接下来的五年,他的战俘身份直到1920年在法国北部被投入恢复战争破坏后才结束. 当德国在惨败之后陷入绝望和分裂。

尽管如此,维尔纳在发现他的犹太遗产后很快升格为高等法院法官,然后被纳粹解职. 他为德国而战 赢得了贪婪的铁十字勋章 他的英勇无足轻重 而预期被捕的压力越来越大,导致他的健康崩溃。

但当在路德会教堂出席侄女的确认仪式时,感觉他的绳索尽头,就像传教士直接谈到他的绝望处境一样. 他向基督敞开了心扉,找到了新的生命和希望.

" 在席卷我的生活的完全黑暗中,我看到了新的光芒, " 他回忆说。 (1) 他与反对纳粹反帝政策的忏悔教会有关联,并被劝告在奇切斯特主教乔治·贝尔博士的帮助下逃离。 维尔纳的妻子莱昂尼(Leonie)和儿子朱尔根(Juergen)留下,但战后得以加入他.

作为德国人,他最初在马恩岛和其他人一起被关押,在那里他带领犹太人同胞信仰基督. 但悲剧性的消息接踵而至,听到他父亲的死讯,他的母亲在集中营被谋杀,他的妹妹伊尔塞在奥斯威辛被毒气冲昏.

Werner在到达这些海岸时不懂英语, 随后他又被重新聘回新西德的法官职位,并同时获得先前被纳粹开除的职务养老金. 但他拒绝了慷慨的提议.

“我不能在上帝部交换服务,以服务于管理人造法律;

接受这个提议将意味着放弃上帝对我的召唤,我不能这样做。 但是,这位谦卑而自卑的人在接下来的岁月里,当他在三个独立的伦敦教区宣布福音时,将产生显著的影响,最后在汉普斯特德的圣卢克(St Luke),他在那里(从1956年到1965年)帮助了更多的犹太人民了解他们的弥赛亚。

他继续热情地宣扬基督,几乎到1991年他最后一口气为止,101. 1岁,感谢战争与恩典,唐·斯蒂芬斯著(福音出版社,2005年),10Publishing的印记. 犹太难民成为牧师,

articles.summary_zh: 文：马克·埃利斯（Mark Ellis）——马克·戴维森（Mark Davidson）10岁时，他的母亲送给他一本哈尔·林赛（Hal Lindsey）的著作《末世的伟大地球》（The Late Great Planet Earth）。这本书最终售出约3500万册，被《纽约时报》评为20世纪70年代最畅销的非小说类书籍。这本书对戴维森产生了深远影响，并塑造了他最初的……文章《圣经预言对伊朗战争有何看法？》最初发表在《上帝报道》上。
articles.title_zh: 圣经预言对伊朗战争有何说法？
articles.content: By Mark Ellis – As a 10-year-old boy, Mark Davidson’s mother gave him Hal Lindsey’s book, The Late Great Planet Earth , which eventually sold some 35 million copies, and was declared the bestselling nonfiction book of the 1970s by the New York Times. The book had a great impact on Davidson and shaped his earliest views about end times Bible prophecy. Shaken by the events of 9/11, Davidson, a retired aerospace engineer, dug more deeply into end-times prophecy, seeking answers about the direction of world events.  As he dove into Scripture related to prophecy, he developed a framework that diverges from traditional teaching in several ways, and resulted in his book: Daniel Revisited : Discovering the Four Mideast Signs Leading to the Antichrist. The most relevant of his teaching to current events is his view of Iran. Based on his study of Daniel 7, Daniel 8 and Revelation 6, Davidson identified four major events, which he calls “signposts,” that he believes will unfold in the Middle East before the Tribulation. The four signposts will all be within the Islamic realm. “This interpretation involves the four beasts of Daniel 7, the ram and goat of Daniel 8, and the four horsemen of Revelation 6,” Davidson told God Reports. “They’re all talking about the same four events, just from different aspects.” He says the first signpost was fulfilled when Iraq’s government changed between 2003 and 2005, and he now sees the Iran conflict and disruption involving the Strait of Hormuz as potential indications that the second is beginning to unfold. The second signpost involves Iran (Shia) attacking its Sunni neighbors. “At some point, Iran will destroy the rest of the Arab oil infrastructure of Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, the UAE, Qatar, and Iraq,” Davidson predicts, based on his interpretation. “They’ve told the U.S. and Israel, if you attack and destroy our energy infrastructure, we’re going to do the same to all the other neighboring countries.” The attacks could be imminent, based on statements by leaders on both sides. “Iran’s threatening to do this prior to November 3 rd as an October surprise, and Trump is threatening to attack after the midterm elections. “So it could actually be quite soon where it blows up. But that’s what I see happening: the U.S. and Israel would attack Iran. Iran would fend it off like they’ve done before, destroy the rest of the Arab infrastructure, taking oil to astronomical prices.” The economic chaos and disruption could potentially threaten the US’s status as the reserve currency for the world. “Iran is going to take away the peace of mind of the entire earth,” Davidson maintains. “People will wonder how they can put food on the table.” Davidson wrote his book to warn the church because he contends the second signpost is going to be terrible. “It’s going to be awful. It’s going to change all our lives and change how we live, both in the United States as well as in much of the world. Mark Davidson “The second signpost is going to hit us in the face. I was completely aghast and flabbergasted that a U.S. president would trigger the second signpost. I was very, very surprised. “This is a whole Pandora’s box, and once the second signpost happens, that leads to the third, which leads to the fourth, which leads to the Tribulation. So, what God has done is He’s used President Trump to trigger the signpost, to trigger the coming of the Antichrist, to trigger the end of the world, and trigger Christ’s return.” If Davidson was advising President Trump, he would tell him to withdraw US forces as soon as possible. Davidson believes the rebuilding of the Jewish Temple will occur during the third signpost. He diverges from traditional teaching with his view that the coming Antichrist will be a Syrian Arab Muslim. “The ten kingdoms are not Roman kingdoms; they are Muslim kingdoms, stretching from Morocco to Pakistan,” he maintains. articles.content_zh:
马克·埃利斯 作为10岁的男孩,马克·戴维森的母亲给了他Hal Lindsey的书"晚大星球地球"(The Late Great Planet Earth),这本书最终售出约3500万份,被纽约时报宣布为1970年代最畅销的非小说书籍. 该书对戴维森影响很大,塑造了他对"圣经预言"末期最早的看法.

受到911事件的震撼,退休的航空航天工程师戴维森更深入地挖掘了末日的预言,寻找世界事件方向的答案. 当他潜入与预言相关的圣经时,他发展了一个与传统教义在几个方面有所区别的框架,并由此产生了他的书:丹尼尔重温:发现四个中东部的标志导致反基督.

他对时事的教导中最相关的是他对伊朗的看法. 根据他对Daniel 7,Daniel 8 and Revelation 6的研究,Davidson确定了四大事件,他认为这四大事件是“标志性人物”,他认为,在Tribulation事件之前,在中东将展开。 这四个路标都将属于伊斯兰范畴.

“这一解释涉及丹尼尔七世的四只野兽、丹尼尔八世的公羊和山羊,以及启示录六世的四匹马。”

“他们都在谈论相同的四个事件, 他表示,第一个路标在伊拉克政府在2003年到2005年间更换时就已经实现,他现在认为,涉及霍尔木兹海峡的伊朗冲突与破坏可能表明第二个路标正在开始展开。 第二个路标是伊朗(Shia)攻击逊尼派邻国。

“在某种程度上,伊朗将摧毁沙特阿拉伯、科威特、阿联酋、卡塔尔和伊拉克的其余阿拉伯石油基础设施。” Davidson根据他的解释预测。 “他们已经告诉美国。

“因此,爆炸可能很快发生。 但这就是我所看到的:美国和以色列会攻击伊朗。 伊朗会像以前一样, 摧毁其他阿拉伯基础设施, 经济混乱和混乱有可能威胁到美国作为世界储备货币的地位。

Davidson认为,“伊朗将夺走整个地球的心灵安宁”。 “人们会怀疑他们如何将食物放在桌子上。” 大卫森写了他的书来警告教会,因为他认为第二个路标会很糟糕. “这将会是可怕的。 这将会改变我们的生活, 改变我们在美国的生活方式,

马克·戴维森 “第二个路标将击中我们的脸。 我感到非常恐怖,并且惊慌失措地说,美国总统会触发第二个路标。 我很惊讶 " 这是整个潘多拉的盒子,一旦发生第二个路标,就会导致第三个路标,从而导致第四个路标,从而导致三难.

因此,上帝所做的是,他利用川普总统来触发路标,引发反基督派的到来,引发世界末日,引发基督的回归. 如果戴维森建议特朗普总统,他会告诉他尽快撤出美军. 戴维森认为重建犹太圣殿将在第三个路标上进行.

他偏离了传统教义,认为即将到来的反基督者将是阿拉伯叙利亚穆斯林。 他认为,“这十个王国不是罗马王国;它们是穆斯林王国,从摩洛哥延伸到巴基斯坦。” 有些人在Davidson的网站上发表评论,

articles.title_zh: Patrick Nagatani：通过色彩、摄影和艺术进行的精神探索
articles.content: Arriving in Albuquerque, New Mexico, in 2009, I was fortunate to catch the final chapter of artist and photographer Patrick Nagatani’ s remarkable career before his death from cancer in 2017. As one of my favorite modern photographers, Nagatani fascinated me with his unique artistic vision, his imaginative compositions, and his ability to transform his photography into extraordinary works of art. Watching him at gallery openings was a pleasure. He was cordial, kind, and genuinely responsive to those who engaged him. There was something refreshing about an artist of his stature who remained approachable, thoughtful, and seemingly delighted to discuss his work. An Artist Shaped by History Photo credit: Grahm Howe, 1979. Patrick Ryoichi Nagatani was born on August 19, 1945, in Chicago, Illinois, only days after the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki. His Japanese American parents had experienced incarceration during World War II, and the legacy of displacement, cultural identity, and nuclear destruction would profoundly influence his artistic imagination. Raised Catholic, Nagatani eventually moved with his family to Los Angeles. He studied at UCLA, earning his Master of Fine Arts in 1980. His early professional experience included model-making for Hollywood productions, helping establish the theatrical techniques that later distinguished his photography. In 1987, he moved to Albuquerque to teach at the University of New Mexico , where he became an influential professor and internationally recognized artist. His celebrated Nuclear Enchantment series examined the disturbing relationship between New Mexico’s landscapes and the nuclear industry. Other projects investigated Japanese American incarceration, archaeology, cultural memory, and the uncertainty of photographic truth. ‘Generation to Generation’, Strategic Defense Initiative (SDI) Nuclear Powered Vehicles, West Mesa, Albuquerque, New Mexico, 1991 & 1993, Chromogenic print (Ilfocolor Deluxe), 17 X 22 and 27 3/4 X 34 1/4 My interest in Nagatani extends beyond the artistry of his photographs—the theatrical tableaux, vibrant colors, and beautifully constructed compositions—to what I perceive as an underlying spiritual search. Throughout his career, questions of identity, mortality, healing, and transcendence surfaced repeatedly. Though not every work was explicitly religious, I suggest that there’s a longing to discover meaning beyond the material world. One early example is his series Colorful Cathedrals (1980–1983), which invites consideration of the relationship between artistic creation and spiritual imagination. Colorful Cathedrals: Light and the Sacred Nagatani’s Colorful Cathedrals emerged during his early experimentation with color photography and constructed imagery. The series was exhibited in Los Angeles and elsewhere, including a 1983 exhibition at the Arco Center for Visual Arts. His artistic practice during this period involved manipulating photographic environments rather than merely documenting existing scenes. Using constructed arrangements, controlled lighting, and photographic experimentation, he explored how color could transform visual experience. Canterbury #1, Kent, England, 1981, 36 X 33 X 2 1/2, nine P-12 Cibachrome prints from original SX-70’s with mixed media (oils, enamels, watercolors, sprayed and selectively hand colored) For me, the title of the series suggests something spiritually evocative. Cathedrals have historically served as architectural expressions of Christian theology, with light and color—particularly through stained glass—symbolizing divine illumination. Having graduated at Canterbury Christchurch University, with an Evensong service at Canterbury Cathedral, I’m drawn to his “Canterbury #1” work. Patrick Nagatani juxtaposes the grandeur of a Gothic cathedral with human hands holding yellow cards, suggesting a tension between sacred architecture and humanity’s search for spiritual meaning. 2009年抵达新墨西哥州阿尔布开克, 我有幸在2017年因癌症去世前, 作为我最喜欢的现代摄影师之一,那加塔尼用他独特的艺术眼光,想象力的构思,以及把他的摄影改造为非凡的艺术作品的能力,让我着迷.

在画廊的开幕式上看着他真是荣幸 他对雇用他的人是真诚、善良和真诚的。 有一些令人振奋的东西 关于他的地位 艺术家保持接触, 深思熟虑, 似乎很高兴讨论他的作品。 An Artist shaped by History Photo credit: Grahm Howe, 1979 (英语).

帕特里克·里约伊奇·纳加塔尼于1945年8月19日出生于伊利诺伊州芝加哥,距广岛和长崎原子弹爆炸仅几天后. 他的日本裔美国父母在二战期间曾遭受过监禁,流离失所,文化认同和核毁灭的遗留影响将深刻影响他的艺术想象.

养成天主教徒,那加塔尼最终随家人移居洛杉矶. 他在加州大学洛杉矶分校学习,1980年挣得他的美术硕士. 他早期的专业经验包括为好莱坞的制作制作模特,帮助建立后来将他的摄影区分开的戏剧技术.

1987年,他搬到阿尔伯克基,在新墨西哥大学任教,在那里他成为了一位有影响力的教授和国际知名的艺术家. 他的著名的"核魅力"系列研究了新墨西哥州地貌与核工业之间的令人不安的关系.

其他项目调查了日本裔美国人的监禁,考古,文化记忆,以及照片真相的不确定性.

一个早期的例子就是他的系列"彩色大教堂"(1980年-1983年),这请人们考虑艺术创作与精神想象之间的关系. 彩色大教堂:光明与圣洁的那加塔尼的彩色大教堂在他早期的彩色摄影和构筑图像实验中出现.

该系列在洛杉矶和其他地方展出,包括1983年在Arco视觉艺术中心展出. 他在此期间的艺术实践涉及操纵摄影环境,而不仅仅是记录现有的场景. 他利用构建的安排,受控的照明,以及摄影实验,探索了色彩如何转化视觉体验.

articles.content:
제47회 신촌포럼이 ‘듣고, 읽고, 행하자’는 주제로 서울 마포구 신촌성결교회(담임 박노훈 목사)에서 개최됐다.

이번 포럼에서는 ‘함께 읽고, 함께 듣고, 다시 오래 머무는 신앙의 여정’을 부제로 공동체 성경읽기 운동을 벌이고 있는 G&M ASIA and Japan 김승환 이사장의 주제강연과 교수들의 패널토의가 마련됐다.

박노훈 목사는 “신촌포럼은 1997년 시작돼 30년을 맞이했다. 매년 두 차례 이상 포럼을 통해 교회와 사회, 신학과 목회 사이 다리를 놓고 새로운 대안을 제시하는 일에 집중해 왔다”며 “이번 포럼은 신앙의 생활화를 제안하고 학교와 교회의 실제 적용 모델을 모색하고자 한다. 참여하는 우리 모두에게 하늘의 귀한 복이 임할 줄 믿는다”고 인사했다.

읽는 것과 듣는 것이 다른가? PRS, 아시아 41개 도시 진행

오희천 박사 사회로 신촌포럼 이상직 위원장의 포럼 소개 후, 김승환 이사장은 ‘Listening the Scripture, Doing the Scripture(성경을 듣고, 행하는 삶)’라는 제목으로 주제강연을 전했다.

김승환 이사장은 “성경을 읽고 들을 때 어떠한 자세와 마음으로 들어야 할지 수많은 사람들이 이야기하고 있다. 유진 피터슨 목사는 내게 필요한 말씀을 선택하고 소비하는 성향을 지적하기도 했다. 이런 ‘성경 소비자들’을 향해, 느헤미야 선지자는 백성들이 말씀에 귀를 기울였다고 전한다”며 “공동체 성경읽기는 디모데전서 4장 13절 말씀 ‘the Public Reading of Scripture’에서 왔다”고 소개했다.

김 이사장은 “말씀이 우리를 깨우치게 하신다. 요한계시록 1장 3절 말씀에서 ‘읽는 자’는 단수형, ‘듣는 자’는 복수형으로 기록돼 있다. 훈련된 사람이 읽고, 청중들이 함께 듣는 것”이라며 “읽고 듣는 데서 끝내지 않고, 행함이 따라와야 한다. 저희 재단은 하나님께서 자라나게 하심을 믿고, 6년 전부터 교회와 신학교를 섬기기로 했다. 지금은 서울과 도쿄를 중심으로, 아시아 41개 도시에서 PRS가 진행되고 있다”고 말했다.

그는 “현재 PRS는 한국에서 서울신대가 가장 밀접하게 함께하고 있다. 고신대와 한동대, 명지학원 등 많은 단체들과 교회들이 함께하고 있다”며 “세계로도 확산되고 있다. 뉴욕을 중심으로 북미와 남미, 유럽과 중동, 아프리카 대학에서도 함께 성경을 읽고 있다. 그리고 하버드 로스쿨에서 몇 년째 모임이 이뤄지고 있다”고 소개했다.

김 이사장은 “읽는 것과 듣는 것이 뭐가 다르냐고 하신다. 그러나 성경을 연구하듯 읽기보다(Reading), 말씀의 현재성에 주목하고자 한다”며 “지나간 글이 아니라 살아있는 말씀을 관계적으로 듣는 행위로서(Listening) 풍성함으로 초대하는 것이다. 이를 위해서는 경청의 자세와 청종이 필요하다”고 덧붙였다.

하나님 말씀과 인간의 들음 들음의 능력, 말씀으로 회복

2부 패널토의에서 ‘믿음은 들음에서 나고’라는 제목으로 오희천 교수(호서대)는 “들음은 행함을 내포한다. 한국어에서 ‘들으라’는 말에는 행하라는 의미도 함축돼 있다. 성경을 왜 들어야 하는가? 들어야 믿음이 생기기 때문”이라며 “하나님 말씀은 살아있고 생명력이 있기 때문에(히 4:12), 그리스도의 말씀(비유)은 지금 여기 생생한 삶의 현장에서 해석돼야 한다”고 말했다.

오희천 교수는 “본래 하나님 말씀과 인간의 들음은 불가분적으로 종속적이었다. 그러나 인간은 보암직도 먹음직도 한 것에 유혹돼, 들음의 능력을 상실했다. 들음의 능력을 상실한 시대는 궁핍한 시대”라며 “설교자는 시인이자 사상가로서 이런 궁핍한 시대의 전도자여야 한다. 상실된 들음의 능력은 그리스도의 말씀(레마)을 통해, 그리스도의 말씀으로 말미암아 회복된다”고 설명했다.

오 교수는 “인간이 하나님을 직접 볼 수 없듯, 하나님 말씀도 직접 들을 수 없다. 기록된 말씀을 읽어야 하나님을 볼(알) 수 있고, 기록된 말씀을 들어야 하나님 말씀(음성)을 들을 수 있다”며 “색과 소리가 너무 강하면, 영적 상상력이 약해진다. ‘무엇을 먹을까 무엇을 마실까’에 대한 관심의 색과 소리가 너무 과하면 하나님 나라와 의를 보기 어렵다. AI의 색과 소리에 너무 집착하면, 소리를 듣지 못하고 자발적으로 문명과 인공지능의 노예가 되기 쉽다”고 우려했다.

예배학적 관점 공동체 성경읽기 신·구약, 공동체 성경 읽기 증언

‘공동체 성경읽기에 대한 예배학적 관점’이라는 주제로 조기연 교수(서울신대)는 “구약 느헤미야 8장 1-10절은 이스라엘 공동체가 ‘공동체 성경읽기’를 통해 모든 백성들이 하나님 말씀을 듣고 깨달으며 하나님을 예배했다고 증언한다”며 “신약 누가복음 4장 16절 이하는 예수께서 공생애 기간 정기적으로 회당에 가셔서 예배에 참여하셨음을 증언한다. 예수께서 ‘이 글이 오늘날 너희 귀에 응했다’고 해석하신 것은 랍비의 자격을 갖추셨음을 의미한다”고 풀이했다.

조기연 교수는 “사도 시대 예배는 크게 성경봉독과 설교, 성찬으로 이뤄져 있었다. 4세기 말까지는 ‘예배의 부름’ 직후 성경봉독으로 예배가 시작됐는데, 이는 동방·서방 교회의 공통적 방식이었다”며 “4세기 안디옥 예배 전통에서는 율법서와 예언서를 읽은 후 신약의 서신서와 사도행전을 읽고, 마지막으로 복음서를 읽었다. 7세기부터는 구약과 신약 한 곳씩 읽었고, 9세기 이후 비잔틴 예전에서는 주일에 신약만 두 곳을 읽었다”고 소개했다.

조 교수는 “초대교회의 성경읽기 방식은 주로 ‘연속 읽기(lectio continua)’였으나, 점차 특정 절기에 읽어야 할 특정 본문들을 결정해서 읽는 ‘선택 읽기(lectio selecta)’로 바뀌었고, 동방·서방 교회 모두 부활절에는 사도행전을 봉독했다”며 “성 주간(Holy Week)에는 예수 그리스도의 수난을 공동체 성경읽기 형식으로 재현하고 묵상했다. 이러한 방식은 예수의 수난을 오늘 예배 공동체가 참여하고 묵상한다는 의미”라고 설명했다.

성서적 토대와 학원 사례 PRS 후 식사, 환대의 표현

‘읽어주는 사람과 듣고 지키는 사람들은 복되도다: PRS/JSU의 성서적 토대와 학원 사례를 중심으로’라는 제목으로 이승문 교수(명지전문대 교목실장)는 “공동체 성경읽기(PRS)는 초대교회 공적 낭독 구조를 현대적으로 회복하려는 실천”이라며 “PRS에서 성경을 함께 들은 직후 즉각적 해석이나 감상 나눔을 유보하는 것은 생각을 금지하기 위해서가 아니라, 본문 자체가 공동체 안에서 충분히 들리도록 시간을 확보하기 위해서”라고 전했다.

이승문 교수는 “‘Just Show Up(JSU)’은 성경이 아닌 일반 도서를 함께 읽는 실천이라는 점에서 PRS와 구별된다. PRS가 말씀의 공적 청취에 초점을 둔다면, JSU는 독서 뒤 자기표현과 상호 경청을 훈련한다”며 “PRS와 식사 제공 후 JSU를 진행하는 것은 처음 온 사람에게도 자리를 내어주고 참여 자격을 묻지 않는 환대의 표현”이라고 밝혔다.

이 교수는 “명지중학교는 청소년 PRS/JSU 그룹 모델을 이루고, 명지전문대학은 대규모 채플(PRS)과 소규모 채플(JSU), 오픈 PRS/JSU, 학과 비전모임 등 기존 교육·신앙 활동에 PRS와 JSU를 정기적으로 진행하고 있다”며 “공동체 성경읽기의 성패는 얼마나 많이 읽고 들었는가보다, 그 말씀이 삶으로 발현되는 것이 얼마나 중요한가를 알게 한다. 한 사람이 읽어주고, 공동체가 함께 듣고, 말씀을 삶에서 지킨다는 원리를 각 기관 상황에 맞게 구현해야 할 것”이라고 제언했다.

기독교 상담의 관점에서 성경 속 ‘나의 이야기’ 듣기

‘들음과 멈춤과 나눔의 미학: 기독교 상담의 관점에서 바라본 공동체 성경읽기(PRS)와 독서모임(JSU)’을 제목으로 홍정택 목사(솔트기독상담센터 대표)는 “PRS와 JSU에서 가장 주목한 것은 공동체 안에서 함께 성경을 읽고 공동체 앞에서 느낀 바를 자유롭게 이야기할 수 있도록 분위기를 제공하는 나눔의 기능”이라고 전했다.

홍정택 목사는 “JSU 독서모임이 ‘읽기→ 멈춤→ 자기언어→ 경청’의 핵심 리듬을 지향하는 점은 기존 주입식 성경공부와 다른 장점을 제공할 수 있다”며 “권위자에게 받는 일방향 교육에서 확장해 성경 이야기에 머물러 있으므로, 성경 이야기 속에서 ‘나의 이야기’를
articles.content_zh:
第47届新村论坛在首尔麻浦区新村圣洁教会（主任牧师朴鲁勋）举行，主题为“聆听、阅读、践行”。本次论坛以“一起阅读、一起聆听、在信仰的旅程中再次长久停留”为副标题，安排了正在开展团体圣经阅读运动的G&M ASIA and Japan理事长金胜焕的主题演讲以及教授们的专题讨论。朴鲁勋牧师表示：“新村论坛始于1997年，如今已走过了30个年头。每年通过至少两次论坛，我们一直致力于在教会与社会、神学与牧会之间搭建桥梁，并提出新的替代方案。”他还表示：“本次论坛旨在倡导将信仰融入生活，并探索学校与教会的实际应用模式。我相信，天上宝贵的祝福将临到我们所有参与者。” 阅读和聆听有什么不同吗？

PRS在亚洲41个城市举办

在由吴熙千博士主持、新村论坛理事长李相直介绍论坛之后，金承焕理事长发表了题为“Listening the Scripture, Doing the Scripture（聆听圣经，践行圣经）”的主旨演讲。金胜焕理事长表示：“有很多人在谈论阅读和聆听圣经时应该以怎样的态度和心态来聆听。尤金·彼得森牧师也指出了人们倾向于选择和消费自己需要的话语。针对这些‘圣经消费者’，先知尼希米说，百姓们聆听了神的话语。”他还介绍说，“集体读经源于提摩太前书4章13节的‘the Public Reading of Scripture’（圣经的公开宣读）。”

金理事长表示：“神的话语使我们得到启迪。在启示录第1章第3节中，“念”是单数，“听”是复数。受过训练的人来朗读，听众们一起聆听。”他还表示：“不能止步于阅读和聆听，而是要付诸行动。我们基金会相信上帝会使我们成长，因此从6年前开始就决定要服侍教会和神学院。目前，PRS正在以首尔和东京为中心，在亚洲的41个城市开展。” 他说：“目前在韩国，首尔神学大学与PRS的合作最为紧密。高神大学、汉东大学、明知学园等许多团体和教会都在参与其中。”他还表示：“PRS也在向全世界传播。以纽约为中心，北美、南美、欧洲、中东和非洲的大学也在共同阅读圣经。

此外，在哈佛法学院，这样的聚会已经持续了好几年。” 金理事长表示：“有人会问，阅读和聆听有什么区别。然而，我们希望关注的是话语的当下性，而不是像研读圣经那样去阅读（Reading）。”他还补充道：“这是一种以关系性的方式聆听（Listening）活生生的话语，而不是过去的文章，从而被邀请进入丰盛的境界。为此，我们需要有倾听的态度和顺服的行动。” 神的话语与人的聆听 聆听的能力，藉着话语得着恢复

在第二部分的专题讨论中，以“信心是因听道而生”为题，湖西大学的吴熙千教授表示：“听道包含了行道。在韩语中，“听”这个词也隐含着“行”的意思。为什么我们要聆听圣经？

因为只有听了才能产生信心。”他还说：“由于神的话语是活泼有力的（来4:12），基督的话语（比喻）必须在当下、在鲜活的生活场景中得到诠释。” 吴熙千教授表示：“本来，神的话语和人的聆听是不可分割地相互依存的。然而，人类被好看又好吃的东西所诱惑，失去了聆听的能力。丧失聆听能力的时代是一个贫乏的时代。”他还表示：“传道人作为诗人兼思想家，应当成为这样一个贫乏时代的传道者。失去的聆听能力将通过基督的话语（rhema），藉着基督的话语得到恢复。” 吴教授表示：“正如人无法直接看见神一样，人也无法直接听见神的话。

只有阅读记录下来的话语，才能看见（认识）神；只有聆听记录下来的话语，才能听到神的话语（声音）。”他还表示：“如果色彩和声音过于强烈，灵性的想象力就会变弱。如果对“吃什么、喝什么”的关注所产生的色彩和声音过于强烈，就很难看到神的国和神的义。如果过于沉迷于人工智能的色彩和声音，就容易听不到声音，从而自愿成为文明和人工智能的奴隶。”

从礼拜学的角度看共同体读经 新约与旧约、共同体读经的见证

以“从礼拜学角度看待团体读经”为主题，赵基妍教授（首尔神学大学）表示：“旧约《尼希米记》第8章1-10节见证了以色列团体通过‘团体读经’让所有百姓聆听并领悟神的话语，并敬拜神。”他还表示：“新约《路加福音》第4章16节以下见证了耶稣在传道期间定期前往会堂并参与礼拜。耶稣解释说‘这段经文今天在你们耳中应验了’，这意味着他具备了拉比的资格。” 赵基妍教授表示：“使徒时代的礼拜主要由圣经朗读、讲道和圣餐组成。

直到4世纪末，“礼拜的呼召”之后，礼拜都以圣经朗读开始，这是东方和西方教会的共同做法。”他还介绍说：“在4世纪安提阿的礼拜传统中，先读律法书和先知书，然后读新约的书信和使徒行传，最后读福音书。从7世纪开始，人们分别读一段旧约和一段新约；9世纪以后，拜占庭礼仪在主日只读两段新约。”

赵教授表示：“早期教会的圣经阅读方式主要是‘连续阅读（lectio continua）’，但后来逐渐转变为‘选择阅读（lectio selecta）’，即确定在特定节期应阅读的特定经文并进行阅读。东方和西方教会都在复活节诵读《使徒行传》。这种方式意味着今天的礼拜群体参与并默想耶稣的受难。”

圣经基础和学校案例 PRS PRS 用餐后、热情好客的表达

李承文教授（明知学院牧师主任）在题为“阅读者、倾听者和坚持者有福：聚焦 PRS/JSU 的圣经基础和学院案例”的标题下说，“社区圣经阅读（PRS）是一种寻求以现代方式恢复早期教会公共阅读结构的实践。”他补充说，“在 PRS 中一起听完圣经后，不立即解释或分享欣赏的原因并不是为了禁止思考，而是因为文本本身是在社区中使用的。“这是为了确保有足够的时间让人们听到。李升文教授表示：“‘Just Show Up (JSU)’与PRS不同，它是阅读一般书籍而不是圣经的做法。

“如果说 PRS 专注于公众聆听神的话语，那么 JSU 则训练阅读后的自我表达和相互聆听，”他说。 “在 PRS 和用餐后举办 JSU 是一种热情好客的表现，为首次来访者提供空间，并且不询问参与资格。”李教授表示：“明知中学形成了青年PRS/JSU团体模式，明知学院设有大礼拜堂（PRS）和小礼拜堂（JSU），开放PRS/JSU，并举办部门愿景会议。” “除了现有的教育和宗教活动之外，PRS 和 JSU 也是定期开展的，”他说。 “社区读经的成功或失败，比读或听多少圣经更重要，而更重要的是在一个人的生活中表达出来的话语有多重要。”

他建议，要根据各机构的情况，落实一个人读、社区共同听、生活中守信用的原则。从基督徒辅导的角度聆听圣经中的“我的故事”

洪正泽牧师（Salt基督教咨询中心代表）在题为“倾听、暂停、分享的美学：从基督徒咨询的角度看社区读经（PRS）和阅读俱乐部（JSU）”的主题中说：“在PRS和JSU，我最关注的是分享功能，它提供了一种氛围，让人们可以在社区中一起阅读圣经，并在社区面前自由地谈论自己的感受。”

articles.title_zh: 刚果民主共和国曼巴萨地区在埃博拉疫情期间至少有26人死亡
articles.content: Twenty-six people have reportedly been killed and several others abducted in a new attack carried out by the Islamist rebels of Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) on Nov. 10, during the night, in Mambasa territory, Ituri province, northeastern DR Congo, a country where nearly 93% of the population is Christian. According to a local association coordinator, Malikidogo, more than six villages were affected, including Kangwayi, Misele, Mingazi, and Mambaka. “The situation is very serious; we identified 26 people killed, several others abducted, and many families are still searching for their missing loved ones,” Malikidogo said. “Aside from the death of many people, five houses were burnt alongside some motorcycles. We are calling on the authorities to take urgent action to protect the population.” Left With Nothing Survivors who succeeded in escaping reported that many families had to run for their lives, leaving their homes and belongings behind. “We were very afraid when we realized that the enemies were already in the village when we heard people crying and others running in every direction,” one survivor said. “We just fled without having time to collect our belongings, just to save our lives. We do not know what will happen next, and we are afraid that they might come and reach Mambasa city where we are today.” The attack comes at a difficult time for local communities, which are already facing the threat of Ebola . Residents are now dealing with both the fear of the disease and the danger of further attacks. There are concerns that the violence could also make it harder to control the Ebola outbreak. People fleeing their villages may spread the disease to other communities, while insecurity could prevent health workers from reaching those who need medical help. A local leader also expressed concern about the situation and called for stronger protection of civilians. “We have suffered for many years because of the atrocities committed by ADF Islamist terrorists,” he said. “We are already struggling with Ebola, and now we are facing these attacks again. We cannot continue living like this. We are calling on the government and security forces to protect our communities before more innocent lives are lost.” To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . For interviews, please email us . To support ICC’s work around the world, please give to our Where Most Needed Fund . articles.content_zh:
据报告,11月10日,民主同盟军伊斯兰叛乱分子在刚果东北部伊图里省曼巴萨县发动了新的袭击,造成26人死亡,另有数人被绑架,该国近93%的人口是基督教徒。

据当地协会协调员Malikidogo说,有6个以上的村庄受到影响,其中包括Kangwayi、Misele、Mingazi和Mambaka。 “局势非常严重;我们确认有26人被杀害,另有数人被绑架,许多家庭仍在寻找失踪的亲人。”

“除了许多人的死亡外,还有五所房屋与一些摩托车一起被烧毁。 我们呼吁当局采取紧急行动保护人民。” 成功逃脱的幸存者一无所有地离开,报告说,许多家庭不得不逃命,留下家园和财物。

一位幸存者说,“当我们意识到敌人已经在村里时,我们非常害怕,当我们听到人们在哭,而其他人则朝每个方向奔跑时”。 “我们刚刚逃离,没有时间收集我们的财产,只是为了拯救我们的生命。

我们不知道接下来会发生什么,我们担心他们会来到我们今天所在的曼巴萨市。” 袭击发生在当地社区面临埃博拉威胁的困难时刻。 居民们现在正在处理对疾病的恐惧和进一步攻击的危险。

人们担心暴力也可能使控制埃博拉疫情变得更加困难。 逃离村庄的人可能把这种疾病传播到其他社区,而不安全则可能妨碍保健工作者帮助需要医疗帮助的人。 一名当地领导人还对局势表示关切,呼吁加强对平民的保护。

他说,“由于民主同盟军伊斯兰恐怖分子的暴行,我们受苦多年。” “我们已经在与埃博拉作斗争,现在我们再次面临这些袭击。 我们不能继续这样生活。 我们要求政府和安全部队在更多的无辜者丧生之前保护我们的社区。” 阅读更多新闻,

articles.title_zh: 食堂大屠杀4天后遇害
articles.content: Just days after the deadly massacre in Cantine, where at least 33 civilians were reportedly killed, suspected Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) fighters have struck again in Beni Territory, claiming four more lives and burning several houses in Mabalako, in the Democratic Republic of Congo. At about 12:20 a.m. on Thursday, Nov. 12, Mabalako once again faced ADF violence , with a fresh overnight attack in the Kamahume neighborhood. According to local civil society representatives, the death toll rose from an initial three to four, while more than seven houses were also set ablaze during the deadly incursion. The attack has renewed fears among civilians already traumatized by the violence that struck Cantine-Aloya less than a week earlier. The proximity of these two attacks in time and location has heightened concerns about the continuing threat posed by the ADF to civilian populations across Beni. “We are living in constant fear,” said Mulwahali, a survivor. “We have not yet recovered from the pain of what happened in Cantine, where innocent people were brutally killed and homes reduced to ashes. Now the violence has reached Mabalako, and once again we are mourning our loved ones and watching our homes burn. We do not know who will be next or where these attackers will strike again. We are even tired of burying our people without heads. All we want is to live in peace and sleep in our homes without fearing that we may never see another morning.” A Need for Security Local civil society representatives have appealed to security services to take full responsibility for protecting civilians, strengthen security operations, and prevent further attacks. Residents of Runzayi, Malondo, Ngazi, and Kibunamaru have also been urged to remain vigilant, maintain calm, and cooperate with security forces by reporting suspicious movements. “We cannot continue living at the mercy of armed attackers,” a local Catholic bishop said. “Although the intervention of the FARDC helped limit the destruction in Mabalako, the fact that the attackers could strike and disappear without their direction being known leaves us deeply frightened. We want security, not another massacre.” To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . For interviews, please email us . To support ICC’s work around the world, please give to our Where Most Needed Fund . The post 4 Killed Days After Cantine Massacre first appeared on International Christian Concern .
articles.content_zh:
据报道,在坎廷发生了至少33名平民被杀的致命屠杀事件,几天后,疑似民主同盟军(民主同盟军)战斗人员再次袭击了贝尼县,在刚果民主共和国的马巴拉科又造成4人死亡,几所房屋被烧毁。 11月,星期四上午12点20分左右.

马巴拉科再次面临民主同盟军的暴力, 据当地民间社会代表说,死亡人数从最初的3人增加到4人,而在致命的入侵中,还有七座房屋被点燃。

袭击使已经因不到一周前袭击Cantine-Aloya的暴力而受到创伤的平民再次感到恐惧。 这两起袭击在时间和地点上接近,使人们更加担心民主同盟军对贝尼各地平民继续构成威胁。 幸存者穆尔瓦哈利说:“我们生活在持续的恐惧之中”。

“我们尚未从坎廷发生的痛苦中恢复过来,在那里,无辜者惨遭杀害,家园沦为灰烬。 现在,暴力已蔓延到马巴拉科,我们再次哀悼我们的亲人,并观看我们的家园被烧毁。 我们不知道下一个是谁,也不知道这些袭击者将在哪里再次袭击。 我们甚至厌倦了无头埋葬我们的人民。

我们只想在家中过上和平的生活和睡觉,而不必担心再有早晨。” 地方民间社会代表呼吁安全部门全面负责保护平民,加强安全行动,防止进一步的袭击。

还敦促Runzayi、Malondo、Ngazi和Kibunamaru的居民保持警惕,保持平静,并与安全部队合作,报告可疑行动。 一位当地天主教主教说,“我们不能继续受武装袭击者的摆布”。

“虽然刚果(金)武装部队的干预有助于限制对马巴拉科的破坏,但袭击者可能袭击并消失而不了解他们的方向这一事实使我们深感恐惧。 我们要的是安全,而不是另一次屠杀。” 阅读更多新闻, 请给我们发电子邮件

articles.summary: On Nov. 6, an 18-year-old Christian girl named Ajak Mabior was beaten to death in Jonglei, South Sudan, after refusing to enter a forced marriage arranged by her family. She was expected to marry an older Muslim man — a marriage she opposed because of her Christian faith and her unwillingness to be forced into it. After…   The post  The Girl They Killed for Refusing a Forced Marriage  first appeared on  International Christian Concern .
articles.summary_zh: 11月6日，一名名叫阿贾克·马比奥尔（Ajak Mabior）的18岁基督徒女孩在南苏丹琼莱州因拒绝接受家人包办的强迫婚姻而被殴打致死。她本应嫁给一位年长的穆斯林男子——由于她的基督教信仰以及不愿意被强迫结婚，她反对这桩婚事。此后……   这篇题为《因拒绝强迫婚姻而被杀害的女孩》的文章  最初发表在  国际基督徒关注组织  网站上。
articles.title_zh: 因拒绝强迫婚姻而被杀害的女孩
articles.content: On Nov. 6, an 18-year-old Christian girl named Ajak Mabior was beaten to death in Jonglei, South Sudan, after refusing to enter a forced marriage arranged by her family. She was expected to marry an older Muslim man — a marriage she opposed because of her Christian faith and her unwillingness to be forced into it. After attempting to escape, she was killed by her own brother and cousin. Days later, police in Bor arrested the two men but released them without charges after family members demanded their freedom, arguing that “there was no case” because they were relatives. A Common Problem The killing has raised serious concerns among Christian leaders about the pressure Christian girls face when their faith and personal convictions conflict with family expectations. “When a young girl is killed for refusing a forced marriage, and the killers walk free because they are family, the message is clear: Tradition is stronger than the law, and stronger than the value of a life,” a local pastor said. “Many of our Christian daughters live under this same shadow.” For Christian girls in South Sudan , forced marriages can become a matter of religious persecution when they are pressured to marry outside their faith and abandon their Christian convictions. Those who refuse may face rejection, threats, intimidation, and violence from their own families. Mabior’s death highlights the vulnerability of young Christian women who seek to remain faithful to Christ while facing pressure to submit to marriages that violate their faith and conscience. “The church teaches that every life is precious because it is created in the image of God,” the pastor added. “Yet when a Christian girl refuses a marriage that would bind her against her will, she can be treated as a traitor to the community. We have buried too many who paid that price.” Seeking Justice The authorities’ response has added to the church’s concerns. Police reportedly released the suspects without the consent of the Jonglei State Caretaker Commissioner. The justification that the suspects were relatives raises serious questions about the protection available to Christian girls facing forced marriages and violence. When perpetrators are released without facing justice, vulnerable Christian women are left with little confidence that the authorities will protect their right to practice their faith and make decisions according to their conscience. “We preach freedom in Christ, but our young people still live in fear of the consequences of that freedom,” the pastor said. “If the police and local authorities remain quiet, the church becomes the only place left where these girls and boys can find a voice. We need courage to speak, and we need the wider Body of Christ to stand with us.” Mabior’s case raises concerns about forced interfaith marriages, religious pressure, and violence against young Christian women in South Sudan. “We call on the wider Body of Christ to pray for Ajak’s justice, and for the protection of Christian girls facing forced marriages because of their faith,” an International Christian Concern (ICC) staffer said. “Pray that the church will have the courage to speak against religious coercion and violence, and that the authorities will uphold the law and protect vulnerable believers.” To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . For interviews, please email us . To support ICC’s work around the world, please give to our Where Most Needed Fund . The post The Girl They Killed for Refusing a Forced Marriage first appeared on International Christian Concern .
articles.content_zh:
11月6日,一名名叫Ajak Mabior的18岁基督教女孩在南苏丹琼格莱州因拒绝参加家庭安排的强迫婚姻而被殴打致死。 她被期望嫁给一个年长的穆斯林男子——她反对这种婚姻,因为她的基督教信仰以及她不愿意被迫加入. 在试图逃跑后,她被自己的哥哥和表妹杀死.

几天后,Bor的警察逮捕了这两名男子,但在家属要求他们自由后,在没有指控的情况下将他们释放,他们辩称“没有案件”,因为他们是亲属。 常见问题 杀害事件引起了基督教领袖的严重关切,基督教女孩在信仰和个人信念与家庭期望相冲突时面临压力。

“当一名年轻女孩因拒绝强迫婚姻而被杀害,而杀人者因是家人而自由行动时,信息是明确的:传统比法律更强大,比生命的价值更强大。” 一位当地牧师说。

“我们许多基督教女儿生活在这种阴影下。” 对于南苏丹的基督教女孩来说,当她们被迫在信仰之外结婚并放弃基督教信仰时,强迫婚姻就可能成为宗教迫害的问题。 拒绝者可能面临自己家庭的排斥、威胁、恐吓和暴力。

Mabior的死亡凸显了基督教青年妇女的脆弱性,她们试图保持对基督的忠诚,同时面临压力,迫使她们向违反其信仰和良心的婚姻屈服。 牧师补充说,“教会教导每一条生命都是宝贵的,因为它是以上帝的形象创造的。”

“当一个基督教女孩拒绝违背她意愿而束缚她的婚姻时,她可以被当作一个叛徒对待。 我们埋葬了太多付出这一代价的人。” 寻求正义 当局的反应增加了教会的关注。 据报告,警方未经琼格莱州看守专员同意释放了嫌疑人。

关于嫌疑人是亲属的理由,令人对面临强迫婚姻和暴力的基督教女孩获得的保护提出严重问题。 当肇事者在没有受到法律制裁的情况下被释放时,脆弱的基督教妇女对当局将保护其信仰和根据其良心作出决定的权利缺乏信心。

牧师说,“我们在基督中宣扬自由,但我们的年轻人仍然生活在对这种自由的后果的恐惧之中。” “如果警察和地方当局保持安静,教堂就成了这些女孩和男孩能够发表意见的唯一地方。

我们需要勇气说话,我们需要更广泛的基督与我们站在一起。” Mabior案引起了人们对南苏丹境内强迫不同信仰间婚姻、宗教压力以及针对基督教青年妇女的暴力的关注。

“我们呼吁广大的基督机构为阿贾克的正义祈祷,并保护因信仰而面临强迫婚姻的基督教女孩。” 一位国际基督教关注组织的工作人员说。

“祈祷教会有勇气反对宗教胁迫和暴力,并祈祷当局将维护法律,保护脆弱的信徒。” 阅读更多新闻, 请给我们发电子邮件 支持电算中心在世界各地的工作,

articles.title: Scrolling the Soul Shallow
articles.summary: Entertainment swamps nearly all of life in triviality. So, how can we resist the tide and embrace a wholehearted, soul-satisfying pursuit of God? Listen Now
articles.summary_zh: 娱乐将生活的几乎所有方面都淹没在琐碎之中。那么，我们该如何抵挡这股潮流，全心全意地追求神，让灵魂得到满足呢？马上收听
articles.title_zh: 滚动灵魂浅滩
articles.content: Audio Transcript We lived through a decade of smartphone abuse and overuse (roughly 2015 to 2024). We talked at length about it on this podcast. I wrote books about it. Most of us have come to terms with when and where we’ve been online too much. We lament the wasted time, knowing we should have been doing more important things. The clock sped up as we lost ourselves in the everlasting scroll of eye-grabbing images and video. But what if time was not the greatest cost? What if something more serious happened to us, a lingering damage still present inside of us now? Today on Ask Pastor John: scrolling the soul shallow. It’s a question from Noah, a young man in Akron, Ohio. “Pastor John, I have made Titus 2:6–8 my aim as a young man. I know Paul is speaking to a young pastor. I am not a pastor, but I want to be self-controlled. I want to show myself ‘to be a model of good works,’ and I want to display ‘integrity, dignity, and sound speech.’ The main struggle I face is the shallowness of the culture in which we live. On my phone, computer, and TV, I see endless examples of flippancy. That’s really all I see some days. The whole world seems bent on numbing our souls to eternal realities. How can a young man resist all this and stay spiritually alert and cultivate these virtues?” One of the reasons I love this question is because I have said many times that the worst problem with television (or now let’s just say Instagram or any online media in general) is probably not the pervasive sexualization of all of life — that’s big enough — but rather the pervasive trivialization of all of life. You can scarcely watch TV ads or be online for more than ten seconds without being dump-trucked with banality and silliness. Grown men and women, even famous grown men and women, act like eleven-year-olds whose high point at summer camp was to bob for apples in a toilet filled with Mello Yello — the apex of satisfaction. That’s the quality that we’re being dumped on every day. This is the world we live in: silliness, humor, fun, joking, casual, flippant, cleverness, whimsical. And all that has made its way tragically into parenting, worship services, preaching, and hosting an event, even a serious one. Many modern people have never tasted serious joy, glad gravity, happy earnestness, or joyful weightiness. They have no category for such a thing. There’s fun and there’s boredom. That’s it. Life is that shallow, that insignificant. So, Noah asks, “How can I resist all this? How can I march to the beat of a different drummer?” 1. Distinguish between joy and fun. First, make sure that you are clear that joy and fun are not identical. Today, the word fun has virtually taken over the experience of serious joy. “Think about the shortness of life and the inevitability of death and the great realities of God.” Fun is what you have when playing with your kids on the living-room floor, flag football with the guys on Saturday, or a day at Disney World. That’s fun — nothing wrong with it. But now, church planting is fun, worship services are fun, Bible studies are fun. It’s as if you learn the language of trees while walking among twenty-foot Georgia pines, and then you visit three-hundred-foot, two-thousand-year-old redwoods in California and you have no language. They’re just fun trees. They’re not magnificent. They’re not breathtaking. They’re not humbling. They’re just fun trees. So, Noah, grow your vocabulary of joy and significance and wonder, because more often than we would like to admit, the heart shrinks to the language we have to express it rather than the other way around. If you call enough magnificent things “fun,” before long, that’s all they’ll be. Your heart will have shrunk to your vocabulary. 2. Know you’re not crazy. Second, listen to the warnings of Scripture to know you’re not crazy. The Bible is very aware of people who are incapable of being happily serious, and all their language is just clever or joking or trifling. - “Like a madman w
articles.content_zh:
音频记录 我们经历了十年的智能手机虐待和过度使用(大约2015年到2024年). 我们在播客上详细谈论了这个问题。 我写过书 我们大部分人都同意我们上网的时间和地点。 我们对浪费时间感到遗憾,因为我们知道我们应该做更重要的事。

时钟加速了,因为我们迷失了自己 在永恒的卷轴 挖眼影像和视频。 但如果时间不是最大的代价呢? 如果更严重的事情发生在我们身上, 那现在我们体内仍然存在的伤害呢? 今天在"问约翰牧师"上:滚动灵魂浅浅. 俄亥俄州Akron的年轻人Noah问:

“约翰神父,我把提图斯2:6-8作为我作为年轻人的目标。 我知道保罗在和一个年轻的牧师说话 我不是牧师,但我想自我控制。 我想展示自己“成为优秀作品的典范”, 我面临的主要斗争是我们所生活的文化的浅浅.

在我的手机、电脑和电视上, 我看到无尽的翻转例子。 这些日子我只看到这些。 整个世界似乎都想把我们的灵魂麻木于永恒的现实。

一个年轻人怎么能抗拒这一切,保持精神警惕,培养这些美德呢?” 我喜欢这个问题的原因之一 是因为我已经说过很多次了 电视最糟糕的问题(或者现在我们只说Instagram或任何一般的网络媒体) 可能不是 普遍的性化 生活的所有 - 这已经够大了 - 而是 普遍的轻视所有o

f 寿. 你几乎不能看电视广告 或在线超过十秒 而不被垃圾车 与平庸和愚蠢。 长大的男女,甚至著名的成年男女,都表现得像11岁的孩子,他们在夏令营的高潮是在充满了梅洛·耶洛的厕所里为苹果吹嘘——满足的顶峰. 这就是我们每天被抛弃的质量。

这就是我们生活的世界: 愚蠢、幽默、有趣、开玩笑、随意、放荡、聪明、狂喜。 在养育子女、礼拜、传教和主持活动,甚至是严肃的活动方面,所有这一切都是可悲的。 许多现代人从未品尝过严肃的喜悦,快乐的引力,快乐的真诚,或者欢乐的重量. 他们没有这样的分类。

有乐趣和无聊。 就这样。 生命是那么浅,那么微不足道。 诺亚问道:我怎能抗拒这一切呢? 我怎能走向一个不同的鼓手呢?” 1.区分欢喜乐. 第一,确保你明白快乐和乐趣并不相同。 今天,乐趣一词几乎取代了严肃的欢乐经历.

“考虑到生命的短暂性、死亡的必然性和上帝的伟大现实。” 有趣的是,当你在客厅地板上和孩子们玩时, 星期六和男生一起打橄榄球, 或者一天在迪士尼世界。 这很有趣, 但现在,教堂的栽培是乐趣,礼拜服务是乐趣,圣经研究是乐趣.

就像在二十英尺高的乔治亚松林中学习树木语言, 他们只是有趣的树。 他们并不伟大。 他们并不令人惊叹。 他们不会发抖。 他们只是有趣的树。

所以,诺亚, 增加你的喜悦和意义 和奇异的词汇, 因为比我们想承认的更多时候, 心脏收缩到 语言 我们必须表达它而不是相反。 如果你在不久之前就称它为“有趣”的话, 你的心会缩到词汇里 2. 知道你没有疯。

第二,听从圣经的警告, 圣经中非常了解那些不能快乐严肃的人,他们所有的语言都只是聪明或开玩笑,或三思而行. - 像个疯子

articles.content: An IMB missionary among the Deaf records a Bible story in sign language. IMB Photo Every dollar you give to the Lottie Moon offering goes to support missionaries like Noah Lewis who live and serve among the lost. Will you consider giving today? Noah Lewis couldn’t help signing along with a worship song playing in the background as Deaf friends gathered in his home for dinner. The International Mission Board appoints missionaries who are both Deaf and hearing to serve among the global Deaf. Many missionaries learn sign language for the first time, while others use their American Sign Language to more quickly learn global sign languages. IMB Photo The International Mission Board missionary was sitting in the living room with his roommate and two friends while others prepared food nearby. As a young, single adult, simply opening the doors to his home in the Middle East has created some of his most fruitful opportunities for gospel conversations. That evening, Lewis was stirred to worship the Lord. “I just love worshiping in sign language because it’s a full-body experience,” Lewis said. Lewis, who is hearing, began signing the song in American Sign Language. Across the room, one of his Muslim friends watched intently. When the song ended, his friend told him it was beautiful and asked to see another. Lewis explained that Christians use songs to worship God. His friend compared what he had seen to hearing the Islamic call to prayer. The exchange opened an opportunity for Lewis to explain Christian worship and why Christians worship Jesus. When his friend asked to see more, Lewis continued signing songs from the playlist. “He was just really captivated by it,” Lewis said. “It really felt like in that moment the Spirit was working in his heart.” The conversation did not end with a profession of faith. Instead, it became another step in a friendship where Lewis has watched spiritual curiosity grow over time. During Ramadan, the same friend asked about fasting. On another night, he asked how Christians pray. Each question has allowed Lewis to explain what Christians believe and why he follows Jesus. Those conversations reflect much of Lewis’ ministry. He has served in the Middle East for nearly a year and a half, spending much of his time learning sign language and building relationships in the local Deaf community. Learning sign language, like learning any language, requires time, practice and immersion in the community that uses it. For Lewis, that process has looked different from the experience of missionaries who can spend several hours each day in a formal language school. There are no comparable sign language centers where he serves, so much of his language learning happens through relationships with Deaf friends. Although Lewis has not had a dedicated language tutor since arriving on the field, personal relationships help him develop a strong conversational understanding of the sign language used where he serves. The process has also drawn him more deeply into the Deaf community he came to reach. “I want to genuinely learn about their language,” he said. “I want to be friends with them. I want to know who they are.” As Lewis’ ability to communicate grows, relationships deepen and opportunities to share the gospel follow. Even when he doesn’t know the exact sign he needs, friends help him find ways to communicate biblical truths. Lewis has learned to faithfully use the language he has while continuing to grow in his ability to communicate the gospel clearly. An IMB worker among the Deaf records a Bible story. Generous giving to the Lottie Moon Christmas Offering supports missions among the global Deaf. IMB Photo When the plan disappeared That dependence on God came into clearer focus during a recent trip to Central Asia. Lewis currently lives and serves in the Middle East, but he arrived on the field with a long-term desire to serve in Central Asia. 一名IMB在聋人中的传教士用手语记录圣经故事. IMB照片 你给洛蒂月球的每一美元 都用来支持传教士 比如诺亚·刘易斯 你会考虑今天给钱吗? 当聋人朋友聚集在家中吃饭时,

国际代表团委员会任命聋人和听力传教士在全球聋人中任职。 许多传教士首次学习手语,而其他传教士则使用他们的美国手语更快地学习全球手语.

IMB照片 国际传教委员会传教士与他的室友和两个朋友坐在客厅里,而其他人则在附近准备食物. 作为一个年轻、单身的成年人,只要打开通往他在中东的家的大门,就为他的福音对话创造了一些最富有成果的机会。 当晚,刘易斯被激起崇拜主.

「我只是喜欢手语崇拜, 正在听话的刘易斯开始用美国手语签署歌曲. 在房间里,他的一个穆斯林朋友故意观看。 歌曲结束的时候,他的朋友告诉他这很美丽,并请求见另一首. 刘易斯解释说,基督徒使用歌曲来崇拜上帝.

他的朋友比较了他所看到的听到的伊斯兰祈祷的呼声. 这次交流为刘易斯解释基督教崇拜和基督徒为何崇拜耶稣提供了机会. 当他的朋友要求看到更多时,刘易斯继续从播放列表上签名歌曲. 刘易斯说:“他只是被它迷住了。”

“在那个时刻,精神确实在他心中发挥作用。” 对话没有以信仰职业结束。 相反,它成为友谊的又一个步骤,刘易斯目睹了精神好奇心随时间推移而增长. 斋月期间,同友问斋事. 在另一个晚上,他问基督徒如何祈祷.

每个问题都让刘易斯解释基督徒相信什么,为什么他跟随耶稣. 这些谈话反映了刘易斯部的许多情况。 他在中东服务了近一年半,花了很多时间学习手语,在当地聋人社区建立关系.

学习手语,就像学习任何语言一样,需要时间,练习和沉浸在使用手语的社区中. 对刘易斯来说,这一进程与传教士的经历不同,传教士可以每天在一所正式语言学校中度过几个小时。

他所服务的手语中心并不存在类似的手语中心,所以他的许多语言学习都是通过与聋人朋友的关系发生的. 虽然刘易斯自到达球场后便没有专门的语言辅导员,但个人关系帮助他发展出对他所服务的手语的强烈的对话理解.

这一过程还使他更深入地融入了他所接触的聋人社区。 他说:“我想真正了解他们的语言。” “我想与他们成为朋友。 我想知道他们是谁。” 随着刘易斯沟通能力的增长,关系加深,分享福音的机会随之而来。

即使他不知道自己需要什么具体标志, 刘易斯学会了忠实使用他拥有的语言,同时继续增强他明确传达福音的能力. 一个IMB工人在聋人中记录了一个圣经故事. 慷慨地给洛蒂月亮圣诞节 提供全球聋人中的支持任务

IMB 图片 当计划消失时 在最近访问中亚期间,这种对上帝的依赖得到了更明确的关注。 刘易斯目前在中东生活和服役,但他远期带着在中亚服役的愿望赶到现场. 他最近的旅行使他能够更多地了解文化,聋人社区

articles.title: Aku Simon dari Kirene
articles.summary_zh: 我是来自古利内的西门。 我的名字表明我住在非洲大陆。
articles.title_zh: 我是古利奈人西门。
articles.content: Aku Simon dari Kirene. Namaku menunjukkan bahwa aku tinggal di benua Afrika. Meski demikian, kulitku tidak hitam dan bibirku pun tidak tebal. Dan meskipun sudah selama beberapa generasi keluargaku berdiam di Kirene, ibu kota Kireneika -- sebuah kota Yunani di Afrika Utara yang terkenal karena kemakmuran dan para ahli filsafatnya -- kulitku tidaklah putih. Aku Simon dari Kirene. Aku orang Yahudi asli sampai ke jantung hati. Sejak kecil, kutaati semua hukum agama tanpa kecuali, walaupun aku tidak lagi fasih berbahasa Aram akibat dibesarkan dalam masyarakat yang berbahasa Yunani. Aku Simon dari Kirene. Aku tidak ingin berkisah tentang diri sendiri. Juga tidak tentang semua pengalaman hidupku. Aku cuma ingin bercerita tentang pengalamanku yang satu itu. Pengalaman yang kemudian mengubah seluruh jalan hidupku. Dan seluruh jalan hidup Anda, sekiranya Anda juga mengalaminya. Hari itu adalah hari Jumat. Aku baru saja tiba di Yerusalem pagi itu. Tujuanku melakukan perjalanan yang jauh itu adalah untuk merayakan hari raya Paskah. Setiap tahun aku melakukannya. Tidak sedikit pun aku heran melihat orang-orang penuh sesak memadati kota. Walaupun letih, segera setelah menaruh barang-barangku di hotel dan membersihkan badan, aku keluar berjalan-jalan untuk menikmati keriuhan kota yang sedang larut dalam semarak pesta. Lengking jeritan anak-anak yang berlari ria kian kemari, teriakan membujuk bahkan kadang-kadang memaksa para pedagang yang menjajakan barang-barangnya, dan bau asap dupa atau suara syahdu orang-orang yang menyanyikan kidung-kidung pujaan -- semua itu membuat aku lupa akan keletihanku. Suasana yang agak liar ini memang berbeda benar dengan suasana Kirene yang sopan dan tertib. Namun, lebih hidup. Tiba-tiba ada kegaduhan yang tak biasa. Para serdadu Roma menyeruak massa. "Ah, lagi-lagi pawai laskar-laskar Romawi untuk mengingatkan siapa yang berkuasa di negeri ini," pikirku. Akan tetapi tidak. Di baris paling depan, ada seorang serdadu yang memegang panji bertulis: "Yesus, orang Nazaret, raja orang Yahudi." Aku memang belum pernah berjumpa dengan-Nya. Akan tetapi, nama "Yesus", siapa yang tidak mengenal-Nya? Dia adalah tokoh paling kontroversial. Yang tidak dapat kumengerti, mengapa serdadu Romawi mengarak panji seperti itu. Karena itu, aku mendekat untuk melihat lebih dekat. Di tengah pagar betis laskar-laskar Roma itu, tiga orang melangkah pelan memanggul salib. "Penjahat-penjahat besar," pikirku. Namun, apa hubungannya dengan panji itu? Kemudian aku semakin mengerti. Riuh rendah massa rakyat menyebut-nyebut nama Yesus sambil mencemooh-Nya. Tidak kurang pula yang meludahi-Nya. Akan tetapi, yang manakah Yesus di antara ketiga orang itu? Aku Simon dari Kirene. Aku semakin mendekat. Lalu aku tahu dengan pasti yang mana Yesus. Dia paling kecil, hampir tidak berotot. Rambut panjang-Nya terurai, lekat di sana-sini oleh darah kering yang berasal dari duri-duri yang teranyam di kepala-Nya. Sekujur tubuh-Nya biru lebam. Langkah-Nya tertatih-tatih. Amat letih. Akan tetapi mata-Nya -- meski merah sebab kurang tidur -- namun tetap tajam menusuk setiap kali menatap. Anehnya, juga begitu lembut menyejukkan. Aku tak dapat lepas memandang mata-Nya itu. Penuh wibawa, tetapi juga begitu menenangkan dan kebapakan. Lalu Dia roboh. Tubuh-Nya yang kecil dan nyaris hancur itu tidak kuat lagi menahan bobot salib di pundak-Nya. Massa berteriak kesenangan bagai binatang liar yang haus darah. Cemeti melayang menyayat punggung-Nya. Darah menyembur. Dan Dia pun bangkit lagi pelan-pelan. Keletihan. Tetapi mata-Nya itu, oi, mata-Nya. Lalu Dia berjalan beberapa langkah. Namun, roboh lagi. Arak-arakan berhenti. Massa semakin buas. Cemeti melayang berulang-ulang. Darah menyembur. Namun, Dia tak mampu bangun kembali. Aku Simon dari Kirene. Entah mengapa, aku tidak terkesan benar oleh semua itu. Kecuali oleh tatapan mata-Nya. Mata-Nya itu, oi, mata-Nya.
