featured.content: Imagine reading a book, watching a show or listening to a podcast when suddenly the story just stops mid-sentence. Maybe the previous reader has ripped out a page, the series was canceled before the showrunners could wrap up the plotline, or the producer distributed the episode before realizing it was incomplete. How incredibly frustrating to not experience the full story from start to finish! It can leave us emotionally unsettled, frustrated or even distraught, because at our core, we desire completion. We want to know how things start and how they end. We don’t just want a taste, because it feels like a tease. We’re left wanting more . And we’re not alone in that desire! The same is true for communities around the world who are still waiting for the full counsel of God’s Word in a language and format they clearly understand. For some, they’re still waiting for the first verse of Scripture to be translated into their language. Others might have a few verses, chapters or Scripture portions . Still others are blessed with a complete New Testament but are waiting for the Old Testament so they can understand everything from Genesis to Revelation. They get a teaser of God’s great story — perhaps enough to understand who Jesus is and that He died for them — but they don’t have the full context as to why His sacrifice was so significant. The Bible changes everything, and together with our partners, Wycliffe believes that everyone should have access to the whole of Scripture. But don’t just take our word for it! Explore these Bible translation stories from our friends around the world who have personally experienced individual and community transformation as a result of encountering God through His Word. Want a glimpse of what it’s like to only have a portion of God’s Word? This “H ly B bl: Incomplete Scriptures” digital booklet helps you see what it’s like to have gaps in your understanding of the Bible. Explore the booklet → The Full “Outfit” of God’s Word Caroline always had access to a Bible growing up. But watching the Chonyi people of Kenya receive the New Testament in their language refreshed her passion for Bible translation, a mission she’s actively engaged in through SIL Kenya, a partner of Wycliffe. “They took a couple of Bibles, wrapped them up like a child,” she shared. “And there was a woman who was carrying the [Bibles]. And they were swinging and dancing, lifting up the [Bibles] and saying, ‘This is our child.’ Calling people, ‘Come,” in the Chonyi language. ‘Come and celebrate the child that has been born in us.’ “That is how the Chonyi people have taken the Bible — the New Testament — in their own language. That it is their child and they’re taking it seriously, making it bear fruit.” People gathered to hear Scripture read in their language, Bible studies began and the impact spread: 300 adults and 50 children gave their lives to Christ! At the celebration, the local pastors shared that now that the New Testament is complete, it’s like they have a shirt. But a shirt isn’t enough; they want a pair of pants (the Old Testament) to complete the outfit! Now work is underway to translate the Old Testament into Chonyi so that they can have the full “outfit” of God’s Word. Praise God! Watch how the Chonyi community celebrated the dedication of the New Testament in their community! One day, someone from the community called the local translation office with a request. “We have been enjoying this Jesus story from this elderly woman, and now it has broken. featured.content: What circumstances or experiences have shaped your life? For 93-year-old Millie (name changed), her testimony was shaped by the Great Depression and deep loss, but also by an enduring faith and a lifetime of seeing God’s faithfulness unfold. Every chapter of her story points back to the same truth: God’s Word sustained her. Millie was only six weeks old when her father suffered severe burns to his legs from an explosion. Overnight, Millie’s mother found herself caring for a newborn and a toddler while tending to a husband who was facing a long and painful recovery. Life was uncertain, and every dollar mattered. Yet when Millie looks back on those difficult years, she doesn’t first remember hardship. She remembers the faith that was demonstrated. Every Sunday morning, Millie’s mother would reach into a small jar where she saved a few quarters and hand one to Millie and one to her sister before they left for church. The family didn’t have much, but her parents believed that honoring God was never dependent on how much they had. “We were taught to tithe,” Millie recalled. “To give to the Lord because of His goodness to us.” Long before Millie understood phrases like “stewardship” or “planned giving,” she was learning a lesson that would shape the rest of her life: Generosity isn’t born out of abundance; it grows from trusting the one who provides. See how God is using the generosity of one group of friends to impact Bible translation → The Scripture Millie Carried Through the Years As Millie grew older, that foundation of faith continued to guide her. She married a godly man, and they centered their efforts around family, teaching and serving others. Both were educators, and they poured themselves into the lives of children while also remaining deeply involved in their church and community. Together, the couple experienced the joys of raising a family. But they also walked through a devastating loss. While Millie was pregnant with their younger son, the couple’s 7-year-old daughter tragically died. It’s difficult to imagine the depth of grief that Millie endured. Through her pain, she turned to God and His Word for comfort. Even now, decades later, she is still anchored by the promises found in Scripture. One particular passage resonates with Millie deeply: You will keep in perfect peace all who trust in you, all whose thoughts are fixed on you! Trust in the LORD always, for the LORD GOD is the eternal Rock. — Isaiah 26:3-4 (NLT) For Millie, Scripture was what met her in her grief, strengthened her through suffering and continued to anchor and guide her throughout the next chapters of her life. This past Easter, Mille’s family experienced another tragic event — her son was involved in a head-on collision. Thankfully he survived but was hospitalized and treated for serious injuries. Millie believes the Lord’s presence was unmistakable in the moments that followed this event. A Gift Rooted in Gratitude Not long after her son’s accident, Millie received a mailing from Wycliffe Foundation that included information about charitable gift annuities. For Millie, this felt like an invitation and an opportunity to respond to God’s faithfulness through generosity. A charitable gift annuity was not a completely new concept to Millie. Through family members connected with Faith Comes By Hearing (a Wycliffe partner organization), she learned about this unique giving option and appreciated that it could provide her with a lifetime income while also supporting a ministry she cared deeply about. When she received the information about charitable gift annuities, she saw it as another opportunity to worship the Lord and express her gratitude for His protection and provision. 是什么环境或经历决定了你的生活? 对于93岁的米莉(名字变了)来说,她的证词是被大萧条和严重损失所塑造的,但也是一种持久的信仰和一生目睹上帝的忠诚发展。 她的故事的每一章都指向同样的真理:上帝的话支撑了她.

米莉只有六个星期大,当她的父亲在爆炸中腿部严重烧伤。 一夜之间,米莉的母亲发现自己在照顾一个新生儿和幼儿,同时照顾一个面临长期痛苦康复的丈夫。 生活是不确定的,每一美元都很重要。 但当米莉回顾那些艰难的岁月时,

以至报应我们的主。 早在米莉明白“偷窥”或“计划施舍”等短语之前,她就已经吸取了将塑造其余生的教训:慷慨并非由丰产而生;它从信任提供者而增长。

幸好他幸存下来,但住院治疗严重受伤。 Milie认为,在事件发生之后的那一刻,上帝的出现是无可置疑的。 Millie在儿子出事不久后收到Wycliffe基金会的邮件,

当她收到有关慈善礼物年金的信息时,她认为这是又一次机会,可以崇拜主,并对他的保护和供养表示感谢. 米莉联系了威克利夫基金会,高级礼品规划顾问迈克尔·奥西平蒂(Michael Occhipinti)迅速与她联系. 在整个过程中,他在她祷告地考虑她的下一步时与她同行。

featured.summary_zh: 伊恩· H ·穆雷（ Iain H. Murray ）的《艾米·卡迈克尔：灰烬之美》（ Amy Carmichael: Beauty for Ashes ）是对爱尔兰传教士前往印度的非凡生活的简短复述。接下来是该标题的第4章， “艰难的日子和黄金岁月。“如果说艾米·卡迈克尔的生活有任何模式的话，那就是令人耳目一新的时代，然后是考验的时代，令人兴奋的‘攀登’的时代[…]艾米·卡迈克尔的帖子：令人耳目一新的时代和考验的时代首先出现在真理美国的旗帜上。
featured.title_zh: 艾米·卡迈克尔：令人耳目一新的时代和审判的时代
featured.content: Iain H. Murray’s Amy Carmichael: Beauty for Ashes is a short retelling of the remarkable life of the Irish missionary to India. What follows is Chapter 4 of that title, ‘Hard Days and Golden Years.’ If there was any pattern to Amy Carmichael’s life it was of times of refreshing then of trials, of exhilarating ‘climbing’ then of walking in dark ravines. In part her explanation was that demonic activity follows the work of the Holy Spirit. As she quoted from George Bowen, When Christianity assumes an aggressive attitude the first result is a great exhibition of Satanic power. Satan’s power to be manifested must be assaulted. 1 Such an understanding does not come so readily to us who do not live, as she did, within sight of demon possession, or within hearing of tom-tom drums calling devotees to idols. Shortly before Walker 2 had left on his last mission, he had been sitting with Amy and others in deck chairs under the stars. ‘We had been talking’, she later wrote, of work and workers, and of those (to me) most wonderful women, who seemed perfectly self-reliant, needing no strong arm alongside. I remember how, suddenly startled at the bare thought of working alone, in the sense of all the burden of responsibility, I exclaimed that I never could do it. Mr Walker laughed. ‘Well, you don’t have to’, he said. 3 Amy was the weaker when her ‘strong arm’ died at the age of fifty-four. What she owed to Walker’s ‘courageous championship’ of the children’s work, ‘through its first very difficult years, no words can tell, nor can words tell how he is missed’. 4 At times, as she faced her loss, she would need to say to herself, ‘Don’t give up, don’t be afraid: go on.’ Prayer for ‘fortitude’ entered her life. There were unsympathetic neighbours who observed the work at Dohnavur who supposed that Amy would now be more vulnerable. One of these was a lawyer who, soon after Walker’s death, wrote with the demand that current work on the building of a wall around the compoundbe stopped, and that a half-built nursery should be pulled down. They were using ground, he claimed, to which they did not have legal title. ‘He had waited till Mr Walker’s death had left us, as he thought, defenceless, almost desolate, and sure to be easily cowed by threats of court trouble.’ The wall building had been prompted by the passage of a tiger through the compound at night; and the new nursery was necessitated by the growing numbers of children for whom Dohnavur had become home. Amy ignored the letter and heard nothing more of the threat. The Dohnavur family of seventy children and grown-ups in 1906, had doubled itself by this date, and the need of more helpers was pressing. Mrs Catherine Carmichael was never able to return. She died on July 14, 1913. A few weeks earlier a letter from her to Amy began with the words, ‘My own most precious earthly possession’. While Amy did not lament her mother’s death—for no Christian death was to be ‘lamented’—in the days ahead she needed to preach to herself, ‘I must remind myself to live in the joy of those gone, not grovel in the sense of my loss.’ Mrs Carmichael had been a constant supporter and representative for Dohnavur in Britain. She acted as the home secretary to whom gifts could be sent, and helped to make her daughter’s books more widely known. In 1912 those books had been noted by Queen Mary, wife of King George V, who expressed her thanks for them. featured.title_zh: IMB传教士在服务之旅中分享首尔的愿景
featured.content: Ask most people what comes to mind when they think of South Korea, and they’ll likely mention K-pop, skincare, cutting-edge technology, or bustling city streets filled with young professionals. Hun and Eunjoo Sol see those things too. But after more than a decade serving as International Mission Board missionaries in Seoul, they also see something many visitors never notice. “Many people think that Korea is exciting and successful,” Hun said. “They think about the K-pop, the K-culture, K-technology, K-cosmetics. Yes, good things… But many Korean people are struggling right now.” The Sols, who were featured in the 2025 Week of Prayer for International Missions , continue to rely on the prayers of faithful Southern Baptists. Prayers sustain them and help to push back the darkness they confront in their home culture. Hun often describes that hidden struggle with a Korean word: han. There is no simple English translation. It speaks to a deep sorrow shaped by generations of war, division, loss, and the quiet resolve to endure. Hun sees it in the young adults he meets every week—people navigating loneliness and relentless expectations, quietly asking what their lives are for beneath a veneer of success. Han is heavy. For many young adults, that weight can feel unbearable. Suicide is one of the leading causes of death among teenagers and young adults in South Korean. Hun and Eunjoo see the effects of that reality every day, and it’s one reason they believe they have no time to waste. That understanding shaped the week of Serve Tour Seoul this summer. There were no construction sites, no paintbrushes, no tools or work gloves. Instead, the team stepped into ministries local churches had been faithfully building long before the volunteers arrived. In May, 27 volunteers from seven churches across the United States came alongside local churches already serving their communities in Seoul, Paju, and Gwangju. They taught English classes, ran children’s camps, walked neighborhoods in prayer, distributed food, and sat down with college students, one conversation at a time. For Nick Holst of Sandals Church in Riverside, California, the goal was simple enough to say in a sentence: “We came to meet people,” Holst said. “We want to hear their stories, and that leads to some very meaningful connections as you get past the surface into something deeper.” That’s where the week actually lived: past the surface and past the small talk, where the quiet weight of han is often carried without words. On college campuses, volunteers played games, asked questions and mostly just listened. Some conversations lasted a few minutes and ended there. Others kept going long past the point where either person expected them to. One morning, after asking his church back home to pray, Holst sat down with a university student named Intec. They talked about culture first, the way strangers do, and then the conversation turned somewhere neither of them planned. “I got to ask him, ‘What do Koreans believe?’” Holst recalled. Intec said he didn’t believe in God. Then he recited John 3:16 from memory, word for word, a verse he’d heard somewhere along the way and never forgotten. Before they parted, Holst asked if he could pray that God would keep drawing Intec toward Himself. “He said yes.” In a city where many conversations never move beyond the surface, the exchange was a reminder of why the team had come. Not to win an argument, but to listen, to ask questions, and to trust God with what happens next. The same pattern unfolded elsewhere, beginning in classrooms and ending on city streets. Jeremy Doyle, missions pastor at Valley Baptist Church in Bakersfield, California, watched an English conversation club grow from two students on its first night to eight by the second. Nobody advertised it as anything more than a place to practice English, but the room kept filling, and so did the conversations. The team’s work with students didn’t stop there. featured.title_zh: IMB传教士使用家庭、咖啡馆、应用程序为西班牙的福音对话敞开大门
featured.content: Men and women gather to discuss spiritual topics with Caleb and Carina Beaty, International Mission Board missionaries who serve in Madrid. IMB Photo Across Spain, people looking for connection and meaningful conversation turn to the internet to find groups where they can meet others. At a café by the river, Caleb and Carina Beaty engage in conversations about finding purpose, beauty and “what’s wrong with the world.” A website called Meetup allows people to search for groups to meet in person. The description of the Beatys’ group indicates that it discusses spiritual topics. People come expecting to talk about faith, so it’s not a surprise when they arrive. Caleb said he always has a list of questions that begin broadly and funnel into questions such as, “If there were a God …” or “What do you think Christians believe about that?” or “Why do you think religions have such different perspectives?” The Beatys’ goal in these conversations is to work toward deeper worldview questions within 45 minutes to an hour. Most of the people who attend their Meetup group are from Madrid, but they also have conversations with people from other countries. During one Meetup, Caleb and Carina shared how creation was perfect, but sin led to a world separated from the Father. God offers salvation through the death and resurrection of Jesus, they explained. “There are times we’re able to get to a clear gospel presentation with a group of people, and sometimes we’re doing pre-evangelism.” Caleb said. Some repeat attendees who have been attending for more than a year quickly jump to the heart of the discussion. “All right, Caleb, what’s the Bible say about suffering?” they’ll ask. Caleb and Carina then have the opportunity to share the Christian perspective. IMB missionaries Caleb and Carina Beaty and their children pose for a photo in a park in Madrid, Spain.  IMB Photo Spain has secularized rapidly since the 1990s, Caleb said. While many may think of it as a Catholic nation, many people do not know the basic tenets of Christianity. “We’ve got all the churches, we’ve got the cathedrals, and they do processions, but the average person on the street does not know anything about the gospel and does not know anything about Jesus,” Caleb said. Younger Spaniards are drawn to their group and are receptive to the gospel because they don’t have a spiritual foundation or know anyone who does. “There’s just this curiosity because, for a lot of them, they’ve never met someone who actually believes that God exists, and that changes your life,” Carina said. “I’ve had people completely shocked that we believe in God. ‘You really believe that God exists?’ They can’t wrap their mind around that.” During one Meetup, a man contrasted Protestant and Catholic beliefs by saying Protestants focus on Jesus’ suffering and Catholics on Mary’s grief. Caleb responded that evangelicals focus on the resurrection. When Caleb said Jesus rose from the dead, the man replied that he needed to look into that. Caleb said encounters like that reveal how little many Spaniards know about the gospel. Caleb noted the irony of the man’s sharing the Catholic perspective without truly understanding it. He is not the only person the Beatys have met who has missed the heart of the gospel. A friend of the Beatys told them she’d heard Jesus died, but she hadn’t heard he rose from the dead. A man reads a passage of Scripture during a Bible study hosted by IMB missionaries Caleb and Carina Beaty at their family’s apartment in Madrid, Spain. Five atheists began attending their Bible study after attending the couple’s Meetup group. IMB Photo The Beatys also host seasonal outreach events through the Meetup. Members from their church in Madrid have started attending the Meetup to learn how the Beatys lead discussions. Their group has become so popular, a waitlist has formed. Caleb and Carina host a small-group Bible study in their home. Five atheists who joined their Meetup now attend the Bible study.

featured.content: An IMB missionary among the Deaf records a Bible story in sign language. IMB Photo Every dollar you give to the Lottie Moon offering goes to support missionaries like Noah Lewis who live and serve among the lost. Will you consider giving today? Noah Lewis couldn’t help signing along with a worship song playing in the background as Deaf friends gathered in his home for dinner. The International Mission Board appoints missionaries who are both Deaf and hearing to serve among the global Deaf. Many missionaries learn sign language for the first time, while others use their American Sign Language to more quickly learn global sign languages. IMB Photo The International Mission Board missionary was sitting in the living room with his roommate and two friends while others prepared food nearby. As a young, single adult, simply opening the doors to his home in the Middle East has created some of his most fruitful opportunities for gospel conversations. That evening, Lewis was stirred to worship the Lord. “I just love worshiping in sign language because it’s a full-body experience,” Lewis said. Lewis, who is hearing, began signing the song in American Sign Language. Across the room, one of his Muslim friends watched intently. When the song ended, his friend told him it was beautiful and asked to see another. Lewis explained that Christians use songs to worship God. His friend compared what he had seen to hearing the Islamic call to prayer. The exchange opened an opportunity for Lewis to explain Christian worship and why Christians worship Jesus. When his friend asked to see more, Lewis continued signing songs from the playlist. “He was just really captivated by it,” Lewis said. “It really felt like in that moment the Spirit was working in his heart.” The conversation did not end with a profession of faith. Instead, it became another step in a friendship where Lewis has watched spiritual curiosity grow over time. During Ramadan, the same friend asked about fasting. On another night, he asked how Christians pray. Each question has allowed Lewis to explain what Christians believe and why he follows Jesus. Those conversations reflect much of Lewis’ ministry. He has served in the Middle East for nearly a year and a half, spending much of his time learning sign language and building relationships in the local Deaf community. Learning sign language, like learning any language, requires time, practice and immersion in the community that uses it. For Lewis, that process has looked different from the experience of missionaries who can spend several hours each day in a formal language school. There are no comparable sign language centers where he serves, so much of his language learning happens through relationships with Deaf friends. Although Lewis has not had a dedicated language tutor since arriving on the field, personal relationships help him develop a strong conversational understanding of the sign language used where he serves. The process has also drawn him more deeply into the Deaf community he came to reach. “I want to genuinely learn about their language,” he said. “I want to be friends with them. I want to know who they are.” As Lewis’ ability to communicate grows, relationships deepen and opportunities to share the gospel follow. Even when he doesn’t know the exact sign he needs, friends help him find ways to communicate biblical truths. Lewis has learned to faithfully use the language he has while continuing to grow in his ability to communicate the gospel clearly. An IMB worker among the Deaf records a Bible story. 一名IMB在聋人中的传教士用手语记录圣经故事. IMB照片 你给洛蒂月球的每一美元 都用来支持传教士 比如诺亚·刘易斯 你会考虑今天给钱吗? 当聋人朋友聚集在家中吃饭时,

国际代表团委员会任命聋人和听力传教士在全球聋人中任职。 许多传教士首次学习手语,而其他传教士则使用他们的美国手语更快地学习全球手语.

IMB照片 国际传教委员会传教士与他的室友和两个朋友坐在客厅里,而其他人则在附近准备食物. 作为一个年轻、单身的成年人,只要打开通往他在中东的家的大门,就为他的福音对话创造了一些最富有成果的机会。 当晚,刘易斯被激起崇拜主.

「我只是喜欢手语崇拜, 正在听话的刘易斯开始用美国手语签署歌曲. 在房间里,他的一个穆斯林朋友故意观看。 歌曲结束的时候,他的朋友告诉他这很美丽,并请求见另一首. 刘易斯解释说,基督徒使用歌曲来崇拜上帝.

他的朋友比较了他所看到的听到的伊斯兰祈祷的呼声. 这次交流为刘易斯解释基督教崇拜和基督徒为何崇拜耶稣提供了机会. 当他的朋友要求看到更多时,刘易斯继续从播放列表上签名歌曲. 刘易斯说:“他只是被它迷住了。”

“在那个时刻,精神确实在他心中发挥作用。” 对话没有以信仰职业结束。 相反,它成为友谊的又一个步骤,刘易斯目睹了精神好奇心随时间推移而增长. 斋月期间,同友问斋事. 在另一个晚上,他问基督徒如何祈祷.

每个问题都让刘易斯解释基督徒相信什么,为什么他跟随耶稣. 这些谈话反映了刘易斯部的许多情况。 他在中东服务了近一年半,花了很多时间学习手语,在当地聋人社区建立关系.

学习手语,就像学习任何语言一样,需要时间,练习和沉浸在使用手语的社区中. 对刘易斯来说,这一进程与传教士的经历不同,传教士可以每天在一所正式语言学校中度过几个小时。

他所服务的手语中心并不存在类似的手语中心,所以他的许多语言学习都是通过与聋人朋友的关系发生的. 虽然刘易斯自到达球场后便没有专门的语言辅导员,但个人关系帮助他发展出对他所服务的手语的强烈的对话理解.

这一过程还使他更深入地融入了他所接触的聋人社区。 他说:“我想真正了解他们的语言。” “我想与他们成为朋友。 我想知道他们是谁。” 随着刘易斯沟通能力的增长,关系加深,分享福音的机会随之而来。

即使他不知道自己需要什么具体标志, 刘易斯学会了忠实使用他拥有的语言,同时继续增强他明确传达福音的能力. 一个IMB工人在聋人中记录了一个圣经故事. 慷慨地给洛蒂月亮圣诞节 提供全球聋人中的支持任务

IMB 图片 当计划消失时 在最近访问中亚期间,这种对上帝的依赖得到了更明确的关注。 刘易斯目前在中东生活和服役,但他远期带着在中亚服役的愿望赶到现场. 他最近的旅行使他能够更多地了解文化,聋人社区

featured.content: The eastern face of St. Peter's Basilica in the Vatican City in Rome, Italy, is famous for its central balcony from which popes give their papal addresses. Most people in Rome have at least a cultural connection to Roman Catholicism as the city is “the heart of Catholicism.” IMB Photo In the city where Jason and Lizzy Davis serve, some steps have a lot of meaning. And the meaning is different for them than it is for the thousands who travel there to visit that site. “If you come to Rome, you can come to a place called the Holy Steps,” Jason said. “People go there, and they’ll crawl up on their knees and pray the rosary all the way up.” From the top of the steps, a mural depicting Jesus on the Cross looks down on those making the pilgrimage. For Jason and Lizzy, it’s a spiritual experience, a picture of a religion that asks people to earn their way to Jesus. “That’s really the opposite of what the gospel is. The gospel is Jesus saying, ‘No, you can’t do it . . . no matter how good you think you are,’” they said. Most people in Rome have at the very least a cultural connection to Roman Catholicism, as the city is “the heart of Catholicism.” Jason explained, “It’s where the Pope lives in the Vatican. It’s very much part of the religion and culture. It’s all intertwined here.” An ‘unavoidable’ call Jason and Lizzy are investing their lives as International Mission Board missionaries in Rome, Italy, to share the truth of the gospel. The Davises partner with national believers through a new church plant, and they’re seeking to plant more churches within the city. Lizzy said for her, the call to missions was unavoidable. “I grew up as a third culture kid, or a missionary kid. My parents were on the mission field, as were my grandparents, all with the International Mission Board.” Then her family moved to Virginia for her dad to work for IMB’s home office staff. As a middle schooler and high schooler, every time Lizzy heard about the need for the gospel to go forth, she felt a burden, a “burning” in her heart. She didn’t know what God would do with that, but she had a feeling she would see one day. Now, years later, she and Jason spend their time trying to find as many opportunities as they can to invite people into their home so they can share the hope of Jesus with them. That can mean Bible study or simply sharing a meal. ‘Completely lost’ Jason has been surprised by just how often people are willing to talk about faith. “You can get into spiritual conversations very quickly with people, especially if you’re just open and honest with them.” Lizzy shared that one of the easiest ways to do this is to be willing to let your day be interrupted. “That’s something I’ve seen Jason do firsthand in our neighborhood. He walks down the street, and everybody knows him because he stops and takes the time to ask them questions about their families, gets to know people, gets to know the newspaper stand guy and the guy at the fruit stand and the grocery store ladies.” She emphasized that caring about people is “what Christ would do.” The Davises, whose previous mission service prevents their photos from being published, live in a neighborhood of about 130,000 people. Their church of 15 people is the only evangelical congregation there. Lizzy said the area is “truly a lost, completely lost, dark neighborhood” with people who have never heard the gospel. Thousands more come to their area on a religious quest. The Davis family’s neighborhood is home to the Basilica Papale di San Paolo (the Papal Basilica of Saint Paul), one of the city’s four major basilicas. “So we get a lot of people coming on spiritual journeys, visiting our neighborhood, seeking some sort of spiritual experience. featured.title_zh: 【2026但以理祷告会：第12天】我曾三次试图结束自己的生命……“即使浑身是血，也要活着。”
featured.content:
2026년 다니엘기도회 12일차 간증 너는 피투성이라도 살아 있으라 강사: 임금주 사모(평택 함께하는교회) 본문: 에스겔 16장 6절

1. 40년을 기다려 주신 하나님

사랑하는 성도 여러분, 오늘 이 자리에 서게 하신 하나님께 모든 영광을 올려 드립니다. 저는 감사일기를 쓰다가, 정확히 777일이 되었다는 사실을 알았습니다. 하나님께서 오늘 어떤 은혜를 베푸실지 기대하는 마음으로 이 자리에 섰습니다.

저는 하나님께서 제 삶에 행하신 일들을 책으로 기록하고 싶어 9년 동안 기도했습니다. 마침내 출판의 길이 열렸을 때 하나님께 여쭈었습니다. “하나님, 제가 무엇을 이루었다고 책을 쓰겠습니까?”

그때 제 마음에 이런 말씀이 들렸습니다. “왜 네가 이룬 것을 쓰려고 하니? 내가 너에게 이루어 준 것을 써라.” 그리고 또 하나의 깨달음을 주셨습니다. “너는 9년을 기다렸니? 나는 너를 40년 기다렸다.”

저는 책 한 권을 위해 9년을 기다렸다고 생각했지만, 하나님께서는 제가 온전히 돌아오기까지 40년을 기다려 주셨습니다. 제가 하나님을 외면하고 스스로를 포기하려 했던 순간에도, 하나님은 저를 놓지 않으셨습니다.

오늘 제 간증은 제가 무엇을 이루었는지가 아니라 하나님께서 어떻게 저를 살리셨는지에 관한 이야기입니다.

저는 어린 시절 알코올 중독이었던 아버지로부터 오랫동안 성적 학대를 당했습니다. 가장 안전해야 할 가정에서 깊은 상처를 받았지만, 누구에게도 말하지 못했습니다. 일곱 남매를 키우느라 지쳐 계신 어머니께 차마 말씀드릴 수 없었습니다.

불교 집안에서 태어났지만, 여덟 살 때 언니를 따라 교회에 갔습니다. 이후 수련회에서 하나님을 깊이 만났고, 의료선교사가 되고 싶다는 꿈을 품었습니다. 그 꿈을 따라 간호학과에 진학했습니다.

그러나 신앙생활을 한다고 어린 시절의 상처가 저절로 사라지지는 않았습니다. 마음속에는 수치심과 열등감이 남아 있었습니다. 용기를 내어 교회에서 제 아픔을 털어놓았지만 그 이야기가 다른 사람들에게 알려지면서 더 큰 상처를 받았습니다. 우울감이 깊어졌고, 스물세 살에 처음으로 제 생명을 포기하려 했습니다. 그 순간 제 입에서 기도가 나왔습니다. “하나님, 저 살고 싶어요. 지금 저를 살려 주시면 하나님을 위해 제 삶을 드리겠습니다.”

저는 어머니께 도움을 청했고 살아남았습니다. 그러나 살아남았다고 해서 마음의 상처까지 치유된 것은 아니었습니다. 그때는 몰랐습니다. 하나님께서 저를 살리신 이유가 있고, 아직 끝나지 않은 이야기가 있다는 사실을 말입니다.

2. 절망의 끝에서 들려온 생명의 말씀

저는 서울대학교병원에서 간호사로 일하면서, 저를 사랑해 주는 사람을 만나 결혼했습니다. 남편은 예수님을 믿지 않았고, 시댁에서도 결혼 후 교회에 다니지 않기를 원했습니다. 저는 그 요구를 받아들여 예배의 자리를 떠났습니다.

그런데 결혼 6년째, 서른두 살이었던 남편이 대장암 말기 진단을 받았습니다. 남편은 투병 중 예수님을 믿고 세례를 받았습니다. 저는 하나님께서 남편을 고쳐 주실 것이라고 기대했지만, 결국 남편은 세상을 떠났습니다. 저는 서른여섯 살에 두 아이를 키우는, 홀로 된 어머니가 되었습니다.

슬픔이 가시기도 전에, 방송을 보고 접근한 사기꾼에게 남편의 사망보험금과 신용대출금까지 빼앗겼습니다. 피해액은 2억 원이 훨씬 넘었습니다. 남편을 잃은 슬픔에 경제적 절망까지 겹치자, 더 이상 살아갈 자신이 없었습니다.

두 번째로 생명을 포기하려던 바로 그때, 전화가 울렸습니다. 평소 새벽기도를 열심히 다니던 후배였습니다. 마지막 인사라도 해야겠다는 생각으로 전화를 받았는데, 후배가 갑자기 말했습니다. “언니, 왜 죽으려고 그래?”

아무에게도 말하지 않았는데 어떻게 알았을까요? 저는 놀라서 하던 행동을 멈추었습니다. 이후 어머니께 도움을 청하고, 그동안 숨겨왔던 사기 피해와 고통을 털어놓았습니다.

나중에 알게 된 사실은 더욱 놀라웠습니다. 제가 죽음을 생각했던 그날, 여러 사람이 저를 위해 중보기도를 하고 있었습니다. 저는 혼자라고 생각했지만, 혼자가 아니었습니다. 제가 기도할 힘조차 없을 때, 하나님께서는 다른 사람들의 기도를 통해 저를 붙들어 주셨습니다.

두 번째 위기를 넘겼지만, 빚과 우울감은 계속되었습니다. 평택으로 생활의 터전을 옮겼어도 마음의 고통은 사라지지 않았습니다. 밖에서는 웃었지만, 혼자 있을 때면 절망이 밀려왔습니다. 2014년, 저는 세 번째로 죽음을 생각했습니다. 더 이상 살아갈 이유를 찾을 수 없었습니다.

그때 하나님께서 제 마음에 주신 말씀이 에스겔 16장 6절이었습니다. “너는 피투성이라도 살아 있으라.” 저는 그 말씀을 읽으며 울었습니다. 하나님께서는 상처를 모두 해결하고 오라고 말씀하지 않으셨습니다. 깨끗해진 다음에 살아도 된다고 하지 않으셨습니다. 피투성이가 된 저를 향해 그 모습 그대로 살아 있으라고 말씀하셨습니다. 마치 하나님께서 저를 너무 사랑하시기에, 제발 죽지 말고 살아 달라고 말씀하시는 것 같았습니다.

그날 빚이 없어지거나 문제가 해결된 것은 아니었습니다. 그러나 살아야 할 이유가 생겼습니다. 저는 그 말씀을 붙들고 하루를 살아냈습니다. 또 하루를 살아냈습니다. 저는 제 인생이 피투성이가 되었다는 사실만 바라보았지만, 하나님께서는 그런 저를 여전히 사랑하고 계셨습니다. 그 사랑이 저를 다시 일으켜 세웠습니다.

3. 하나님 아버지의 기쁨이 되고 싶습니다

2015년 12월 31일, 송구영신예배 때였습니다. 목사님께서 새해 소원을 하나님께 말씀드리라고 하셨습니다. 그 순간 제 입에서 뜻밖의 기도가 나왔습니다. “하나님, 저 하나님 아버지의 기쁨이 되고 싶어요.” 당시 제게 가장 절실한 문제는 빚을 갚는 일이었습니다. 그런데 저는 빚을 해결해 달라고 기도하지 않고, 하나님의 기쁨이 되고 싶다고 고백했습니다.

더 놀라운 것은 제가 하나님을 자연스럽게 ‘아버지’라고 불렀다는 사실입니다. 어린 시절 아버지에게 받은 상처 때문에 아버지라는 말조차 편안하지 않았습니다. 그런데 하나님을 사랑하는 아버지로 부르고 있었습니다.

저는 그것이 성령님께서 제 마음에 주신 소원이라고 믿었습니다. 그때부터 예배를 회복하고 말씀을 가까이하기 시작했습니다.

이사야 55장 3절 말씀처럼 하나님께 귀를 기울이고 나아갈 때, 영혼이 살아나는 것을 경험했습니다. 경제적 문제가 해결되는 것보다, 하나님과의 관계가 회복되는 것이 먼저라는 사실을 깨달았습니다.

저는 다시 하나님께 제 삶을 드리고 싶었습니다. 의료선교의 꿈도 떠올랐습니다. 그러나 하나님께서는 제가 생각하지 못한 길을 준비하고 계셨습니다.

하나님께서는 제게 새로운 만남을 허락하셨습니다. 아내와 사별한 목사님을 만나게 된 것입니다. 저는 재혼을 앞두고도 마음이 복잡했습니다. 남아 있는 빚이 있었고, 목회자의 아내로 살아갈 자신도 없었습니다.

그래서 하나님께 기도했습니다. 결혼이 경제적 문제를 해결하기 위한 수단이 되지 않도록 남은 채무를 정리할 길을 열어 달라고 구했습니다.

그 과정에서 예상하지 못한 도움을 받았습니다. 4천만 원을 지원받아 남아 있던 빚을 해결할 수 있었습니다. 저는 하나님께서 제 삶을 얼마나 세밀하게 돌보고 계신지 깨달았습니다.

2016년 12월 30일, 저희는 결혼했습니다. 그러나 사모가 되었다고, 오래된 죄책감이 모두 사라진 것은 아니었습니다.

결혼한 지 약 7개월이 지났을 때, 남편에게 갑작스러운 청력 문제가 생겼습니다. 양쪽 귀로 소리를 듣기 어려워졌습니다. 남편을 병원에 데려가던 날, 차 안에서 잠든 남편을 바라보다 이런 생각이 들었습니다. ‘이 사람이 나를 만나지 않았다면 어쩔 뻔했을까?’ 그러나 곧 제 자신을 향한 부정적인 생각이 밀려왔습니다. 그 순간 제 마음에 다른 말씀이 들렸습니다. “너라서. 네가 가장 잘할 수 있어서.”

저는 그 말씀 앞에서 울었습니다. 오랫동안 제 자신을 정죄했지만, 하나님께서는 부족한 저를 사용하고 계셨습니다. 저희 부부는 남편의 청력 회복을 위해 기도했습니다. “하나님, 사람의 말을 잘 듣지 못하더라도 하나님의 음성은 가장 잘 듣는 목회자가 되게 해 주세요.”

이후 남편은 양쪽 귀에 인공와우 수술을 받았고, 청력이 크게 회복되는 은혜를 경험했습니다

2026但以理祷告会第12天见证 即使浑身是血，也要活着 导师：王妃（平泽同心教会） 文本：以西结书 16:6

1. 等了四十年的神

亲爱的信徒们，我将一切荣耀归给神，因为他让我今天站在这里。当我写感恩日记的时候，我发现已经是777天了。我站在这里，期待神今天会给我什么样的恩典。我祷告了九年，因为我想把神在我生命中所做的一切写在书上。当出版之路终于打开时，我问上帝。 “上帝啊，我为什么要写一本关于我所取得的成就的书？”

当时我心里就听到了这句话。 “你为什么想写你所取得的成就？

“写下我为你做了什么。”他给了我另一种认识。 “你等了九年？我等了你四十年。”

我以为我等了一本书等了9年，但上帝等了我40年才完全回来。即使当我试图离开神、放弃自己时，神也没有放过我。我今天的见证不是关于我所成就的事，而是关于神如何拯救我。小时候，我曾长期受到酗酒父亲的性虐待。我在家里受到了深深的伤害，那里本应该是我最安全的地方，但我不能告诉任何人。我不忍心告诉母亲，她因为抚养七个兄弟姐妹而疲惫不堪。

虽然我出生在一个佛教家庭，但我八岁时就和姐姐一起去教堂。后来，我在一次静修中与神有了深刻的接触，并梦想成为一名医疗布道士。我追随这个梦想进入了护士学校。然而，过宗教生活并没有自动让我童年的创伤消失。我的心里还残留着一种羞耻感和自卑感。我鼓起勇气在教堂分享我的痛苦，但当这个故事被其他人知道时，我更加受伤。我的抑郁症加深了，23岁时，我第一次尝试放弃自己的生活。那一刻，我的口中发出了祈祷声。 “上帝，我想活下去。如果你现在救我，我愿意为你献出我的生命。”

我向母亲求助才得以幸存。

然而，活下来并不代表我内心的伤口就痊愈了。我当时并不知道。上帝拯救我是有原因的，还有一个故事还没有结束。 2.在绝望的尽头听到的生命之言

在首尔国立大学医院担任护士期间，我遇到了一个爱我的人并结婚了。我的丈夫不相信耶稣，我的姻亲也不希望我婚后去教堂。我接受了请求并离开了礼拜仪式。然而，我们结婚六年后，我 32 岁的丈夫被诊断出患有晚期结肠癌。在与病魔抗争的过程中，我丈夫信了耶稣并受了洗。我期待上帝医治我的丈夫，但他最终去世了。

36岁那年，我成为了一位抚养两个孩子的单亲妈妈。悲伤还没散去，我丈夫的身故保险金和信用贷款钱就被看了广播后接近我的骗子拿走了。损失达2亿多韩元。由于失去丈夫的悲痛加上经济上的绝望，我不再有生活的信心。正当我准备第二次放弃生活时，电话响了。他是一名经常参加清晨祈祷的大三学生。我接起电话，本想作最后的告别，师弟却突然开口了。 “姐姐，你为什么想死？”

如果我不告诉任何人我怎么知道？我很震惊，停下了手上的事情。后来，我向妈妈求助，告诉她我一直隐瞒的欺骗和痛苦。

后来我发现更令人惊讶的事情。在我想到死亡的那一天，有几个人为我代求。我以为我是孤独一人，但事实并非如此。当我连祷告的力气都没有的时候，神就借着别人的祷告来支持我。尽管第二次危机已经结束，但债务和萧条仍在继续。虽然搬到了平泽，但心里的痛苦并没有消失。我在外面笑了，但当我独自一人时，绝望淹没了我。 2014年，我第三次想到死亡。我再也找不到活下去的理由了。神当时赐给我心的话就是以西结书16:6。 “即使浑身是血，也要活下去。”读这些话时我哭了。

上帝并没有告诉我们在来之前解决所有的伤口。他没有说洁净了就可以活了。他满身是血地告诉我，要像我一样活下去。就好像上帝如此爱我，他告诉我要活下去，不要死。那天并没有消除债务或解决问题。但现在我有了活下去的理由。我坚持着这句话，度过了每一天。我又活了一天。我只看到我的生命沾满了鲜血，但神仍然爱我。正是这份爱让我重获新生。 3. 我想成为天父上帝的喜乐

那是2015年12月31日，松谷永信仪式期间。

2026 다니엘기도회 11일차 간증 육신의 생각과 영의 생각 강사: 한영호 목사(나눔선교회 대표) 본문: 로마서 8장 5–11절 중심 말씀: 로마서 8장 6절 “육신의 생각은 사망이요 영의 생각은 생명과 평안이니라.”

1. 저는 22년 동안 마약 중독자로 살았습니다

사랑하는 성도 여러분!

저는 여러분 앞에 훌륭한 목사로 서 있는 사람이 아닙니다. 저는 22년 동안 마약 중독자로 살았던 사람입니다. 마약을 사용했을 뿐 아니라 직접 만들어 팔기도 했습니다. 마약을 팔면서 많은 돈을 벌었고, 조직에 몸담아 살아왔습니다. 남들보다 잘나 보이고 싶었고, 가진 것을 자랑하고 싶었습니다. 제 인생의 중심에는 언제나 제가 있었습니다.

사람들은 저에게 묻습니다. “목사님, 왜 마약을 하셨습니까?” 저는 솔직하게 대답합니다. 좋아서 했습니다. 마약이 좋았기 때문에 22년 동안 빠져 살았습니다. 물론 끊고 싶은 마음도 있었지만, 마음 한편에는 여전히 마약을 원하는 욕망이 자리 잡고 있었습니다.

이것이 중독의 무서움입니다. 머리로는 잘못이라는 사실을 알면서도, 그 행동을 반복합니다. 그만두고 싶지만 그만둘 힘이 없습니다. 스스로 통제할 수 있다고 생각하지만 어느 순간 다시 끌려갑니다.

저는 기독교인들을 무척 싫어했습니다. 미국 로스앤젤레스에서 제게 마약을 사러 오는 사람들 가운데 교회에 다니는 사람들이 많았습니다. 저는 그들에게 물었습니다. “당신들은 하나님을 믿는다면서 왜 마약을 합니까?”

저는 하나님을 믿지 않았습니다. 아니, 제 자신조차 믿지 못했습니다. 나 자신도 믿을 수 없는데 어떻게 보이지 않는 하나님을 믿겠습니까?

그런 제가 지금 여러분 앞에서 하나님 말씀을 전하고 있습니다. 제가 목사가 될 것이라고는 단 한 번도 생각해 본 적이 없습니다. 하나님께서는 제가 상상하지 못했던 인생을 살게 하셨습니다.

오늘 본문은 육신을 따르는 사람은 육신의 일을 생각하고, 영을 따르는 사람은 영의 일을 생각한다고 말씀합니다. 저는 육신의 욕망을 따라 살았던 사람이었습니다. 돈과 쾌락과 자기 자랑이 제 삶의 목적이었습니다. 그러나 그 끝에는 생명이 아니라 죽음이 기다리고 있었습니다.

2. 죽음의 자리에서 살아 계신 하나님을 만났습니다

저는 조직 생활을 하면서 많은 위험을 겪었습니다. 폭력 속에서 살아왔고, 몸에는 지금도 그 흔적들이 남아 있습니다. 죽음에 이를 만큼 끔찍한 일을 경험하기도 했습니다.

그 과정에서 저는 죽어 있는 제 육신을 바라보는 것과 같은 놀라운 체험을 했습니다. 어떻게 설명해야 할지 모르겠습니다. 분명히 죽었다고 생각했는데, 다시 눈을 떠 보니 살아 있었습니다. 그때 저는 지금까지 살아온 인생을 돌아보게 되었습니다. 제가 믿었던 돈도, 힘도, 조직도, 제 자신도 결국 저를 구원할 수 없다는 사실을 깨달았습니다.

어느 날 샤워실에서 하나님께 기도했습니다. “하나님, 당신이 정말 살아 계신다면 저에게 한 가지만 해 주십시오. 다시는 마약을 하지 않게 해 주십시오. 그렇게 해 주신다면 제 인생을 당신께 바치겠습니다.”

그때 저는 신앙생활을 제대로 알지도 못했습니다. 성경을 공부한 사람도 아니었습니다. 그런데 제 마음속에 ‘사도행전’이라는 말이 강하게 떠올랐습니다. 평생 제대로 들어본 적도 없는 말이었습니다.

그 체험 이후 세상이 완전히 다르게 보이기 시작했습니다. 모텔 방문을 열고 밖으로 나왔는데, 하늘이 그렇게 아름다울 수 없었습니다. 나무도 아름다웠고 작은 개미조차 사랑스럽게 보였습니다.

저는 원래 개미를 싫어했습니다. 개미가 보이면 죽여 버리던 사람이었습니다. 그런데 그 작은 생명조차 소중하게 느껴졌습니다. 길거리에서 노숙인을 만났을 때도 이전과는 다른 마음이 생겼습니다. 그 사람을 위해 기도하고 싶었습니다.

제가 달라진 것은 단순히 마약을 하지 않게 되었다는 사실만이 아닙니다. 세상을 바라보는 눈이 달라졌습니다. 사람을 대하는 태도가 달라졌습니다. 무엇이 소중한 것인지 깨닫게 되었습니다.

하나님의 영이 제 안에 들어오시면서 삶의 방향이 바뀐 것입니다. 저는 천국이 단지 죽어서 가는 장소만은 아니라고 생각합니다. 살아 계신 하나님께서 우리와 함께하시는 곳에서 우리는 천국의 기쁨을 경험할 수 있습니다. 저 같은 마약 중독자가 변화되어 목사가 된 것은 전적으로 하나님의 은혜입니다.

3. 신앙은 말이 아니라 삶으로 증명하는 것입니다

저는 거룩한 척 하는 목사가 되고 싶지 않습니다. 사람들에게 훌륭하게 보이는 목사도 되고 싶지 않습니다. 저는 인간다운 목사, 정직한 목사, 솔직한 목사가 되고 싶습니다.

사람들은 목사에게 학력을 묻습니다. 어느 학교를 졸업했고, 어디에서 석사와 박사학위를 받았는지 궁금해합니다.

저는 한국에서 중학교 1학년 때 퇴학당했습니다. 마약 중독자로 살았고 감옥에도 드나들었습니다. 미국에서 고등학교를 졸업하고 이후 신학을 공부했지만, 그것이 제 인생에서 가장 중요한 이야기는 아닙니다.

어느 교회에서 이력서를 보내 달라고 해서 제 과거를 그대로 적어 보냈습니다. 중학교 퇴학, 마약 중독, 감옥 생활까지 기록했습니다. 그러자 이것이 무슨 이력서냐는 반응이 돌아왔습니다. 나중에 학력과 학위까지 정리해 보냈더니 왜 처음부터 그렇게 보내지 않았느냐고 했습니다.

저는 묻고 싶었습니다. “제가 지금 여러분 앞에서 학위를 설교하고 있습니까? 저는 살아 계신 하나님을 만난 이야기를 전하고 있습니다.”

신앙에서 중요한 것은 겉으로 드러나는 자격만이 아닙니다. 그 사람이 실제로 어떤 삶을 살아가느냐는 것입니다.

저는 나눔선교회에서 중독자들과 함께 생활합니다. 그들과 먹고 자며 하루 24시간을 함께 보냅니다. 함께 살아보면 금방 알게 됩니다. 말로는 얼마든지 거룩한 척할 수 있지만, 생활에서는 숨길 수 없습니다. 제가 하는 말과 행동을 원생들이 모두 지켜봅니다.

설교 시간에 사랑을 말하면서 생활에서는 사랑하지 않는다면, 그들은 금방 알아차립니다. 정직을 가르치면서 제가 거짓말을 한다면, 누가 제 말을 믿겠습니까?

저는 원생들에게 신앙생활을 무조건 열심히 하라고 가르치지 않습니다. 사랑을 실천하라고 말합니다. 믿음은 하나님 은혜로 주어지는 것입니다. 그 은혜를 받은 사람이라면 이웃을 사랑해야 합니다.

교회에서 찬양을 잘하는 것도 중요합니다. 기도를 열심히 하는 것도 중요합니다. 그러나 예배당 문을 나선 이후의 삶이 더욱 중요합니다. 참된 신앙은 예배당에서만 나타나는 것이 아니라 일상생활 속에서 증명되어야 합니다.

4. 중독자들을 변화시키려다, 오히려 제가 변화되었습니다

저는 나눔선교회를 30년 동안 섬겨 왔습니다. 현재 약 40명의 원생이 함께 숙식하며 생활하고 있습니다. 그동안 약 1,200명의 중독자가 이곳을 거쳐 변화의 과정을 경험했습니다.

처음 이 사역을 시작할 때는 중독자들을 돕고 싶었습니다. 저처럼 고통받는 사람들과 함께하고 싶었습니다.

저는 중독자를 무조건 가르치거나 통제하려는 사람이 되고 싶지 않았습니다. 저 역시 누군가가 저를 억지로 변화시키려고 하면 강하게 저항하던 사람이었습니다.

제게 필요했던 것은 저를 정죄하는 사람이 아니라, 제 곁에서 함께 걸어주는 사람이었습니다. 예수님께서 우리에게 오셔서 친구가 되어 주셨듯이 저도 그들에게 친구가 되어 주고 싶었습니다.

그런데 30년을 함께 살아보니, 놀라운 사실을 깨달았습니다. 제가 그들을 변화시킨 것이 아니었습니다. 오히려 그들이 저를 변화시키고 있었습니다.

저는 원생들과 함께 살면서 정직을 배웠습니다. 인내를 배웠습니다. 사랑이 무엇인지 배웠습니다. 저들이 있었기에 제가 지금까지 마약을 하지 않고 살아올 수 있었다고 생각합니다.

목사가 성도들에게 은혜를 주기만 하는 것이 아닙니다. 성도들도 목사에게 은혜를 줍니다. 우리는 서로를 통해 배우고 성장합니다.

저는 나눔선교회가 원생들만을 위해 세워진 곳이라고 생각하지 않습니다. 하나님께서 저를 위해 세워주신 공동체라고 믿습니다. 그곳에서 저는 매일 제 자신을 돌아봅니다. 아침에 일어나면 이렇게 기도합니다. “하나님, 오늘도 제 자신에게 속지 않게 해 주십시오.”

저는 제 자신을 너무 잘 압니다. 제 생각과 욕망을 의지하는 순간 다시 문제가 시작될 수 있다는 사실을
featured.content_zh:
2026 但以理祷告会第 11 天见证 肉体的意念和圣灵的意念 导师：韩英浩牧师（分享宣教首席执行官） 文本：罗马书 8:5-11 关键信息：罗马书 8:6 “因为体贴肉体的就是死，体贴圣灵的就是生命平安。”

1.我吸毒了22年

亲爱的信徒们！我并不是以一个伟大的牧师的身份站在你们面前。我吸毒已有 22 年了。他们不仅使用毒品，还制造并出售毒品。我靠卖毒品赚了很多钱，并以组织成员的身份生活。我想看起来比别人更好并炫耀我所拥有的。我一直是我生活的中心。人们问我。

“牧师，你为什么吸毒？”我如实回答。我这样做是因为我喜欢它。我喜欢毒品，所以我沉迷了22年。当然，我想戒掉，但我的一部分仍然有吸毒的欲望。这就是对成瘾的恐惧。即使我们心里知道这是错误的，我们还是会重复这种行为。我想放弃，但我没有力气放弃。你以为你可以控制它，但在某些时候你又被拖了回去。我真的很讨厌基督徒。在洛杉矶来向我购买毒品的人中，有很多人去教堂。我问他们。 “你说你信上帝，但你为什么要吸毒？”

我不相信上帝。不，连我自己都不相信。

当我不能相信自己时，我怎么能相信一位看不见的上帝呢？我现在正在你们面前宣讲神的话语。我从来没有想过我会成为一名牧师。上帝给了我一个我无法想象的生活。今天的经文说，随从肉体的人，思念肉体的事；随从圣灵的人，思念圣灵的事。我是一个随从肉体欲望而活的人。金钱、快乐和自豪是我一生的目标。但最终等待的不是生，而是死。 2.我在死亡现场遇见了永生神

我在组织工作时面临很多风险。我经历过暴力，暴力的痕迹仍然留在我的身上。

我经历过一些非常可怕的事情，几乎导致了死亡。在这个过程中，我有一种奇妙的体验，就像看着我的尸体一样。我不知道该如何解释。我以为我死了，但当我再次睁开眼睛时，我还活着。那时，我回顾了迄今为止的生活。我意识到，到最后，我所相信的金钱、权力、组织、我自己都救不了我。有一天，我在洗澡时向上帝祈祷。 “上帝，如果你还活着，请为我做一件事：永远不要再吸毒。如果你这样做，我就把我的生命交给你。”

那时我连宗教生活都不太了解。他不是一个研究圣经的人。

但“使徒行传”这个词强烈地浮现在我的脑海里。这是我一生中从未真正听到过的事情。那次经历之后，世界开始看起来完全不同了。当我打开汽车旅馆的门出来时，天空从未如此美丽。树很漂亮，就连小蚂蚁也看起来很可爱。我原本讨厌蚂蚁。他是一个见蚂蚁就杀的人。但即使是这样的小生命也让人感到珍贵。即使当我在街上遇到一个无家可归的人时，我的感觉也与以前不同。我想为那个人祈祷。对我来说，改变的不仅仅是我不再吸毒。我看待世界的方式已经改变。我对人的态度发生了变化。我意识到什么是珍贵的。

当神的灵进入我里面时，我生命的方向就改变了。我相信天堂不仅仅是你死后去的地方。我们可以体验永生神与我们同在的天堂的喜乐。像我这样的吸毒者能够改变并成为一名牧师，完全是神的恩典。 3. 信心不是用言语来证明，而是用生命来证明。

我不想成为一个假装圣洁的牧师。我不想成为一个在人们看来很棒的牧师。我想做一个人性化的牧师，一个诚实的牧师，一个诚实的牧师。人们向牧师询问他们的教育程度。我很好奇你是哪所学校毕业的，硕士和博士学位是在哪里获得的。我在韩国读初中一年级时被学校开除。

我像吸毒者一样生活，进出监狱。虽然我在美国高中毕业，后来又学习了神学，但这并不是我一生中最重要的故事。一个教会让我发简历，我就把我的过去写下来发给他们。他记录了被中学开除、吸毒甚至入狱的经历。然后回复问这是什么样的简历。后来我把我的学历和学位发给他，他问为什么一开始就不发给我。我想问。 “我现在正在向你讲道吗？我正在告诉你我与永生神的相遇的故事。”

信仰重要的不仅仅是外在的资格。这是关于这个人实际上过着什么样的生活。

featured.summary: Revd Beilieü Shüya (15.8.1928 to 18.9.2026), remembered as the first CRC woman to be ordained, passed away at the age of 98 in Kohima, leaving behind a remarkable legacy of Christian faith, missionary
featured.content: Revd Beilieü Shüya (15.8.1928 to 18.9.2026), remembered as the first CRC woman to be ordained, passed away at the age of 98 in Kohima, leaving behind a remarkable legacy of Christian faith, missionary commitment, education, and service. Her life was a testimony to perseverance, spiritual conviction, and obedience to the call of GOD, extending her influence beyond Nagaland into Arunachal Pradesh. The eldest of ten children of Lhousuohie Shüya and Zeno Dolie Shüya of Meriema village, she belonged to a family closely connected with the region’s Christian history. Her maternal grandfather was reportedly the second person from Khonoma village to embrace Christianity. Her mother was also the sister of Angami Zapu Phizo, the legendary Naga nationalist leader. An Exceptional Educational Journey Revd Shüya received her early education at Mission School, Kohima, before continuing her studies at Mission School, Golaghat, Government High School, Kohima, and Cotton College, Guwahati. She completed the first two years of her Bachelor of Arts degree at Scottish Church College, Calcutta, and her final year at Tribhuvan University, Nepal. Her academic achievements extended across several disciplines. She obtained a diploma from the International Montessori Association, Kolkata, completed a Perspective Course in Education at William Carey University, California, earned a Bachelor of Education degree from Utkal University, Bhubaneswar, and pursued a Master of Theology at Los Angeles University. She also earned a Master of Arts in Tenyidie from Ura Academy. Her educational background reflected a lifelong commitment to learning, teaching, and the development of people through knowledge and faith. A Life Transformed By The Holy Spirit A defining moment in her spiritual journey came in 1946, when she experienced what she described as the filling of the Holy Spirit. From then on, her life became increasingly devoted to Christian ministry rather than earthly popularity or recognition. In 1978, she was ordained at the World Mission Conference in Chennai, becoming the first CRC woman to receive ordination, according to accounts of her life. Her ordination represented a significant milestone for CRC women in Christian ministry and demonstrated her determination to serve despite the social and institutional challenges of her time. Her Christian convictions also brought hardship. She was imprisoned for her faith and reportedly imprisoned again in 1956 because of her family connection with A. Z. Phizo. During periods of imprisonment in Kohima, Nagaon, and Guwahati, she translated numerous passages of the Bible. Even confinement could not silence her commitment to GOD’S Word. featured.content: Après avoir été jugé apte à voyager, le pape Léon XIV s’apprête à effectuer son voyage apostolique en Amérique latine. Du 11 au 17 novembre, il retrouve le Pérou, pays auquel il est si profondément attaché et où il a passé de nombreuses années comme missionnaire, puis évêque de Chiclayo. C’est ici que Léon XIV, qui maîtrise déjà plusieurs langues, dont l’anglais, l’espagnol, l’italien et le français, aurait également appris le quechua, langue héritée de l’Empire inca. S’il ne l’a jamais parlée publiquement depuis le début de son pontificat, plusieurs témoignages confirment qu’il s’y est initié. Une promesse de l’entendre prochainement parler une nouvelle langue ? Dans un article publié par El País, un religieux augustin espagnol affirme que Robert Prevost a appris cette langue lors de son séjour missionnaire. Le cardinal Joseph Tobin, archevêque de Newark, a également confié à CNN que le nouveau Pape en avait acquis quelques rudiments. Plus révélateur encore, Janina Sesa, ancienne directrice de Caritas Tout lire… The post Léon XIV a-t-il vraiment appris à parler quechua ? appeared first on Aleteia .
featured.content_zh:
在被评估为适合出行后，利奥十四世教宗正准备前往拉丁美洲进行牧灵访问。11月11日至17日，他将重返秘鲁，这是他深爱着的国家，他曾在这里度过了许多年，先是作为传教士，后来成为奇克拉约主教。

利奥十四世已经掌握了多种语言，包括英语、西班牙语、意大利语和法语，据称他正是在这里学习了印加帝国传承下来的语言——克丘亚语。虽然自就任教宗以来，他从未在公开场合使用过这种语言，但多方证词证实他曾学习过这种语言。是否意味着我们很快就能听到他用一种新语言讲话？

在《国家报》发表的一篇文章中，一位西班牙奥古斯丁会修士表示，罗伯特·普雷沃斯特在传教期间学习了这种语言。纽瓦克大主教、枢机主教约瑟夫·托宾（Joseph Tobin）也向美国有线电视新闻网（CNN）透露，新任教宗已掌握了一些基础知识。

更具启发性的是，雅尼娜·塞萨（Janina Sesa），前明爱会主任 阅读全文…… 文章《利奥十四世真的学会了说克丘亚语吗？》最初发表于Aleteia。

featured.content:
2026년 11월 5일부터 13일까지 캄보디아에서는 ‘국가통합을 위한 스포츠’를 주제로 제5회 내셔널게임이 개최중이다. 2년마다 열리는 이번 대회중 유도 부문은 5일부터 8일까지 열렸다. 특히 유도 종목은 지난 5년간 대한민국 교계와 유도계의 지속적인 지원과 협력이 이어져 온 분야라는 점에서 그 주목을 받았다.

캄보디아 유도연맹에 따르면 유도 종목 종합 1위는 왕립군(Royal Cambodian Armed Forces) 팀이 차지했다. 왕립군은 금메달 5개, 은메달 1개, 동메달 1개를 획득하며 우수한 성적을 거뒀다.

이번 성과에는 캄보디아 유도연맹 소속으로 왕립군 선수들을 지도하는 쏙 다라(SOK DARA) 감독과 한국인 이승찬 코치의 지도를 받아 온 선수들의 활약이 있었다. 특히 두 지도자의 제자인 왕립군 소속 선수들이 전원 입상했다는 점에서 의미를 더했다.

올해로 5년째 캄보디아 유도선수들을 섬겨 온 이선교사는 이번 성과에 대해 캄보디아 유도연맹과 한국교회 및 유도계 관계자들의 지속적인 소통과 협력이 있었기에 가능했다고 밝혔다. 그는 “혼자 감당할 수 있는 사역이 아니었다”며 함께해 온 이들에게 감사를 전했다.

실제로 이번 성과의 배경에는 지난 한국 유도계의 물적·인적 지원이 있었다. 현 대한체육회 경기력향상위원장이자 한국마사회 유도 감독인 김재범 감독과 경기도유도회 이종명 전무는 캄보디아 유도계에 24년부터 물적자원을 지원해 왔다.

아울러 공식적인 지도자 파견 경로를 통해 대한유도회 4단을 보유한 이 선교사가 현지의 인적자원으로 쓰일 수 있도록 힘썼다.

캄보디아 유도연맹 차원의 지원도 이어졌다. 부회장 임마누엘 디아즈(EMMANUEL DIAS)와 총감독 마르 봉 비볼(MAR VONG VIBOL)은 이승찬 코치의 생활 여건과 활동 범위를 고려해 실질적인 지원 방안을 구축했다. 캄보디아 국립 올림픽 스타디움 내부에 숙소를 제공함으로써 주거 부담을 덜고 선수 지도와 외부사역에 집중할 수 있도록 했다.

이방인 선교사이자 유도 코치에게 훈련장 숙소를 제공한 일은 불교국가에서는 매우 이례적인 사례이다. 이러한 지원과 협력의 현장 소식을 접하게된 재캄보디아한인회 제15대 회장 임종원 당선인도 대회장을 방문하여 유도연맹 관계자들과 인사를 나누고 이 선교사를 격려했다.

이러한 활동 기반이 처음부터 마련되어 있었던 것은 전혀 아니었다. 정착 과정에서 언어와 문화의 장벽은 상당한 어려움이었다. 생계와 사역을 스스로 감당하는 자비량 선교사로서 크메르어를 익히고 현지 문화를 이해하는 일은 쉽지 않았다.

이때 도움을 준 이들이 유도의 형제 스포츠인 캄보디아 레슬링 팀이었다. 캄보디아 여자 레슬링 국가대표팀 코치 샘 소티아라는 과거 캄보디아에 파견됐던 남북한 레슬링 지도자들에게 도합 15년가까이 한국어로만 레슬링을 배운 경험을 바탕으로, 이 선교사가 현지에 도착한 2022년부터 크메르어 교육과 빠른 문화 적응을 위해 때로는 엄격한 훈육을 통해 현지의 생활 방식과 소통 문화를 익히도록 이끌어냈다.

이러한 경험들이모여 이승찬 코치의 지도 철학에도 영향을 주었다. 그의 훈련 방식은 다른 종목의 외국인 지도자들과 구별된다는 현지 관계자들의 평가를 받고 있다. 그는 연맹의 코치로서의 권한과 지위를 앞세우기보다는 맡은 임무와 책임을 먼저 다하는 데 집중해 왔다. 또한 삶에서 하루도 거르지 않고 선수들과 함께 땀 흘리는 루틴을 통해 그리스도인의 동행을 자연스럽게 드러내는 방식을 고수해 왔다.

이번 대회에서 주목받은 선수 가운데 한 명은 초빈(Cheeav Chovin)이다. 남자 유도 -55kg급에 출전한 그는 이 선교사가 사역 초기 껀달주 유도대표팀을 섬기던 시절부터 함께해 온 그리스도인 유도선수다. 5년간 이어진 사제 간의 동행 속에서 초빈 선수는 재작년 국가대표팀의 주력 선수이자 왕립군 소속 선수로 성장했다.

이번 우승을 계기로 초빈 선수는 캄보디아 왕립군 당국으로부터 군 계급과 정복을 부여받을 예정이다. 이에 따라 군인으로서 정기적인 급여를 받으며 생활할 수 있는 안정적인 기반도 마련될 것으로 기대된다.

이코치는 우승을 축하하고 격려하기 위해 초빈 선수에게 소정의 감사헌금을 전달했다. 선수에게 전달된 헌금은 포이에마예수교회(담임 김현섭 목사)와 대한체육회 경기력 향상 위원장 김재범(한국마사회 유도단) 감독, 경기도유도회 이종명 전무, 재캄보디아한인회 제15대 회장 임종원 당선인의 도움으로 마련됐다. 한국교회와 유도계, 재외 한인사회가 함께한 후원이 한 선수의 성장을 축복하는 자리로 이어진 것이다.

왕립군 유도선수들을 지도해 온 쏙 다라(SOK DARA) 감독은 이승찬 선교사에 대해 다음과 같이 말했다.

“우리 유도인들 중 그 누구도 한국인 유도 코치 LEE를 이방인이라고 생각하지 않습니다. 그는 우리 왕립군 선수들의 훈련자이자 가족입니다.”

지난 5년간 대한민국 교계와 유도계가 캄보디아 유도 현장에서 이어 온 스포츠 선교는 일회성 후원에 머물지 않았다. 현지 관계자들과 신뢰를 쌓고 선수들의 삶에 동행하는 과정이었다. 2026년 캄보디아 내셔널게임에서 나타난 성과는 그 과정이 맺은 하나의 결실이다.

국적과 언어가 다른 사람들이 유도를 매개로 협력하고, 그리스도인 선수는 자신의 재능을 발전시켜 군인으로서 자립할 수 있는 길을 마련했다는 점에서 더욱 의미가 깊다.
featured.content_zh:
第五届全运会于2026年11月5日至13日在柬埔寨举行，主题为“体育促进民族融合”。本届比赛每两年举办一次，柔道项目于第五届至第八届举行。尤其是柔道运动，是近五年来韩国宗教界和柔道界持续支持与合作的领域，备受关注。据柬埔寨柔道联合会称，柬埔寨皇家武装部队队在柔道比赛中获得总成绩第一名。皇家陆军表现出色，获得五枚金牌、一枚银牌和一枚铜牌。这一成绩是由柬埔寨柔道总会皇家陆军运动员教练SOK DARA和韩国教练李升灿执教的运动员取得的。

特别有意义的是，作为两位领导人的弟子的所有皇家军选手都获得了奖品。今年已经为柬埔寨柔道运动员服务五年的李传教士表示，这一成绩的取得得益于柬埔寨柔道总会、韩国教会以及柔道行业官员之间不断的沟通与合作。他对那些一直与他在一起的人表示感谢，并说：“这不是我一个人可以处理的事工。”事实上，这一成绩的背景是韩国柔道界的物质和人力支持。现任韩国体育理事会成绩提高委员会委员长、韩国赛马院柔道教练金在范教练和京畿道柔道协会常务理事李钟明24年来一直为柬埔寨柔道界提供物质资源。此外，还努力确保这位拥有韩国柔道协会四段的传教士能够通过官方领导人派遣渠道作为当地人力资源。

柬埔寨柔道联合会继续提供支持。副总裁EMMANUEL DIAS和总经理MAR VONG VIBOL考虑了李升灿教练的生活条件和活动范围，制定了切实可行的支持计划。通过在柬埔寨国家奥林匹克体育场内提供住宿，减轻了运动员的住房负担，让运动员能够专注于训练运动员和外事工作。为外国传教士和柔道教练提供训练营住宿在佛教国家是非常不寻常的案例。柬埔寨韩国人协会第15任会长林正元得知这一支持与合作的消息后也亲临会场，与柔道联合会官员互致问候，并对传教士表示鼓励。此类活动的基础从一开始就没有到位。

语言和文化障碍是定居过程中的重大困难。作为一名自给自足、照顾自己生计和事工的传教士，学习高棉语和了解当地文化并不容易。此时提供帮助的是柬埔寨摔跤队，它是柔道的兄弟运动。柬埔寨女子国家摔跤队教练萨姆·索蒂亚拉(Sam Sotiara)根据过去近15年派往柬埔寨的朝鲜和韩国摔跤领导人仅用韩语学习摔跤的经验。从2022年开始，当这些传教士到达该国时，他带领他们通过高棉语教育以及有时严格的纪律来学习当地的生活方式和交流文化，以快速适应文化。这些经历汇集在一起​​影响了李升灿教练的执教理念。

他的训练方法被当地官员评价为与其他运动项目的外籍教练不同。他并没有优先考虑自己作为足协教练的权威和地位，而是首先专注于履行自己的职责和责任。此外，他还保持着一种自然地展现基督徒陪伴的方式，通过与球员们一起挥汗如雨的例行公事，不缺席生活中的每一天。 Cheeav Chovin是本次比赛中备受关注的选手之一。他参加了男子柔道-55公斤级比赛，是一名基督教柔道运动员，自传教士李传道初期在坎达尔州柔道队服役时就一直跟随他。在神父们的五年陪伴中，肖万成长为国家队的主力球员，并于前年成为皇家陆军的一员。

凭借这次胜利，肖万有望获得柬埔寨皇家军事当局颁发的军衔和制服。因此，预计将为士兵在领取定期工资的同时建立稳定的生活基础。李教练向肖万致以小小的谢意，以祝贺和鼓励获胜者。送给运动员的礼物是在Poiema Jesus Church（金贤燮牧师）、韩国体育振兴会成绩提高会长金在范（韩国竞马协会柔道队）教练、京畿道柔道协会执行董事李钟明、柬埔寨韩国协会第15任候任会长林正元的帮助下准备的。韩国教会、柔道界和海外韩国人团体的共同支持，为运动员的成长提供了祝福的机会。曾担任皇家陆军柔道运动员教练的 SOK DARA 教练对传教士 Seungchan Lee 说道：

“我们柔道运动员都不认为韩国柔道教练李是局外人。他是我们皇家陆军运动员的教练和家庭成员。”

五年来，韩国教会和柔道界在柬埔寨柔道场开展的体育传教工作并没有停留在一次性赞助上。这是一个与当地官员建立信任并陪伴球员生活的过程。 2026 年柬埔寨全运会取得的成果就是这一进程的成果之一。更有意义的是，它为不同国籍、不同语言的人们通过柔道合作提供了一条途径，也为基督教运动员提供了一条发挥才能、独立成为军人的途径。

featured.title: 35 priests could not help her. In a church she saw Jesus crush what was choking her
featured.summary: 🇱🇰North Central Province· 2021
featured.summary_zh: 北中央省
featured.title_zh: 35位神父都无法帮助她。在教堂里，她看到耶稣粉碎了正在扼住她喉咙的东西。
featured.content: Chandra lived in a rural village in Sri Lanka's North Central Province, and she was slowly falling apart. Pain, weakness, a heart that raced for no reason doctors could name. She and her family were Hindu, so they did what they knew to do. They went to priest after priest. Thirty-five of them. Nothing changed. In July 2021 they walked into a church instead. As people prayed for her, Chandra saw something. Demons were trying to strangle her, and then Jesus Christ stepped in and stamped on them. She felt the pain and the sickness drain out of her body as they were defeated. In the vision Jesus spoke Scripture over her, from Psalm 34. "They looked to Him and were radiant," He said, and told her she would be radiant too if she trusted Him. The prayer a father prayed Her husband Dinesh, a day labourer, watched his wife come back to life and made God a promise. "God, if you will heal my wife, I will dedicate my daughter for your service." The whole family, who had barely heard the name of Jesus, gave their lives to Him. Their daughter Tenusha told her class what had happened, that her mother was free and that Jesus forgives sinners and makes them new. They did not keep it to themselves. A house church started in their home with four people. By now it is forty-six. Jesus is still stronger than whatever is choking the life out of you. He steps in, He stamps it down, and He calls you radiant.
featured.content_zh:
钱德拉住在斯里兰卡中北部省的一个乡村,她慢慢地分崩离析. 痛苦,软弱,一个无缘无故的心脏 医生无法命名 她和她的家人是印度教徒,所以他们做了他们知道的事。 他们跟随牧师去了牧师那里. 三十五门. 什么都没有改变。 2021年7月,他们走进了一座教堂。

当人们为她祈祷时,钱德拉看到了一些东西. 恶魔试图掐死她,然后耶稣基督介入并盖在他们身上. 她感到痛苦和疾病 排出她的身体 当他们被打败。 在视觉中,耶稣说圣经 超过她,从Psalm 34。 他说:他们崇拜他,而且赞颂他超绝万物。他说:她也超绝万物,如果她信任他。

一个父亲祈祷她的丈夫迪尼什(Dinesh),一个白天的劳工,看着他的妻子复活,并给上帝一个承诺. "上帝,如果你能治愈我的妻子, 我将奉献我的女儿为你服务。" 几乎听不到耶稣之名的全家都为他献出了生命.

他们的女儿特努沙告诉了班上所发生的事情,她的母亲是自由的,耶稣宽恕了罪人,使他们成为新人. 他们没有保守秘密。 一所房屋教堂在他们家中开始,共有4人. 时已四十六. 耶稣仍然比任何 扼杀你生命的东西更强大 他走进来,他把它印下来,他叫你光辉。

featured.title: A widow heard the good news from a travelling salesman and could not unhear it
featured.summary: Laos· 2022
featured.title_zh: 一位寡妇从一位推销员那里听到了好消息，从此念念不忘。
featured.content: Pei was a fifty-two-year-old widow in Laos, raised the way her whole village was raised, worshipping ancestors and local spirits in a place where the government pushes atheism and neighbours warn that following the God of foreigners will offend the gods of home. Then a salesman came through and, somewhere between selling his goods, told her about Jesus. Salvation as a gift, not a payment. Pei believed it. She let go of the ancestor worship she had carried her whole life and quietly followed Jesus instead. The cost at her own front door She was discipled in secret for four months, growing strong enough to speak. The first people she told were her daughter and her son-in-law, who happens to be a policeman. They did not celebrate. He threatened her, saying that if she did not stop believing in Jesus, they would report her, jail her, or throw her out. In June they made good on it, tossing her clothes into the yard and telling her to go live with the people who gave her this Jesus. She went. She did not go back. A widow with nothing chose Jesus over a roof, because she had found something no one could evict from her heart. Following Jesus is not always safe, but it is always worth it. What Pei found is worth more than what it cost her, and it is offered to you too.
featured.content_zh:
裴 was在老挝是一位52岁的寡妇,养大了整个村庄的养殖方式,在政府推崇无神论的地方崇拜祖先和地方灵灵,邻居警告说,追随外国人神会冒犯家乡神灵. 然后一个推销员走过来,在出售他的商品之间,告诉她耶稣的事. 救世是礼物,不是报酬

裴 believed信之. 她放弃了她毕生怀念的祖先的崇拜,悄悄地跟随耶稣. 在她自己的前门付出的代价 她被秘密地关了四个月, 变得足够强大,可以说话。 她告诉的第一个人是她的女儿和女婿,她们碰巧是一名警察。 他们没有庆祝。

他威胁她,说如果她不停止相信耶稣,他们会告发她,监禁她,或者把她赶出去. 6月,他们在上面做得很好,把她的衣服扔到院子里,并告诉她去和给她这个耶稣的人一起生活. 她去了 她去了吗? 她没有回去。 一个什么都没有的寡妇选择了耶稣 而不是一个屋顶, 因为她已经发现了一些没人能从她的心脏里赶走的东西。

追随耶稣并不总是安全的,但总是值得的. 裴氏发现的比付出的代价更值钱,也是献给你的.

featured.title: He found a Bible in a secondhand shop and thought he was the only Christian in Yemen
featured.summary: 🇾🇪Yemen· 2000s
featured.summary_zh: 🇾🇪也门·21世纪初
featured.title_zh: 他在一家二手商店里找到了一本圣经，以为自己是也门唯一的基督徒。
featured.content: Mohammad grew up in Yemen, in a conservative Muslim home, in a country with almost no visible church at all. About seventeen years ago he found a Bible in a secondhand shop. He took it home and read it in hiding, because being caught with it could cost him everything. What he read pulled him in, and he gave his life to Jesus. Then came a strange loneliness. "When I came to faith, I thought I was the only believer in Yemen," he said. "For a long time, I didn't know any other Yemeni Christians." He was never actually alone He was wrong about being alone, and God kept proving it. Mohammad and his wife Alima, who came to Jesus after reading the Gospels herself, had been unable to have children for seven years. They prayed, and the infertility ended. Once, in a car accident, Mohammad says he saw a white light in the shape of a cross. Slowly he found other Yemeni believers, received discipleship, and today helps lead a house church in one of the hardest places on earth to follow Jesus. The man who thought he was the only one is now helping build a family of them. If you feel like the only believer in your world, take heart. Jesus is already gathering people you have not met yet, and He has not left you on your own.
featured.content_zh:
默罕默德成长于也门,在一个保守的穆斯林家庭,在一个几乎完全没有可见教堂的国家. 大约十七年前,他在二手店里发现了一本圣经. 他带回家藏起来读,因为被抓到会损失一切. 他读到的东西把他拉进来 他把生命交给耶稣 然后出现了奇怪的孤独

"当我回到信仰中,我以为我是也门唯一的信徒,"他说. "很久以来,我不认识其他也门基督徒". 他从不孤单 他不该独自一人 上帝一直在证明 默罕默德和他的妻子阿利玛在亲自阅读福音书后来到耶稣身边,已经无法生育7年. 他们祈祷,不孕症结束。

有一次,在一次车祸中,默罕默德说看到十字架形状的白光. 他慢慢地找到了其他也门信徒,获得了门徒资格,今天帮助带领一所位于地球上最难的地方的房屋教堂追随耶稣. 认为自己是唯一一个的人 现在正在帮助他们建立一个家庭。 如果你觉得自己是世上唯一相信的人,请记住。

耶稣已经聚集了你们尚未认识的人,他没有离开你们。

featured.title: Karma said he had to earn heaven. At 17 he heard he could be forgiven
featured.summary: Rakiraki· 1990s
featured.summary_zh: 拉基拉基·1990年代
featured.title_zh: 因果报应说他必须修功德才能上天堂。17岁时，他听说自己可以得到宽恕。
featured.content: Simon Gounder was born into a strict Hindu family in Fiji. His great-grandfather had been shipped from India as a contract labourer after the British took the islands in 1874, and the family settled in a small village in the north of Viti Levu. Simon grew up inside a system with clear rules. "As a Hindu, we believed in karma," he said. "If you do good karma, you get to heaven. If you do bad karma, you will be punished." It was a ledger he could never quite balance. He knew his own wrongs too well. The night the ledger closed At seventeen, a friend invited him to a Christian youth meeting in another town. There he heard something that did not fit anything he had been taught. That Jesus Christ could simply forgive sins. Not offset them, not average them out over lifetimes. Forgive them. Simon felt the weight of his own failures and, for the first time, an offer to be free of them. "I gave my life to Jesus that night," he said. He hid it from his parents at first. When they found out, they were not happy. But the son who came home changed did not stop there. In time he led his whole family to Christ, and he went on to plant a ministry that carries the same forgiveness to others. Karma keeps a running tab you can never clear. Jesus tears the tab up. Whatever you are carrying tonight, He is still in the business of forgiving it all at once.
featured.content_zh:
西蒙·古德出生于斐济一个严格的印度教家庭. 他的曾祖父在1874年英国人攻占群岛后,作为合同工从印度被运走,全家定居在维提莱武北部的一个小村庄. 西蒙在一个有明确规则的系统中长大. "作为一个印度教徒,我们相信因果报应,"他说. "若作善因缘即得上天.

若作恶报果报果报果. " 这是他无法平衡的分类账 他对自己的错误太了解了 结账的那一晚 17岁时,一位朋友邀请他到另一个城镇的一次基督教青年会议. 在那里,他听到一些不符合他所教过的东西。 耶稣基督可以宽恕罪过

不抵消它们, 也不平均出一生。 原谅他们 西蒙感受到了自己失败的轻重,并首次提出摆脱这些失败. "当晚我把生命交给耶稣,"他说. 起初他瞒着父母 当他们发现, 他们不高兴。 但回家的儿子变了 并没有停下来。

时他带领全家来到基督身边,他继续栽培一个对别人同样怀有宽恕的部. 卡玛一直有追踪器 你永远无法清除 耶稣撕开标签。 无论你今晚携带什么 他现在仍然要马上原谅这一切

featured.title: A soldier who should have died in battle walked into a demon's shrine
featured.summary: 🇲🇲Myanmar· 2010s
featured.title_zh: 一名本应死于战斗的士兵走进了恶魔的神殿
featured.content: Pastor Dano was a soldier before he was a pastor. He came out of the battlefield alive when he had no reason to, and he never shook the sense of why. "I believe God preserved my life from death on the battlefield for a purpose," he said. The purpose showed up in a Buddhist village that wanted nothing to do with him. The vice chief's son was tormented, demon-possessed, and no one could help. Dano fasted and prayed for three days. Then, near midnight, he went to the shrine where the boy was and did the only thing he knew to do. "I called upon the name of the Lord," he said, "and the demon left the young man." The night the shrines fell silent Villagers said every evil spirit left the village at once. Dano went from shrine to shrine, praying against the darkness that had ruled the place for generations. The vice chief's family, who had braced for his anger, found grace instead. They gave their lives to Jesus, and four more families followed. The people who once opposed him now follow his lead. There is a church in that village today where there used to be shrines. The name of Jesus is still stronger than every dark thing that has ever frightened you. One believer, praying at midnight, was enough to set a whole village free.
featured.content_zh:
牧师达诺在担任牧师之前是一名军人. 他毫无理由地活着走出战场,从未动摇过为什么的感官. "我相信上帝为了某种目的在战场上拯救了我的生命". 宗旨现于一佛村中欲与他无相. 副宰相的儿子被折磨,妖魔吞噬,无人能助.

达诺斋戒祈祷三天. 然后,近午夜,他去了男孩所在的神殿,做了他唯一知道该做的事. "我呼唤天主之名,"他说:"妖魔离开了少年. 夜神社失声村民说 每一个邪恶的灵魂 立刻离开村庄

达诺从神社到神社,祈祷反抗历代统治这个地方的黑暗. 副局长的家族,他为愤怒而坚韧不拔,却找到了恩典。 他们把生命献给了耶稣,还有四个家庭随行. 曾经反对他的人现在遵循他的路线。 今天村里有一座教堂 曾经有神社

耶稣的名字仍然比每件令你害怕的黑暗事物更强大. 一个信徒在午夜祈祷 足以让整个村庄自由

featured.title: You can kill me, but you cannot take my faith in Jesus
featured.summary: 🇧🇩Bangladesh· 2021-2022
featured.title_zh: 你可以杀了我，但你不能夺走我对耶稣的信仰
featured.content: Nur Alam and Afzal Hosen left Islam to follow Jesus in 2021, and they were baptised soon after. They did not keep it quiet. They wanted the Muslim community they came from to know the Jesus they had found, so they handed out Bibles and booklets around their part of Bangladesh. That is when the trouble started. A group seized Nur and locked him in a room for thirty hours, no food, no water, no sleep, demanding he return to Islam and threatening to kill him and his family. He would not bend. "At some point during the interrogation," Nur said, "they became hopeless, seeing my strong faith in Jesus." A faith they could not confiscate Days after Nur was freed, they came for Afzal. They beat him and accused him of being paid to convert. His answer has the ring of the early church about it. "You can kill me," he told them, "but you cannot take my faith in the Lord Jesus away from me." Both men were released, bruised and exhausted and still standing. They had discovered the thing every threat runs into eventually. You can take a man's freedom, his comfort, even his life, but the faith Jesus plants in a heart is not yours to seize. If Jesus is worth that to two young men in Bangladesh, He is worth your whole life too.
featured.content_zh:
努尔·阿拉姆(Nur Alam)和阿夫扎尔·霍森(Afzal Hosen)于2021年离开伊斯兰教跟随耶稣,他们不久就接受了洗礼. 他们没有保持沉默。 他们希望来自他们的穆斯林社区了解他们找到的耶稣,于是他们散发了他们所在的孟加拉国地区的圣经和小册子. 这就是问题开始的时候。

一群人抓住努尔,把他锁在一个房间里30小时,没有食物,没有水,没有睡眠,要求他返回伊斯兰教,并威胁要杀死他和他的家人. 他不会弯腰的 "在审讯期间的某个时候,"努尔说:"他们变得无望,看到我对耶稣的强烈信仰". 努尔解放后,他们无法没收信仰,他们来到阿夫扎尔。

他们殴打他,并指控他被收钱皈依。 他的答案是早期教会的戒指 他对他们说:你们可以杀我,但你们不能夺走我对主耶稣的信仰。 两人被释放,伤痕累累,仍然站立. 他们发现了每个威胁最终都遇到的东西

你可以拿一个人的自由,他的舒适,甚至他的生命, 但是信仰耶稣植根于一个心脏 不是你的夺取。 如果耶稣对孟加拉国的两个年轻人来说是值得的,那么他也值得你一辈子。

featured.title: Her church offering came to the exact amount of her power bill, to the penny
featured.summary: 🇺🇸United States· 2020s
featured.title_zh: 她的教会奉献金刚好等于她的电费，一分不差。
featured.content: Lina Johnson did not have enough to cover her power bill. She had told no one the amount. Not a friend, not her church, no one. It was her private worry, the kind you carry quietly and hope somehow resolves. That same week an offering came around at church for a family in need, and Lina gave what she could. Twenty-six cents. It was almost nothing, and she gave it anyway. Down to the penny The next day a friend told her the rest of the story. The offering the church had taken was for her. And when they counted it, it came to the exact amount of her power bill. To the penny. "The offering they took in church yesterday was for me," Lina said, "and it was the exact amount as my power bill. It was to the penny and I never told anyone how much my bill was." Here is the detail that undoes you. Had she given more than her twenty-six cents, the total would have overshot the bill, and the provision would have lost its edge. Even her small gift was part of God's arithmetic. God is not rounding up or guessing. He knew the number she never spoke aloud, and He met it precisely, through people who had no idea. The Father who counts the hairs on your head knows your bill too, down to the last penny.
featured.content_zh:
莉娜·约翰逊没有足够的钱来支付她的权力法案. 她没有告诉任何人这个数额。 不是朋友,也不是她的教堂,没有人 这是她的私人担忧, 你悄悄地携带的, 希望某种程度上解决。 在同一周,教堂里出现了一具供奉物,供奉一个有需要的家庭,莉娜尽了力. 26分钱. 几乎什么都没有,她还是给了它。

下到一分钱 第二天,一个朋友告诉她了其余的故事. 教堂的供奉是给她的 当他们数起来时, 她的权力法案的准确数额就到了。 至一分钱. "他们昨天在教堂里接受的献礼是给我的,"莉娜说,"这是确切的金额,就像我的权力法案.

我从来没有告诉任何人我的账单是多少". 这是让你难受的细节 如果她付出超过26美分,总额会超过法案,而规定会失去优势. 她的小礼物也是上帝算术的一部分 神不是围观或猜测。

他知道她从不大声说话的号码 他通过不知道的人 准确地认识了这个号码 算你头上头发的神父也知道你的帐单 一直到最后一分钱

featured.title: He was taught Christians do not pray. Then he watched his uncle pray before a meal
featured.title_zh: 他被教导说基督徒不祷告。然后，他看到叔叔在饭前祷告。
featured.content: Charles Yabaga Diarra grew up in a strict Muslim family in Lere, Mali, where Christians were mocked and misunderstood. His father, a headmaster and politician, ran the house like a school. As a boy, Charles fled about a hundred and fifty miles to stay with an uncle, and there he ran straight into something he had been told did not exist. His uncle, a Christian pastor, bowed his head and prayed before the meal. Charles was stunned. "Because we are Christians, we pray before meals," the uncle explained. Charles had been taught that Christians do not pray at all. That simple prayer, in his own language, lodged in him and would not leave. Just show me the way His father pulled him back and forced him into Quranic school, but the seed was planted. Years later, back with his uncle, tired and searching, Charles finally prayed his own prayer. "Lord, I'm really tired of seeking the truth. Just show me the way." A verse he had heard at a Vacation Bible School came back to him, and in November 1981 he gave his life to Jesus. The cost has been real. Charles is a preacher now, displaced by Mali's conflict and facing daily pressure. But he did not go alone. Of his fourteen siblings, most now follow Jesus, and around a hundred Christians gather at his extended family events. One uncle praying over dinner turned a whole family toward Jesus. Your quiet, ordinary faithfulness may be planting more than you know.
featured.content_zh:
查尔斯·亚巴加·迪亚拉(Charles Yabaga Diarra)在马里勒尔一个严格的穆斯林家庭长大,在那里基督徒受到嘲笑和误解. 他的父亲是一名校长和政治家,他像学校一样管理着房子. 童年时,查尔斯逃离了大约一百五十英里,与一个叔叔住在一起,在那里,他直接遇到了他被告知的东西并不存在.

他的叔叔,一位基督教牧师,低头祷告,在饭前祷告. 查尔斯被惊呆了 "因为我们是基督徒,我们吃饭前祈祷",叔叔解释道. 查尔斯被告知基督徒根本不祷告 用他自己的语言祈祷,他不会离开。

只要告诉我他父亲把他拉回来的方式 强迫他进入古兰经学校 但种子是种的 多年之后,与他的叔叔一起回来,疲惫和寻找,查尔斯终于自己祈祷. "主啊,我真的厌倦了寻找真相. "给我带路" 他在一所假期圣经学校听到的一首诗回到了他身边,1981年11月他把生命献给了耶稣.

代价是真实的。 查尔斯现在是一名传教士,因马里的冲突而流离失所,每天都面临压力。 但他没有一个人去。 他的十四个兄弟姐妹中,大多数现在都跟随耶稣,大约一百名基督徒聚集在他的大家庭活动中. 一个叔叔为晚餐祷告 整个家庭都向耶稣倾斜 你安静的,普通的忠诚 可能是种更多 比你知道。

featured.title: Kasih Tuhan Tiada Taranya
featured.summary_zh: p style="margin-bottom:1em; ">作者：Romauli br Marpaung Shalom，我叫 Romauli br Marpaung。
featured.title_zh: 上帝的爱是无与伦比的
featured.content: p style="margin-bottom:1em;">Oleh: Romauli br Marpaung Shalom, Nama saya Romauli br Marpaung. Saat ini, saya berusia 23 tahun. Saya berasal dari keluarga Kristen. Saya anak pertama dari lima bersaudara. Keluarga saya, dahulunya, bukan keluarga yang harmonis. Orang tua saya sering bertengkar. Namun, saat kelas IV SD, bapak saya bertobat sungguh-sungguh dan menyerahkan dirinya untuk diperlengkapi di Sekolah Alkitab Purbasari Pematang Siantar. Setelah selesai sekolah, beliau akhirnya diangkat menjadi seorang Pendeta, dan saya mulai pelayanan sejak kelas V SD di Gereja Kemuliaan Sion sebagai pemain musik tunggal. Pada 2013, saat saya lulus SMA, saya berharap bisa kuliah di Universitas Sumatera Utara (USU) Medan. Namun, saat mengikuti SBMPTN, saya gagal karena tidak lulus seleksi. Akhirnya, bapak saya mengusulkan supaya saya kuliah di Solo karena dia punya rekan pendeta yang anaknya kuliah di Solo juga. Saya mengikuti keinginan bapak saya karena beliau rindu saya bisa menjadi seorang hamba Tuhan. Akhirnya, saya kuliah di STT Berita Hidup, Solo, dan mengikuti semua kegiatan, aturan yang ada di kampus tersebut. Saya dibaptis saat duduk di bangku SMA kelas XI. Awalnya, saya kuliah di Berita Hidup karena orang tua dan pelarian, tetapi pada akhirnya saya bertobat dan percaya sungguh-sungguh kepada Tuhan Yesus saat kuliah semester 2. Pelayanan-pelayanan yang Tuhan percayakan kepada saya itu tidak mudah. Ada banyak masalah yang saya hadapi, baik itu dari asrama, tempat pelayanan, maupun kampus. Kalau bukan karena kekuatan Tuhan, mungkin saya tidak mampu. Namun, Tuhan Yesus baik, Dia memberi pertolongan saat saya benar-benar tidak mampu menjalaninya. Saya pelayanan di Gereja Bethel Tabernakel, Karanganyar. Saya mulai melayani di sana sejak Agustus 2014 sampai saat ini. Saya dipercaya untuk melayani di beberapa bagian, seperti melayani anak-anak sekolah minggu, pemuda/remaja, jemaat dewasa, maupun yang sudah lanjut usia. Selain itu, saya juga ambil bagian dalam musik, yaitu melatih anak-anak sekolah minggu belajar musik. Selain itu, saya juga diberi kesempatan oleh pendeta saya untuk membuka Bimbingan Belajar di Bibis Luhur Solo. Sewaktu kuliah, saya ditempatkan praktik tahunan di Gereja Kristus Rahmani Indonesia (GKRI), Jimbaran Bali. Tantangan yang saya hadapi adalah saya melayani orang-orang Kristen yang sudah berkeluarga, tetapi belum terikat dalam pernikahan. Saya juga membantu mengajar di PAUD Shinam, Jimbaran, milik gereja tersebut. Saya bersyukur untuk semua pelayanan yang telah dipercayakan gereja kepada saya. Saya bisa menjalani semua ini dengan pertolongan Tuhan. Yang saya rindukan dalam pelayanan adalah saya bisa memberikan yang terbaik untuk Tuhan dan gereja, menjadi berkat bagi banyak orang, dan tetap setia terhadap panggilan Tuhan. Saya juga rindu suatu saat saya bisa membuka pelayanan sendiri. Saya tahu itu tidak mudah, tetapi saya percaya kuasa pertolongan Tuhan nyata bagi saya. Kiranya kesaksian ini bisa menjadi berkat bagi semua orang, dan saya rindu kita tetap percaya bahwa segala sesuatu yang kita lakukan untuk Tuhan tidak akan kembali dengan sia-sia, melainkan Dia akan memberkati kita senantiasa (Kolose 3:23). Mulailah mengatakan bahwa pelayanan itu adalah sebuah kehormatan, bukan beban. Tuhan Yesus memberkati. "Dan, Maria berkata, "Sesungguhnya, aku ini hamba Tuhan. Terjadilah padaku seperti yang engkau katakan itu." Kemudian, malaikat itu pergi meninggalkannya."(Lukas 1:38, AYT)

p style="margin-bottom:1em;">作者：Romauli br Marpaung Shalom，我叫 Romauli br Marpaung。我今年 23 岁。我来自一个基督徒家庭。我是五个兄弟姐妹中的老大。我的家庭以前并不和谐。我的父母经常吵架。

然而，当我上小学四年级时，我父亲真心悔改，并前往位于Pematang Siantar的Purbasari圣经学校接受装备。毕业后，他最终被任命为牧师，而我从小学五年级开始就在锡安荣耀教会担任独奏乐手。

2013 年，当我高中毕业时，我希望能在棉兰的北苏门答腊大学 (USU) 上大学。然而，在参加全国统一高考（SBMPTN）时，我因为没有通过选拔而落榜了。最后，我父亲建议我去梭罗上大学，因为他有一位牧师朋友，他的孩子也在梭罗上大学。我听从了父亲的意愿，因为他希望我能成为神的仆人。

最后，我在梭罗的生命福音神学院（STT Berita Hidup）上学，并参加了该校的所有活动，遵守了该校的所有规定。我在读高一的时候受洗。起初，我因为父母和逃避现实的原因而就读于生命信息神学院，但最终我在第二学期时悔改并真心信靠主耶稣。

神托付给我的服侍并不容易。我面临着很多问题，无论是来自宿舍、事工场所还是校园。如果不是因为上帝的力量，我可能无法做到。然而，主耶稣是良善的，当我已经实在无法承受时，祂会伸出援手。我在卡朗亚尔的伯特利会幕教会（Gereja Bethel Tabernakel）服侍。

我从 2014 年 8 月开始在那里服侍，至今仍在继续。我受托在几个部门服侍，例如服侍主日学儿童、青年/青少年、成年会众以及老年人。此外，我还参与音乐方面的工作，即指导主日学儿童学习音乐。

此外，我的牧师还给了我机会，在梭罗的Bibis Luhur开设学习辅导班。在大学期间，我被安排在巴厘岛金巴兰的印度尼西亚基督慈悲教会（GKRI）进行年度实习。我面临的挑战是我要服侍那些已经有家庭但尚未缔结婚姻的基督徒。

我还协助在属于该教会的金巴兰 Shinam 幼儿教育中心（PAUD Shinam）进行教学。我感谢教会将所有这些事工托付给我。在神的帮助下，我能够做到这一切。我在侍奉中渴望的是，我能够为上帝和教会尽我所能，成为许多人的祝福，并始终忠于上帝的呼召。

我也希望有一天我能自己开办一间教会。我知道这并不容易，但我相信上帝的帮助对我来说是真实的。愿这个见证能成为所有人的祝福，我希望我们能继续相信，我们为神所做的一切都不会徒劳无功，祂必会永远赐福于我们（歌罗西书 3:23）。

开始说服自己，服侍是一种荣誉，而不是一种负担。愿主耶稣赐福。 “马利亚说：‘我是主的使女。愿照你的话成就在我身上。” 天使就离开她去了。”（路加福音 1:38，AYT）

featured.title_zh: 我是古利奈人西门。
featured.content: Aku Simon dari Kirene. Namaku menunjukkan bahwa aku tinggal di benua Afrika. Meski demikian, kulitku tidak hitam dan bibirku pun tidak tebal. Dan meskipun sudah selama beberapa generasi keluargaku berdiam di Kirene, ibu kota Kireneika -- sebuah kota Yunani di Afrika Utara yang terkenal karena kemakmuran dan para ahli filsafatnya -- kulitku tidaklah putih. Aku Simon dari Kirene. Aku orang Yahudi asli sampai ke jantung hati. Sejak kecil, kutaati semua hukum agama tanpa kecuali, walaupun aku tidak lagi fasih berbahasa Aram akibat dibesarkan dalam masyarakat yang berbahasa Yunani. Aku Simon dari Kirene. Aku tidak ingin berkisah tentang diri sendiri. Juga tidak tentang semua pengalaman hidupku. Aku cuma ingin bercerita tentang pengalamanku yang satu itu. Pengalaman yang kemudian mengubah seluruh jalan hidupku. Dan seluruh jalan hidup Anda, sekiranya Anda juga mengalaminya. Hari itu adalah hari Jumat. Aku baru saja tiba di Yerusalem pagi itu. Tujuanku melakukan perjalanan yang jauh itu adalah untuk merayakan hari raya Paskah. Setiap tahun aku melakukannya. Tidak sedikit pun aku heran melihat orang-orang penuh sesak memadati kota. Walaupun letih, segera setelah menaruh barang-barangku di hotel dan membersihkan badan, aku keluar berjalan-jalan untuk menikmati keriuhan kota yang sedang larut dalam semarak pesta. Lengking jeritan anak-anak yang berlari ria kian kemari, teriakan membujuk bahkan kadang-kadang memaksa para pedagang yang menjajakan barang-barangnya, dan bau asap dupa atau suara syahdu orang-orang yang menyanyikan kidung-kidung pujaan -- semua itu membuat aku lupa akan keletihanku. Suasana yang agak liar ini memang berbeda benar dengan suasana Kirene yang sopan dan tertib. Namun, lebih hidup. Tiba-tiba ada kegaduhan yang tak biasa. Para serdadu Roma menyeruak massa. "Ah, lagi-lagi pawai laskar-laskar Romawi untuk mengingatkan siapa yang berkuasa di negeri ini," pikirku. Akan tetapi tidak. Di baris paling depan, ada seorang serdadu yang memegang panji bertulis: "Yesus, orang Nazaret, raja orang Yahudi." Aku memang belum pernah berjumpa dengan-Nya. Akan tetapi, nama "Yesus", siapa yang tidak mengenal-Nya? Dia adalah tokoh paling kontroversial. Yang tidak dapat kumengerti, mengapa serdadu Romawi mengarak panji seperti itu. Karena itu, aku mendekat untuk melihat lebih dekat. Di tengah pagar betis laskar-laskar Roma itu, tiga orang melangkah pelan memanggul salib. "Penjahat-penjahat besar," pikirku. Namun, apa hubungannya dengan panji itu? Kemudian aku semakin mengerti. Riuh rendah massa rakyat menyebut-nyebut nama Yesus sambil mencemooh-Nya. Tidak kurang pula yang meludahi-Nya. Akan tetapi, yang manakah Yesus di antara ketiga orang itu? Aku Simon dari Kirene. Aku semakin mendekat. Lalu aku tahu dengan pasti yang mana Yesus. Dia paling kecil, hampir tidak berotot. Rambut panjang-Nya terurai, lekat di sana-sini oleh darah kering yang berasal dari duri-duri yang teranyam di kepala-Nya. Sekujur tubuh-Nya biru lebam. Langkah-Nya tertatih-tatih. Amat letih. Akan tetapi mata-Nya -- meski merah sebab kurang tidur -- namun tetap tajam menusuk setiap kali menatap. Anehnya, juga begitu lembut menyejukkan. Aku tak dapat lepas memandang mata-Nya itu. Penuh wibawa, tetapi juga begitu menenangkan dan kebapakan. Lalu Dia roboh. Tubuh-Nya yang kecil dan nyaris hancur itu tidak kuat lagi menahan bobot salib di pundak-Nya. Massa berteriak kesenangan bagai binatang liar yang haus darah. Cemeti melayang menyayat punggung-Nya. Darah menyembur. Dan Dia pun bangkit lagi pelan-pelan. Keletihan. Tetapi mata-Nya itu, oi, mata-Nya. Lalu Dia berjalan beberapa langkah. Namun, roboh lagi. Arak-arakan berhenti. Massa semakin buas. Cemeti melayang berulang-ulang. Darah menyembur. featured.content_zh:
我是来自古利内的西门。我的名字表明我住在非洲大陆。尽管如此，我的皮肤并不黑，嘴唇也不厚。尽管我的家族已经在昔兰尼生活了几代人，昔兰尼是昔兰尼加的首府，这是一座位于北非的希腊城市，以其繁荣和哲学家而闻名，但我的肤色并不白。我是古利奈的西门。

我从心底里是一个地道的犹太人。从小到大，我毫无例外地遵守所有宗教律法，尽管由于在讲希腊语的社区长大，我已经不再精通阿拉姆语。我是古利奈人西门。我不想谈论我自己。也不想讲述我所有的生活经历。我只想讲述我那一次的经历。

这段经历后来改变了我的人生轨迹。如果您也经历过，那么也会改变您的人生轨迹。那天是星期五。那天早上我刚抵达耶路撒冷。我长途跋涉的目的就是为了庆祝逾越节。我每年都这样做。看到熙熙攘攘的人群挤满了这座城市，我一点也不感到惊讶。

尽管很累，但在酒店放下行李并洗漱完毕后，我还是出门散步，享受这座沉浸在节日气氛中的城市的喧嚣。

到处跑来跑去的孩子们尖叫声，叫卖的小贩们劝诱甚至有时强迫的吆喝声，还有熏香的味道或人们吟唱赞美诗的悠扬声音——这一切都让我忘记了疲惫。这种略显喧闹的氛围与古利奈文雅有序的氛围截然不同，但却更有活力。

突然间，出现了一阵不寻常的喧哗。罗马士兵挤过人群。“唉，又是罗马士兵的游行，用来提醒人们谁才是这个国家的统治者。”我想。但是不是。在最前面一排，有一名士兵拿着一面旗帜，上面写着：“拿撒勒人耶稣，犹太人的王。” 我确实从未见过祂。

但是，“耶稣”这个名字，谁不认识他呢？他是最具争议的人物。我不明白的是，为什么罗马士兵要举着这样的旗帜游行。因此，我走近仔细观察。在罗马士兵的方阵中间，有三个人背着十字架缓缓前行。“大坏蛋，”我想。不过，这和那面旗帜有什么关系？

然后我渐渐明白了。人群喧嚣着，一边喊着耶稣的名字，一边嘲笑祂。还有不少人向祂吐唾沫。但是，这三个人当中哪一个是耶稣呢？我是古利奈人西门。我走得越来越近。然后我确切地知道谁是耶稣。他是三人中个子最小的，几乎没有肌肉。

祂的长发散乱，这里那里都沾满了干涸的血迹，这些血迹来自祂头上戴着的荆棘冠。祂的全身都瘀青了。祂的步伐蹒跚。祂非常疲惫。但是祂的眼睛——尽管因为睡眠不足而发红——但每次注视时仍然锐利如刀。奇怪的是，他的眼神也如此温柔、令人舒心。我无法移开视线，不去看祂的眼睛。

充满威严，但也非常平和和慈父般。然后祂倒下了。祂瘦小而几乎破碎的身体再也承受不住肩上十字架的重量。人群像嗜血的野兽一样欢呼雀跃。鞭子抽打着祂的背。鲜血喷涌而出。祂又慢慢地站了起来。祂疲惫不堪。但是祂的眼睛，哎呀，祂的眼睛。

然后他走了几步。然而，祂又倒下了。游行队伍停了下来。人群变得越来越凶狠。鞭子一次又一次地挥舞着。鲜血喷涌而出。然而，祂再也无法站起来了。我是古利奈人西门。不知为何，这一切并没有真正触动我。除了祂的眼神。祂的眼睛，哎呀，祂的眼睛。

因此，当一名士兵突然拉我时，我好像失去了知觉。然后把十字架放在我身上。

La moyenne d’âge dépassait même les 35 ans, souligne-t-il, voyant dans cet engagement « un symbole de l’enthousiasme de tout le peuple argentin ». Il rappelle également que le pays a toujours été très mobilisé lors des Journées mondiales de la jeunesse, qui ont contribué à faire grandir « l’esprit du volontariat ». featured.content_zh:
阿根廷主教团传播事务主任马克西莫·尤尔维诺维奇先生（Don Máximo Jurvinovic）自豪而准确地宣布了这一数字：共有 25,077 名志愿者在教宗访问的各个地点（布宜诺斯艾利斯、克莱波尔、科尔多瓦和卢汉）报名。

他赞扬他们“出色的服务和培训工作”，并强调他们为履行职责做了大量准备。他向Aleteia强调：“他们的工作非常出色，对于教宗此次访问所需的所有服务而言都必不可少。”他表达了组织方对数千名志愿者的感激之情。

虽然年轻人占多数，但这场动员活动吸引了所有年龄段的人群。他指出，参与者的平均年龄甚至超过了 35 岁，他认为这种参与热情“象征着全体阿根廷人民的热情”。

他还提到，在世界青年日期间，该国始终积极动员起来，这有助于“志愿服务精神”的蓬勃发展。对于年轻的会计师瓜达卢佩来说，服务经历……文章“像耶稣那样服务”：为利昂十四世动员的2.5万名志愿者的见证最初发表在Aleteia上。

featured.content: El “Tomus ad Flavianum”: piedra angular del dogma cristológico León Magno fue un teólogo de precisión y profundidad extraordinarias. Su famosa carta doctrinal al patriarca Flaviano de Constantinopla —conocida como el Tomus ad Flavianum— definió con claridad la doctrina católica sobre las dos naturalezas de Cristo: divina y humana, unidas en una sola Persona. Este documento fue leído en el Concilio de Calcedonia (451) ante cientos de obispos que, al escucharlo, exclamaron: “Pedro ha hablado por boca de León.” Con esa expresión, la Iglesia universal reconocía el primado de la sede romana y la continuidad entre el Apóstol Pedro y sus sucesores. En tiempos en que el poder imperial pretendía someter la doctrina al control político, León reivindicó que la autoridad del Papa no depende del César ni de los concilios, sino de Cristo mismo, que prometió: “Tú eres Pedro, y sobre esta piedra edificaré mi Iglesia.” Gracias a su intervención, el Concilio de Calcedonia se convirtió en un hito de la ortodoxia cristológica y en un testimonio de la primacía del Romano Pontífice. El Papa León no impuso su autoridad con la fuerza, sino con la verdad; no por ambición humana, sino por fidelidad al depósito recibido. El Papa que detuvo a Atila En el año 452, la amenaza de los hunos llegó hasta las puertas de Italia. Atila, llamado “el azote de Dios”, había devastado Europa central y avanzaba hacia Roma. Sin ejército ni armas, León decidió ir al encuentro del invasor acompañado solo de algunos clérigos. El encuentro en el río Mincio, cerca de Mantua, se convirtió en uno de los episodios más sobrecogedores de la historia. La tradición narra que Atila, al ver al Papa, quedó sobrecogido por una fuerza sobrenatural y decidió retirarse. Algunos cronistas antiguos dicen que el caudillo vio detrás de León a los santos Pedro y Pablo empuñando espadas. Fuera cual fuera la causa, el hecho histórico es indiscutible: el Papa, solo con su autoridad moral, salvó a Roma de una destrucción segura. Tres años después, en el 455, León volvió a intervenir ante el vándalo Genserico, quien, aunque saqueó la ciudad, accedió a no incendiarla ni matar a sus habitantes. En una era de barbarie y desesperanza, el Papa se convirtió en defensor de la dignidad humana y de la civilización cristiana naciente. Un pastor de almas y doctor de la fe Más allá de los hechos históricos, el legado espiritual de León Magno se encuentra en sus Sermones y Cartas, textos que combinan rigor teológico, belleza retórica y profundidad pastoral. Sus homilías sobre la Encarnación y la Pascua son verdaderas joyas del pensamiento cristiano. En ellas resuena una teología que no separa la doctrina de la vida, ni la fe de la caridad. Fue también un reformador eclesial: disciplinó al clero, combatió los abusos, promovió la vida monástica y fortaleció la autoridad episcopal. Instituyó la solemnidad de la Natividad del Señor en Roma y consolidó la liturgia romana, que más tarde se extendería a toda la cristiandad. En un tiempo en que el caos amenazaba con disolver las instituciones, León mostró que la verdadera reforma de la Iglesia comienza en la santidad de sus pastores. De su espiritualidad brota una enseñanza perenne: el cristiano no puede dejarse arrastrar por el miedo ni por la confusión del mundo. Como escribió en una de sus homilías más célebres: “Reconoce, cristiano, tu dignidad. Y, puesto que has sido hecho partícipe de la naturaleza divina, no vuelvas a la antigua vileza con una conducta indigna.” En esas palabras se resume toda su visión: la fe no es una idea, sino una transformación de la persona; una participación real en la vida de Cristo. El Doctor que iluminó siglos León Magno murió el 10 de noviembre del año 461. Fue sepultado en la Basílica de San Pedro y proclamado Doctor de la Iglesia en el siglo XVIII por el Papa Benedicto XIV. Su influencia doctrinal se extendió por siglos y moldeó el pensamiento cristiano sobre el sacerdocio, la autoridad papal y la teología de la Encarnación. Su magi
