featured.title: Why Did Prosecutors Agree To Omit References to Katy Perry From the Opening Statements at Trial ?
featured.summary: Prosecutors agreed to remove references to Katy Perry from their opening statement at Russell Brand's London rape trial after objections from his lawyers. The decision emerged on Thursday, 5 November
featured.summary_zh: 在拉塞尔·布兰德的伦敦强奸案庭审中，经其律师提出异议，检方同意从开庭陈述中删除提及凯蒂·佩里的内容。该决定于11月5日星期四公布。
featured.title_zh: 为什么检察官同意在庭审开场陈述中省略对凯蒂·佩里的提及？
featured.content: Prosecutors agreed to remove references to Katy Perry from their opening statement at Russell Brand's London rape trial after objections from his lawyers. The decision emerged on Thursday, 5 November 2026, after a jury returned verdicts at Southwark Crown Court. Brand, 51, was convicted of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault involving four women. Jurors acquitted him of two further rape charges and one count of attempted indecent assault. He had denied all seven charges, which concerned six women. Details of the pretrial discussions became public after reporting restrictions ended. They showed how Brand's former marriage was kept out of the prosecution's opening address, although he later mentioned Perry while giving evidence. Why Katy Perry References Were Removed From the Opening Lead prosecutor Riel Karmy-Jones KC acknowledged in written submissions that references to Brand's relationship with Perry after 2009 'may be sensitive'. According to Sky News' court reporting, prosecutors were 'content to remove these from the opening' following defence submissions. The agreement was limited to the opening statement. It did not prevent every mention of Perry during the proceedings or establish that the relationship itself was evidence of wrongdoing. Perry was not accused of any offence. Prosecutors also agreed to leave out references to Brand's earlier religious beliefs and his 2024 baptism. His Christian conversion was nevertheless mentioned during questioning of his wife, Laura, showing that the restrictions on the opening did not cover all subsequent testimony. Other arguments before the trial concerned references to Brand's past drug and alcohol use. His lawyers challenged their relevance to the allegations, and material about treatment at a sex addiction clinic was omitted from a former assistant's evidence. Those disputes were separate from the agreement concerning Perry. The Crown Prosecution Service confirmed that investigators had not asked Perry for a witness statement. Senior Crown Prosecutor David Roberts said reasonable lines of inquiry relevant to the charges had been pursued. There is no basis in that statement to suggest Perry refused to cooperate. Katy Perry's Marriage Still Entered the Courtroom Perry and Brand began dating in 2009 and married in Rajasthan, India, in 2010. They separated in December 2011, and their divorce was finalised in 2012. The offences for which Brand was convicted took place between 2004 and 2009. During his evidence, Brand referred to the marriage and said it had brought him 'staggering fame'. The comment arose from his own testimony, not the prosecution's opening statement. It did not turn Perry into a witness or complainant. The Crown Prosecution Service said the women whose cases resulted in convictions came forward independently after a television investigation aired in September 2023. Prosecutors relied on their accounts and testimony from other witnesses to present evidence of Brand's conduct. Following the verdict, Roberts said Brand had 'used his celebrity status to commit sexual crimes'. The agency thanked the women for coming forward and stressed that sexual offences can be prosecuted years after they occur. The complainants have lifelong anonymity. Mr Justice Joel Bennathan refused Brand bail and remanded him in custody ahead of sentencing on Monday, 9 November. The judge warned that he faced a 'significant custodial term'. Rape carries a maximum penalty of life imprisonment in England and Wales. © Copyright IBTimes 2026. All rights reserved.

Brand被定罪的罪行发生在2004年至2009年期间。 在他的证据中,布兰德提到了这段婚姻,并说这给他带来了"恶搞的名声". 评论来自他本人的证词,而不是检方的开场白。 它没有将Perry变成证人或投诉人。

featured.title_zh: 圣洁教会各宗派“在孤立的时代，成为‘联结的教会’”
featured.content:
고립, 노인 넘어 청년·중장년 등 생애 전반 확산, 사각지대 우려 5단계 ‘연결하는 교회 모델’ 제시 교단 차원 전문인력 지원 체계

한국성결교회연합회(대표회장 이기용 목사, 이하 한성연)가 1인 가구 증가와 초고령화, 디지털 단절 등으로 심화되는 ‘사회적 고립’ 문제에 대해 사회복지 사역을 통한 대안을 모색했다.

한성연 사회복지분과(위원장 이근수 목사)가 주최하고 기성 사회복지부가 주관한 ‘2026 한국성결교회연합회 사회복지정책포럼’이 지난 11월 12일 서울 영등포구 신길교회(이기용 목사)에서 열렸다.

‘지역사회의 희망이 되는 성결교회: 고립된 사회, 연결하는 교회’를 주제로 열린 이번 포럼에는 기성·예성·나성 3개 성결교단 목회자와 사회복지 전문가 등 130여 명이 참석해 교회의 공적 역할과 실천 방안을 논의했다.

2부 포럼에서는 예성 사회복지위 고문 김병천 목사를 좌장으로 조성희 교수(서울신대 사회복지학과)가 ‘고립된 사회, 연결하는 교회: 사회적 고립을 돌보는 한국교회의 역할’을 주제로 기조발제에 나섰다.

조성희 교수는 “전체 가구의 36.1%가 1인 가구인 시대에, 고립은 노인뿐 아니라 청년·중장년 등 생애 과정 전반으로 확산되고 있다”며 기존 신청주의 복지체계의 사각지대를 지적했다. 그는 “교회는 생활권 내 상시 공간과 세대를 아우르는 소그룹 네트워크를 보유한 최적의 관계안전망”이라며 ①발견 ②접촉(안부·식사) ③신뢰관계 형성 ④지역 전문자원 연결 ⑤지속적 동행 등 5단계 ‘연결하는 교회 모델’과 교단 차원 매뉴얼·전문인력 지원체계 구축을 제안했다.

조 교수는 이러한 돌봄이 개별 교회의 선의에만 의존하지 않도록 교단 차원에서 △목회자 및 평신도 대상 고립 위험신호 발견·대응 교육 실시 △고립 가구 발굴 및 관계 돌봄 매뉴얼 보급 △사회복지사·상담가·의료인 등 교단 내 전문인력 네트워크 구축 △소규모 재정 지원 체계 마련 △우수 실천사례의 표준 모델 확산 등이 뒷받침되어야 한다고 제언했다.

3부 사례발표에서는 이계상 목사(나성 평택대 교수)를 좌장으로, 3개 교단별 구체적 복지목회 모델이 소개됐다.

첫 발제에서 ‘초고령사회 한국교회 노인복지목회 대안 및 실천사례’를 발표한 김재열 장로(기성 낙원교회·동원대 교수)는 2050년 노인 성도 비율이 43.9%에 달할 것으로 전망하며 ‘노인영성 복지목회’로의 전환을 촉구했다.

김 장로는 △지자체 위탁을 통해 지역 복지 허브 역할을 수행하는 대형교회 모델(안성교회) △순수 민간 자원으로 25년간 무료급식과 도시락 배달을 이어온 소형교회 모델(사랑의쉼터교회) △장기요양기관 운영을 통해 자비량 목회와 농촌 폐쇄교회 재생을 이룬 모델(시온교회) 등을 비교 분석하고, 교단 내 사회복지국 신설 및 목회자 이중직 규정 완화 등을 제안했다.

이어 이규 목사(예성 시티미션교회)는 ‘고립 외국인 유학생을 위한 D.C.C(Dream Community Center)’를 소개했다. 국내 체류 외국인 유학생이 30만 명을 넘어선 가운데, 경제난과 언어 장벽, 단기 체류 구조로 고립된 유학생들을 위해 크리스천 ‘드림 파트너’와 일대일로 매칭해 현실적·정서적·영적 필요를 채우는 사역 성과를 공유했다.

마지막으로 오경근 박사(나성 주사랑교회·서일대 특임교수)는 ‘AI 시대, 사람 곁에 남는 교회’를 주제로 ‘관계적 공유제’와 ‘AI 기반 지역공동체 돌봄’ 모델을 제시했다. 오 박사는 “관계의 빈곤은 관계로만 채워지며 알림의 끝에는 반드시 사람이 있어야 한다”며 AI가 지역 내 필요와 자원을 정리하고 돌봄 일정을 관리하는 조력자 역할을 수행하되, 최종 판단과 실제 만남, 지속적인 동행은 사람이 감당하는 순환적 공동체 모델을 강조했다.

이번 포럼은 왕수일 목사(기성 사회복지위원장)의 폐회기도로 마무리됐다. 한성연 사회복지분과는 이날 논의된 정책과 사례를 바탕으로 지교회 일선 현장에 적용 가능한 복지목회 협력을 이어갈 계획이다.

앞선 1부 개회예배는 사회복지분과위원장 이근수 목사의 사회로 예성 사회복지부장 이정소 목사의 기도, 나성 총회감독 최형영 목사의 축사, 서울신대 총장 황덕형 박사의 환영사, 예성 총회장 이종만 목사의 축도로 진행됐다.

‘젖과 꿀이 흐르는 땅’이라는 제목으로 설교한 대표회장 이기용 목사는 “나눔이 있는 곳, 하나님의 축복을 흘려보내는 곳이 젖과 꿀이 흐르는 땅”이라며 “지속적으로 나누고 흘려보내기 위해서는 성령의 도움을 받아야 한다. 사회복지 사역에도 성령 역사가 일어나야 한다”고 강조했다.
featured.content_zh:
隔离，蔓延到老年人以外的整个生命周期，包括青年和中年人；对盲点的担忧；提出“连接教会模式”的五步法；宗派层面的专业支持体系

韩国圣洁教会协会（首席执行官李基勇牧师，以下简称韩成渊）通过社会福利事工寻求替代方案，以解决因单人家庭增加、超老龄化和数字脱节而日益加深的“社会孤立”问题。由韩成渊社会福祉部（李根洙牧师）主办、社会福祉部承办的“2026年韩国圣洁教会协会社会福祉政策论坛”于11月12日在首尔永登浦区新吉教会（李基龙牧师）举行。

本次论坛以“圣洁教会作为社会的希望：连接孤立社会的教会”为主题，来自吉城、艺声、罗城三个圣洁教派的牧师和社会福利专家等约130人出席，讨论了教会的公共角色和行动计划。在第二场论坛上，由艺城社会福利委员会顾问金秉天牧师主持的曹成熙教授（首尔神大学社会福利系）做了题为“孤立的社会，连接教会：韩国教会在应对社会孤立中的作用”的主题演讲。曹成熙教授说：“在36.1%的家庭是单身家庭的时代，孤立是不仅波及到老年人，还波及到整个生命周期，包括年轻人和中年人。”指出了现有申请人福利制度的盲点。

他表示，“教会是最优的关系安全网，拥有永久的生活空间和跨越代际的小团体网络”，并提出了五步“连接教会模式”，包括：①发现、②接触（问候、吃饭）、③建立信任关系、④连接当地专业资源、⑤持续陪伴，并建立宗派层面的人工和专业支持体系。曹教授建议，在宗派层面，为确保这种关怀不单单依赖于个别教会的善意，△对牧师和平信徒进行隔离风险信号检测和应对培训△识别隔离家庭并分发关系关怀手册△在宗派内部建立社工、辅导员、医务人员等专业人员网络△建立小规模的财政支持体系△传播最佳实践的标准模型等。

案例介绍的第三部分，由李桂相牧师（罗城平泽大学教授）担任主持人，介绍了三个教派各自的具体福利事工模式。在第一个演讲中，金载烈长老（老乐院教会、东远大学教授）发表了《超级老龄化社会中韩国教会老年福利事工的替代方案和实践案例》，预测到2050年老年信徒的比例将达到43.9%，并呼吁向“老年灵性福利事工”过渡。金长老对比分析了△作为地方福利中心的大型教会模式通过地方政府委托（安城教会） △ 以纯私人资源持续提供免费餐食和盒饭25年的小型教会模式（爱心庇护教会） △ 通过长期看护机构的运营实现自给自足和农村封闭教会复兴的模式（锡安教会），并提出在教派范围内设立社会福利办公室并放宽牧师双职规定。建议。

接下来，艺城市宣教会的李奎牧师介绍了“为孤立的外国学生提供的D.C.C（梦想社区中心）”。在韩国滞留的外国学生人数超过30万的情况下，我们分享了我们的事工成果，通过与基督徒“梦想伙伴”一对一匹配，满足了因经济困难、语言障碍和短期居留而孤立的外国学生的实际、情感和精神需求。最后，吴庆根博士（罗城朱桑郎教会、首尔大学特聘教授）以“人工智能时代与人们保持密切关系的教会”为主题，介绍了“关系共享系统”和“基于人工智能的地区社区关怀”模式。

吴博士表示，“关系的贫乏只能靠关系来填补，通知的最后一定要有一个人”，并强调了循环社区模式，其中人工智能扮演帮助者的角色，组织当地的需求和资源，管理护理时间表，但最终的决定、实际的会议和持续的陪伴都是由人类来处理的。本次论坛在王秀一牧师（社会福利委员会委员长）的闭幕祈祷中结束。韩成渊社会福祉科根据今天讨论的政策和事例，计划继续在分会前线开展福祉事工合作。开幕仪式的第一部分由社会福利委员会委员长李根洙牧师主持，艺城社会福利部部长李正昭牧师进行了祈祷，乐城总会理事长崔亨英牧师致贺词，首尔神学大学校长黄德庆博士致欢迎辞，艺城总会会长李钟万牧师进行了祝福。

以“流奶与蜜之地”为题讲道的代表会长李基龙牧师强调：“分享的地方，神的祝福流淌的地方，就是流奶与蜜的地方。”他又说：“要不断地分享、流动，就必须得到圣灵的帮助。圣灵的工作也必须发生在社会公益工作中。”

featured.summary_zh: 10月初，一名20岁的科普特基督徒被伊斯兰国家集团绑架并杀害。Milad Malak住在埃及的Sebarbay ，在当地的科普特教会担任教会执事。然而，由于该国的经济衰退，他于9月2日前往利比亚寻找工作。他制作了......在利比亚殉难的埃及基督徒后首次出现在国际基督教关注。
featured.title_zh: 埃及基督徒在利比亚殉道
featured.content: In early October, a 20-year-old Coptic Christian was kidnapped and killed at the hands of the Islamic State group. Milad Malak lived in Sebarbay, Egypt, and served as a church deacon at a local Coptic church. However, because of the country’s economic decline, he traveled to Libya on Sept. 2 to find work. He made a day’s journey with two Muslim friends and arrived in Zliten, where they stayed with other Egyptian migrant workers. On the morning of Oct. 4, ISIS militants kidnapped them. The captors subjected the group to abuse while they held them hostage for ransom money. Milad’s friends were released after their families paid a $4,700 ransom. They are now receiving medical treatment at a hospital in Egypt. Milad’s sister, Madonna Malek, told Worthy News that their family paid a ransom, but because he was the only Christian in the group, his kidnappers refused to release him and violently pressured him to convert to Islam. Milad stood strong in his faith until the end. He told his persecutors, “Even if you cut me into pieces, I would never renounce my faith.” When the militants realized they could not force him to abandon his God, they killed him. Faithful Until the End After hearing about his death from his friends, Milad’s family appealed to the Egyptian government, asking them to intervene and demand that his body be returned home. Several weeks went by until it was finally released, and on Oct. 28, grieving family members and fellow Christians gathered to celebrate the life of their beloved son and friend. “He was faithful to Christ till his last breath,” a family friend said. Open Doors ranked Libya as the ninth most dangerous place to be a Christian. A Muslim-majority nation, Christians face heavy pressure to abandon their faith. Milad’s death has reminded believers of the massacre that occurred in 2015, when 20 Coptic Christians and one Ghanaian were beheaded by militants in Libya for standing strong in their faith. Milad joins them as yet another martyr who inspires Christians worldwide to be bold witnesses for Christ until the very end. Story by Bella Agnello To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . featured.content_zh:
10月初,一名20岁的科普特·克里斯蒂安被伊斯兰国集团绑架并杀害. 米拉德·马拉克居住在埃及塞巴拜,并在当地的科普特教堂担任教堂执事. 然而,由于该国经济下滑,他于9月2日前往利比亚寻找工作。

他与两个穆斯林朋友共度了一天的旅程,并抵达兹利滕,在那里他们与其他埃及移徙工人住在一起。 10月4日上午,伊斯兰国武装分子绑架了他们。 抓捕者在以赎金为人质时虐待该团伙。 Mirad的朋友在家人支付了4700美元的赎金后被释放。

他们目前正在埃及的一家医院接受治疗。 米拉德的妹妹麦当娜·马利克(Madonna Malek)告诉沃西新闻,他们的家人支付了赎金,但由于他是这群人中唯一的基督徒,绑匪拒绝释放他,并用暴力逼迫他皈依伊斯兰教. 米拉德坚守信仰,直到最后.

他对他的迫害者说:即使你把我割成碎片,我也不会放弃我的信仰。 当激进分子意识到他们不能强迫他放弃上帝时,他们杀了他. Milad的家人在从朋友那里得知他的死讯后,

几个星期过去了,直到最终发行,10月28日,悲痛的家人和基督徒同胞聚集在一起,庆祝他们心爱的儿子和朋友的生命. 一位家庭朋友说:“他忠于基督直到最后一口气”。 开放门将利比亚列为第九个最危险的基督徒地点.

作为一个穆斯林占多数的民族,基督徒面临着放弃信仰的沉重压力. Milad的死让信徒想起了2015年发生的大屠杀,当时利比亚有20名科普特基督徒和1名加纳人因坚守信仰而被激进分子斩首. 米拉德与他们一起成为另一个烈士,他激励全世界的基督徒成为基督的大胆见证,直到最后.

featured.title: After his daughter was killed, he prayed for a Bible no one could take from him
featured.summary: Uzbekistan and Tajikistan· 2020s
featured.summary_zh: 乌兹别克斯坦和塔吉克斯坦·2020年代
featured.title_zh: 女儿被杀后，他祈祷能拥有一本无人能夺走的圣经
featured.content: Rashid Kadirov was a Muslim in Central Asia when the worst thing happened. His six-year-old daughter Azizza was killed by a drunk neighbour driving a tractor. In his grief he went looking for something the ache could rest on, and he went to the Koran. There he read a line, in Surah 5:70, that pointed back to the Gospels as holy scripture. So he prayed a strange, specific prayer. He asked God for an Injil, a New Testament. His friends brought him one. It was a stolen Gideon Bible, taken from a vandalised car. It did not last. When the friends took it back, Rashid prayed again, this time for a Bible no one could take away from him. The book that stayed Then a couple arrived from Tajikistan, sent by a former classmate of his who had himself come to Christ. They carried a Bible and a copy of the JESUS Film. Rashid and his wife Aleka watched it, and as the good news was explained, each of them, without telling the other, quietly prayed to receive Jesus. Aleka barely understood it all. "She had very little understanding of the Gospel," she said later, "and yet peace flooded her heart." They were baptised in Tajikistan, and Rashid started telling others what he had found. A grieving father asked for a book, and God gave him a Person. The peace Rashid could not manufacture arrived the moment Jesus did. He is close to the brokenhearted, and He is near to you.
featured.content_zh:
拉希德·卡迪罗夫(Rashid Kadirov)是中亚穆斯林,当时最糟糕的事情发生了. 他的六岁女儿Azizza被驾拖拉机喝醉的邻居杀死. 在悲痛中,他去寻找可以安息的东西,他去了可兰经. 在那里,他读到了一行,在苏拉5:70中,指向福音书作为圣经. 所以他祈祷了一个奇怪的,具体的祈祷.

他向上帝祈求"印吉尔","新约". 他的朋友给他带来了一个。 是一辆被偷来的吉迪恩圣经 从被破坏的汽车上拍下来的 它没有持续。 当朋友们收回它时,拉希德再次祈祷,这次要一本圣经,没有人能夺走他. 留下来的书 之后一对夫妇从塔吉克斯坦赶来,他们是由自己来到基督的前同学派来的.

他们携带了圣经和JESUS电影的拷贝. 拉希德和他的妻子阿莱卡观看了,正如好消息被解释的那样,他们每个人都在不告诉对方的情况下悄悄地祈祷要接受耶稣. 阿莱卡根本不懂这些

"她对福音几乎没有什么了解,"后来她说,"然而和平却淹没了她的心. 他们在塔吉克斯坦接受洗礼,拉希德开始告诉其他人他发现了什么. 一个悲伤的父亲要求一本书,上帝给了他一个人. 和平拉希德无法在耶稣到达的时候制造。 他与心碎者密不可分,他与你们密不可分。

featured.title: Arrested at the hospital where he worked, he turned the prison into a pulpit
featured.summary: 🇪🇷Eritrea· 2010s
featured.summary_zh: 🇪🇷厄立特里亚·21世纪10年代
featured.title_zh: 他在自己工作的医院被捕，并将监狱变成了讲坛。
featured.content: Dr Berhane was a new believer in Jesus, working in a hospital in Eritrea, when the secret police came for him. His crime was his faith. They put him in prison for eleven months, in one of the harshest systems on earth, a place designed to make Christians disappear and go quiet. He did the opposite. "Every day I was clapping my hands," he said, "and prisoners would come forward and I shared the gospel." A man who had only recently met Jesus decided his cell was simply the next place to introduce Him. Three Bibles and a valley of death The authorities took his Bible. He smuggled another in. They took that one too, and he smuggled a third. He leaned hard on the Psalms, and when fellow prisoners were taken out and executed, the old line about walking through the valley of the shadow of death stopped being poetry and became the thing that held him upright. Eleven months of that did not break him. It made him a preacher. The guards meant to silence a new Christian and instead handed him a congregation with nowhere to go. Wherever they put you, Jesus goes with you, and He is not intimidated by the walls. Dr Berhane found that out in an Eritrean prison. You can trust it wherever you are.
featured.content_zh:
Berhane博士是耶稣的新信徒,在厄立特里亚的一家医院工作,当时秘密警察来找他。 他的罪行是他的信仰。 他们把他关进监狱11个月,在地球上最严酷的系统之一,一个旨在使基督徒消失和安静的地方. 他做的恰恰相反。

"每天我拍手,"他说:"囚犯会站出来,我分享福音". 一个刚认识耶稣的人决定 他的牢房只是下一个介绍他的地方 三个圣经和一个死亡之谷 当局拿走了他的圣经。 他又偷渡进来了 他们也拿走了那个 他走私了三分之一

他极力倚靠"诗经",当狱友被带出处死时,关于走过死亡阴影谷的老台词不再是诗歌,成为了扶他站直的东西. 11个月没有打倒他。 这让他成了传教士。 守卫们打算让新基督徒安静下来,反而给了他一个无处可去的会众.

无论他们把你放在哪里,耶稣都跟着你,他不受墙壁的恐吓. Berhane博士在厄立特里亚的一所监狱发现了这一点。 你可以相信它 无论你在哪里。

featured.summary_zh: 11月6日，一名名叫阿贾克·马比奥尔（Ajak Mabior）的18岁基督徒女孩在南苏丹琼莱州因拒绝接受家人包办的强迫婚姻而被殴打致死。她本应嫁给一位年长的穆斯林男子——由于她的基督教信仰以及不愿意被强迫结婚，她反对这桩婚事。此后……   这篇题为《因拒绝强迫婚姻而被杀害的女孩》的文章  最初发表在  国际基督徒关注组织  网站上。
featured.title_zh: 因拒绝强迫婚姻而被杀害的女孩
featured.content: On Nov. 6, an 18-year-old Christian girl named Ajak Mabior was beaten to death in Jonglei, South Sudan, after refusing to enter a forced marriage arranged by her family. She was expected to marry an older Muslim man — a marriage she opposed because of her Christian faith and her unwillingness to be forced into it. After attempting to escape, she was killed by her own brother and cousin. Days later, police in Bor arrested the two men but released them without charges after family members demanded their freedom, arguing that “there was no case” because they were relatives. A Common Problem The killing has raised serious concerns among Christian leaders about the pressure Christian girls face when their faith and personal convictions conflict with family expectations. “When a young girl is killed for refusing a forced marriage, and the killers walk free because they are family, the message is clear: Tradition is stronger than the law, and stronger than the value of a life,” a local pastor said. “Many of our Christian daughters live under this same shadow.” For Christian girls in South Sudan , forced marriages can become a matter of religious persecution when they are pressured to marry outside their faith and abandon their Christian convictions. Those who refuse may face rejection, threats, intimidation, and violence from their own families. Mabior’s death highlights the vulnerability of young Christian women who seek to remain faithful to Christ while facing pressure to submit to marriages that violate their faith and conscience. “The church teaches that every life is precious because it is created in the image of God,” the pastor added. “Yet when a Christian girl refuses a marriage that would bind her against her will, she can be treated as a traitor to the community. We have buried too many who paid that price.” Seeking Justice The authorities’ response has added to the church’s concerns. Police reportedly released the suspects without the consent of the Jonglei State Caretaker Commissioner. The justification that the suspects were relatives raises serious questions about the protection available to Christian girls facing forced marriages and violence. When perpetrators are released without facing justice, vulnerable Christian women are left with little confidence that the authorities will protect their right to practice their faith and make decisions according to their conscience. “We preach freedom in Christ, but our young people still live in fear of the consequences of that freedom,” the pastor said. “If the police and local authorities remain quiet, the church becomes the only place left where these girls and boys can find a voice. We need courage to speak, and we need the wider Body of Christ to stand with us.” Mabior’s case raises concerns about forced interfaith marriages, religious pressure, and violence against young Christian women in South Sudan. “We call on the wider Body of Christ to pray for Ajak’s justice, and for the protection of Christian girls facing forced marriages because of their faith,” an International Christian Concern (ICC) staffer said. “Pray that the church will have the courage to speak against religious coercion and violence, and that the authorities will uphold the law and protect vulnerable believers.” To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . For interviews, please email us . To support ICC’s work around the world, please give to our Where Most Needed Fund . The post The Girl They Killed for Refusing a Forced Marriage first appeared on International Christian Concern .
featured.content_zh:
11月6日,一名名叫Ajak Mabior的18岁基督教女孩在南苏丹琼格莱州因拒绝参加家庭安排的强迫婚姻而被殴打致死。 她被期望嫁给一个年长的穆斯林男子——她反对这种婚姻,因为她的基督教信仰以及她不愿意被迫加入. 在试图逃跑后,她被自己的哥哥和表妹杀死.

几天后,Bor的警察逮捕了这两名男子,但在家属要求他们自由后,在没有指控的情况下将他们释放,他们辩称“没有案件”,因为他们是亲属。 常见问题 杀害事件引起了基督教领袖的严重关切,基督教女孩在信仰和个人信念与家庭期望相冲突时面临压力。

“当一名年轻女孩因拒绝强迫婚姻而被杀害,而杀人者因是家人而自由行动时,信息是明确的:传统比法律更强大,比生命的价值更强大。” 一位当地牧师说。

“我们许多基督教女儿生活在这种阴影下。” 对于南苏丹的基督教女孩来说,当她们被迫在信仰之外结婚并放弃基督教信仰时,强迫婚姻就可能成为宗教迫害的问题。 拒绝者可能面临自己家庭的排斥、威胁、恐吓和暴力。

Mabior的死亡凸显了基督教青年妇女的脆弱性,她们试图保持对基督的忠诚,同时面临压力,迫使她们向违反其信仰和良心的婚姻屈服。 牧师补充说,“教会教导每一条生命都是宝贵的,因为它是以上帝的形象创造的。”

“当一个基督教女孩拒绝违背她意愿而束缚她的婚姻时,她可以被当作一个叛徒对待。 我们埋葬了太多付出这一代价的人。” 寻求正义 当局的反应增加了教会的关注。 据报告,警方未经琼格莱州看守专员同意释放了嫌疑人。

关于嫌疑人是亲属的理由,令人对面临强迫婚姻和暴力的基督教女孩获得的保护提出严重问题。 当肇事者在没有受到法律制裁的情况下被释放时,脆弱的基督教妇女对当局将保护其信仰和根据其良心作出决定的权利缺乏信心。

牧师说,“我们在基督中宣扬自由,但我们的年轻人仍然生活在对这种自由的后果的恐惧之中。” “如果警察和地方当局保持安静,教堂就成了这些女孩和男孩能够发表意见的唯一地方。

我们需要勇气说话,我们需要更广泛的基督与我们站在一起。” Mabior案引起了人们对南苏丹境内强迫不同信仰间婚姻、宗教压力以及针对基督教青年妇女的暴力的关注。

“我们呼吁广大的基督机构为阿贾克的正义祈祷,并保护因信仰而面临强迫婚姻的基督教女孩。” 一位国际基督教关注组织的工作人员说。

“祈祷教会有勇气反对宗教胁迫和暴力,并祈祷当局将维护法律,保护脆弱的信徒。” 阅读更多新闻, 请给我们发电子邮件 支持电算中心在世界各地的工作,

featured.title: They locked the pastor in a psychiatric ward. He led a hundred men to Jesus
featured.title_zh: 他们把牧师关进了精神病病房。他带领一百人归向耶稣
featured.content: Pastor Bakhytzhan Kashkumbaev was an elderly man when Kazakhstan arrested him in May 2013. The charges were strange, that he had harmed a church member's health and stirred up religious hatred. They sentenced him toward ten years and put him in a psychiatric ward, where inmates were routinely drugged. On the way in, he thought it might be the end of his mind. "This is probably the last time I will talk to you in my right mind," he said. Then a question reached him, the kind God uses. "Where is your faith?" Under the cover of the risen Lord Something lifted. "I felt like I was under the cover of the risen Lord," he said. The old man who expected to lose himself instead found Jesus nearer than the walls. He started talking to the men around him. To a prisoner wrecked by drug addiction he said simply, "Only Jesus can help you." Over nine months inside, nearly one hundred inmates gave their lives to Christ. "In prison," he said, "the Holy Spirit opened one dimension of prayer to me." The place meant to break him became the most fruitful pulpit of his life. They released him in early 2014. He walked out having planted the good news in the last place anyone would look for it. God is not locked out by any door that locks you in. He was already inside, waiting.

2013年5月哈萨克斯坦逮捕Bakhytzhan Kashkumbaev牧师时,他是一位老人。 指控是奇怪的,他伤害了一名教会成员的健康并煽动了宗教仇恨。 他们判处他十年监禁,并把他关进精神病病房,囚犯经常在那里服药。 进来的路上,他觉得这也许是他心智的终结.

"这可能是我最后一次在正确的思想中和你说话,"他说. 然后,一个问题来到他身上,神用的那种。 "你的信仰在哪里?" 在升起的上帝的掩护下 有东西解除了 "我觉得自己在升天主的掩护下,"他说. 期待失去自我的老人却发现耶稣比墙壁更靠近. 他开始和周围的人交谈

对一个吸毒成瘾的囚犯来说 他只是说 只有耶稣才能帮助你 里面有九个月,近一百名囚犯为基督献出了生命。 "在狱中",他说"圣灵为我打开了祈祷的一个维度". 打算打破他的地方成为了他一生中最有成果的支点. 他们于2014年初释放了他。

featured.title_zh: 魔鬼的娱乐使命
featured.content: The following is the substance of a pamphlet published by Archibald G. Brown, a student and then great ally of C. H. Spurgeon in the cause of the gospel in London. Brown here draws attention to a practice that was gaining ground in the churches of his day: that of holding ‘amusements’ of various kinds, which obscured, diverted from, and in some cases replaced the proper ministry of local churches. Brown was savagely attacked in the wake of the publication of the pamphlet, derided as ‘a kill-joy,’ ‘a morbid pietist,’ and ‘a sour bigot.’ His meaning, however, had been deliberately misrepresented. 1 Brown nowhere objects to all amusement per se , but amusement which masquerades as ministry, distracting the church and deceiving needy sinners. While the context in which Brown wrote may be different from ours, we need to hear his burden for a Church—and for Christians—to make a decisive break with the world and its practices. An Evil in the Camp of the Lord DIFFERENT days demand their own special testimony. The watchman who would be faithful to his Lord and the City of his God has need to carefully note the signs of the times and emphasize his witness accordingly. Con­cerning the testimony needed now, there can the little, if any, doubt. featured.content: By ICC Fellow Lisa Navarrette For years, Fadi has told his children the same thing: We stay. He is a Christian father in Lebanon. His family has lived in the same town for generations, and his parents are buried nearby. Fadi’s children were baptized in the church where he married his wife, Nour. His small business survived political unrest, the economic collapse, the Beirut port explosion, and another round of regional conflict. Leaving always felt like surrender. But lately, the calculation has changed. Fuel costs have risen again. Groceries take a larger share of the family’s income. Electricity is unreliable, so the business depends partly on a generator. Transportation costs more. His oldest daughter has been accepted to a university abroad, while his younger son talks openly about finding work in Europe. One evening, Fadi places two folders on the kitchen table. One contains bills. The other contains immigration documents. “We don’t have to decide tonight,” she said. Fadi looks at the paperwork for a long time. Years earlier, violence made the family afraid to leave home. Now economics is making them wonder whether they should leave the country. That is the final link in the chain this series examines. Fighting to Stay High fuel prices do not create religious persecution. But when families have already endured violence, displacement, discrimination, destroyed livelihoods, or political instability, rising energy costs can make recovery harder and staying less sustainable. In 2026, the World Bank warned that the Middle East conflict had created a major energy shock, raising fuel prices, increasing inflation, disrupting transportation and logistics, and weakening economic growth. Its October 2026 regional economic update found that fragile and conflict-affected economies were experiencing especially severe pressure , with poverty still rising in parts of the region even as it declined elsewhere. Those regional trends eventually become household questions: Can the business stay open? Can the family still afford food? Will there be jobs for the children? Is rebuilding worth the cost? Lebanon illustrates how those pressures can accumulate. Christians there have not experienced the same mass expulsion seen in parts of Iraq or Syria, but International Christian Concern (ICC) has documented how economic collapse, political instability, regional conflict, and emigration continue to weaken one of the Middle East’s most important Christian communities. No single crisis explains why a family leaves. That is what makes the process easy to overlook. A Christian family may survive violence but lose its savings. It may survive political instability but lose its business. It may rebuild after displacement only to discover that electricity, fuel, food, and transportation have become increasingly expensive. Eventually, the question is no longer only whether the family is safe. It is whether the family can build a future. Affording Daily Life The same dynamic is evident in Syria, where many people have tried to return after years of war. In May 2026, ICC reported that about 1.67 million refugees and 1.9 million internally displaced Syrians had returned since December 2024. Yet the agency warned that damaged housing, limited livelihoods, weak infrastructure, poverty, and restricted access to basic services continued to threaten the sustainability of those returns. A separate 2026 assessment hosted by UNHCR reached a similar conclusion : whether people remain after returning depends heavily on housing, employment, services, and economic opportunity. For Christian communities, that distinction matters. Imagine a family returning to a Syrian town after years abroad. They repair part of their home. Their children reenter school. The father begins rebuilding a small business. Then expenses start adding up. Electricity remains unreliable. Fuel for the generator costs more. Transportation to work and school takes a larger share of income. Food prices

由ICC研究员莉萨·纳瓦雷特(Lisa Navarrette) 多年来,法迪对他的孩子说了同样的话:我们留下。 他是黎巴嫩的基督教父亲. 他的家族世代居住在同一个城镇,父母也葬在附近. Fadi的孩子在与妻子Nour结婚的教堂接受洗礼。

他的小企业在政治动荡,经济崩溃,贝鲁特港口爆炸以及另一轮区域冲突中幸存下来. 离开总是觉得投降。 但最近,计算方式发生了变化。 燃料成本再次上升。 食谱占家庭收入的较大份额。 电力不可靠,因此业务部分依赖于发电机. 运输成本更高。

他的大女儿被录取到国外的一所大学,而小儿子则公开谈论在欧洲找工作. 一天晚上,法迪把两个文件夹放在厨房桌子上. 一个有账单。 另一个文件载有移民证件。 “我们不必在今晚决定, 法迪很长一段时间都在看文件 几年前,暴力使家庭不敢离家。

现在经济学让他们怀疑他们是否应该出国。 这是本系列审查的链条的最后环节。 高油价斗争不会造成宗教迫害。

但是,当家庭已经忍受了暴力、流离失所、歧视、生计被摧毁或政治不稳定时,能源成本的上升会使恢复更加困难,并降低可持续性。

2026年,世界银行警告说,中东冲突造成了严重的能源冲击,燃料价格上涨,通货膨胀加剧,交通和后勤中断,经济增长减弱.

其2026年10月的区域经济最新情况发现,脆弱和受冲突影响的经济体正承受着特别严重的压力,该区域部分地区的贫困现象仍在加剧,尽管其他地区的贫困状况有所下降。 这些区域趋势最终成为家庭问题:企业能否继续开放? 家人还能买得起食物吗? 孩子们会有工作吗?

重建值得付出代价吗? 黎巴嫩说明了这些压力如何能够累积。 但国际基督教关注组织(ICC)记录了经济崩溃、政治不稳定、地区冲突和移民继续削弱中东最重要的基督教社区之一。

没有一个危机能解释一个家庭为什么离开。 这使得这一进程容易被忽视。 一个基督教家庭可能会在暴力中幸存下来,但却会失去积蓄。 它可能在政治不稳定的情况下生存下来,但失去了业务。 它可能在流离失所后重建,只为了发现电力、燃料、粮食和交通越来越昂贵。

最后,问题不再仅仅是家庭是否安全。 家庭是否能够建立未来。 每日生活 同样的动态在叙利亚也很明显,许多人在多年战争之后试图返回叙利亚。 2026年5月,国际刑事法院报告说,自2024年12月以来,约有167万难民和190万境内流离失所的叙利亚人返回。

然而,该机构警告说,住房受损、生计有限、基础设施薄弱、贫穷以及获得基本服务的机会有限,继续威胁着这些回返的可持续性。 难民署主办的2026年的单独评估得出了类似结论:人们返回后是否仍留在当地,在很大程度上取决于住房、就业、服务和经济机会。

对基督教社区来说,这种区别很重要。 想象一个家庭在海外多年后返回叙利亚城镇。 他们修补了一部分家 他们的孩子重新入学。 父亲开始重建小生意. 然后费用开始增加。 电力仍然不可靠。 发电机的燃料成本更高。 工作和上学的交通占收入的较大份额。

featured.content: How old were you when you first learned that Jesus loves you? Perhaps you’ve always known it and can’t remember a day when you didn’t know the song “Jesus Loves Me” or couldn’t recite John 3:16 by heart. Maybe you were a teenager and learned about Jesus’ love through a friend or church summer camp. Or were in college and went to a concert where the gospel was clearly articulated. Maybe you were in the trenches of the workforce, and a coworker boldly shared with you about the God who radically changed their life. Regardless of how old you were, each of us who has chosen to follow Jesus has an origin story — a moment in our lives when the knowledge that “Jesus loves me, this I know, for the Bible tells me so” moved from head knowledge to heart belief. And from then on, our lives were transformed forever. This is the truth of the gospel and the power of understanding that Jesus loves you. People around the world are discovering the personal truth of John 3:16 for themselves in a language and format they clearly understand. Explore why understanding that “God so loved the world” transforms entire communities → A Changing Reality Throughout Christian history, the gospel has spread from one community to the next. Stories were told and retold, Scripture was translated, churches were planted, and discipleship deepened as people learned more about Jesus. Bible translation is foundational to all ministries of the church. It fuels evangelism, church planting, discipleship and more. It equips people to move from a blurry picture of who God is to a clear understanding and personal encounter with Jesus as Lord. Through Scripture, people are able to read, hear or see the love of God on display. Just two decades ago, most of the world’s language communities still needed Bible translation work to begin , let alone be completed. But praise God, in the last few years, we’ve seen tremendous progress made, with Bible translation underway in more languages than ever before . While the change in numbers is exciting, what’s more important is what they signify: Every number represents a person who has a story that matters to God. For these communities, the stories of future generations are being completely rewritten as children will now grow up never remembering a day when they didn’t have access to God’s Word in a language and format they clearly understand. That statement bears repeating: There will now be people who never remember a day when they didn’t have access to God’s Word in a language and format they clearly understand. From the first word of Genesis to the last word of Revelation, the Bible tells one incredible story: God’s love for the world and His invitation for people from every nation and language to know Him. Get a glimpse of how God continues writing this story today as more and more people are experiencing the power of His Word. Watch the video → A New Generation Growing Up With God’s Word Let’s take a look at some of the recent communities that are experiencing not only life transformation but generational transformation as they encounter Jesus personally through Scripture. Jakalteko | Guatemala The Jakalteko Bible was dedicated in July 2026 in Guatemala! During the celebration, John 1:1-18 was read aloud — a passage that focuses on Christ, the eternal Word and our Redeemer. Early on, many women in the community memorized Job 19 . Like Job, they had faced various hardships in their lives and identified with his suffering. The book reminded them that God remains in control and that, in the midst of difficult circumstances, their Redeemer will deliver them and comfort them in their pain. Today, they have the full counsel of God’s Word and can now see this Redeemer fulfilled in Jesus in the New Testament. They are overjoyed that the Bible has arrived in the language they were born into! When the Bible was distributed, one mother who is raising her family alone said with joy and tears: “Thank God we have the Bible in our language. Now

featured.content: How old were you when you first learned that Jesus loves you? Perhaps you’ve always known it and can’t remember a day when you didn’t know the song “Jesus Loves Me” or couldn’t recite John 3:16 by heart. Maybe you were a teenager and learned about Jesus’ love through a friend or church summer camp. Or were in college and went to a concert where the gospel was clearly articulated. Maybe you were in the trenches of the workforce, and a coworker boldly shared with you about the God who radically changed their life. Regardless of how old you were, each of us who has chosen to follow Jesus has an origin story — a moment in our lives when the knowledge that “Jesus loves me, this I know, for the Bible tells me so” moved from head knowledge to heart belief. And from then on, our lives were transformed forever. This is the truth of the gospel and the power of understanding that Jesus loves you. People around the world are discovering the personal truth of John 3:16 for themselves in a language and format they clearly understand. Explore why understanding that “God so loved the world” transforms entire communities → A Changing Reality Throughout Christian history, the gospel has spread from one community to the next. Stories were told and retold, Scripture was translated, churches were planted, and discipleship deepened as people learned more about Jesus. Bible translation is foundational to all ministries of the church. It fuels evangelism, church planting, discipleship and more. It equips people to move from a blurry picture of who God is to a clear understanding and personal encounter with Jesus as Lord. Through Scripture, people are able to read, hear or see the love of God on display. Just two decades ago, most of the world’s language communities still needed Bible translation work to begin , let alone be completed. But praise God, in the last few years, we’ve seen tremendous progress made, with Bible translation underway in more languages than ever before . While the change in numbers is exciting, what’s more important is what they signify: Every number represents a person who has a story that matters to God. For these communities, the stories of future generations are being completely rewritten as children will now grow up never remembering a day when they didn’t have access to God’s Word in a language and format they clearly understand. That statement bears repeating: There will now be people who never remember a day when they didn’t have access to God’s Word in a language and format they clearly understand. From the first word of Genesis to the last word of Revelation, the Bible tells one incredible story: God’s love for the world and His invitation for people from every nation and language to know Him. Get a glimpse of how God continues writing this story today as more and more people are experiencing the power of His Word. Watch the video → A New Generation Growing Up With God’s Word Let’s take a look at some of the recent communities that are experiencing not only life transformation but generational transformation as they encounter Jesus personally through Scripture. Jakalteko | Guatemala The Jakalteko Bible was dedicated in July 2026 in Guatemala! During the celebration, John 1:1-18 was read aloud — a passage that focuses on Christ, the eternal Word and our Redeemer. Early on, many women in the community memorized Job 19 . Like Job, they had faced various hardships in their lives and identified with his suffering. The book reminded them that God remains in control and that, in the midst of difficult circumstances, their Redeemer will deliver them and comfort them in their pain. Today, they have the full counsel of God’s Word and can now see this Redeemer fulfilled in Jesus in the New Testament. They are overjoyed that the Bible has arrived in the language they were born into! When the Bible was distributed, one mother who is raising her family alone said with joy and tears: “Thank God we have the Bible in our language. Now

也许你在劳动力的战壕里, 一个合作者大胆地与你分享上帝 谁彻底改变了他们的生活。 无论你多大,选择跟随耶稣的我们每个人都有一个起源故事——在我们生活中的这一刻,“耶稣爱我,我知道,因为圣经如此告诉我”的知识从头知识转移到心信。

从那时起,我们的生活就永远改变了 这是耶稣爱你的福音和理解的力量的真理. 世界各地的人们正在用他们明白的语言和格式,为自己发现约翰3:16的个人真理.

探讨为什么“上帝如此热爱世界”会改变整个社区? 基督教历史上不断变化的现实,福音从一个社区传播到另一个社区。 故事被讲述和重播,圣经被翻译,教堂被种植,随着人们更多地了解耶稣,门徒身份加深. 圣经翻译是教会所有各部的基础.

它为福音派,教会的种植,门徒活动等等提供了燃料. 它使人们能够从模糊的上帝是谁的画面走向一个明确的理解和与耶稣作为主的个人交锋. 通过圣经,人们能够阅读,听到或看到上帝的爱在展示.

就在20年前,世界上大多数语言社区仍然需要开始圣经翻译工作,更不用说完成了。 但赞美上帝, 在过去几年里, 我们看到了巨大的进步,

虽然数字的变化令人振奋, 每个数字都代表着一个对上帝很重要的故事的人. 对于这些社群来说, 后代的故事正在被完全改写, 因为孩子们现在长大了,

这一声明值得重申: 现在人们将永远不记得有一天,他们无法以他们明白的语言和格式获得上帝的启示。 从创世纪的第一个字到启示录的最后一个字,圣经讲述了一个不可思议的故事:上帝对世界的爱,以及他邀请来自每个民族和语言的人来了解他.

当越来越多的人正在经历着他的话语的力量时, 让我们看看最近的一些社区,

危地马拉 2026年7月危地马拉献上雅卡尔特科圣经! 在庆典期间,约翰1:1-18被高声朗诵——这一段以基督,永恒之言和我们的救世主为焦点. 早期,许多社区妇女怀念工作19。 与Job一样,他们的生活也面临各种困难,并认同他的痛苦。

这本书提醒他们,上帝仍然在控制之中,在困难的情况下,他们的救赎者会将他们送去,并在他们的痛苦中安慰他们. 今天,他们有充分的神话的劝告,现在可以看到这个救世主在新约中的耶稣实现了. 他们太高兴了 圣经已经用他们生下来的语言传下来了!

在分发《圣经》时,一位独自抚养家人的母亲欢呼和流泪地说:“感谢上帝,我们的语言有《圣经》。 现在

featured.summary_zh:
上帝继续召唤 他的族人将福音传到地底 11月9日,在俄亥俄州代顿附近的第一浸信会Kettling教堂的Sugarcreek校区,33名国际传教委员会传教士站在家人、朋友和支持者面前,申明他们服从这一呼吁。

独立浸信会的受托人任命了得到充分支持的传教士,他们代表10个州,包括俄亥俄州的两名候选人,以及许多致力于圣的南方浸信会教会。
featured.title_zh: 俄亥俄州派遣庆祝活动确认33名IMB传教士为全球服务
featured.content: Participants at the IMB Sending Celebration on Nov. 9, 2026, celebrated God's faithfulness in sending 33 new missionaries to the nations. Held at the Sugarcreek campus of First Baptist Kettering near Dayton, Ohio, the event launched the State Convention of Baptists in Ohio annual gathering. For security reasons, some newly appointed missionaries are not publicly identified. IMB Photo God continues to call His people to carry the gospel to the ends of the earth. During a Sending Celebration Nov. 9 at the Sugarcreek Campus of First Baptist Church Kettering, near Dayton, Ohio, 33 International Mission Board missionaries stood before family, friends and supporters, affirming their obedience to that call. Trustees of the IMB appointed the fully supported missionaries who represent 10 states – including two candidates from Ohio – and many Southern Baptist churches committed to sending and sustaining those called by God to go to the mission field. Senior Pastor Chad Keck welcomed those in attendance, sharing his appreciation for the partnership with Southern Baptist churches to cooperatively send and support missionaries. The Sending Celebration is meeting in conjunction with the State Convention of Baptists in Ohio. Chad Keck, senior pastor of First Baptist Kettering near Dayton, Ohio, left, and Jeremy Westbrook, executive director-treasurer of the State Convention of Baptists in Ohio, right, welcome guests gathered for the IMB Sending Celebration, which kicked off the convention’s annual gathering. IMB Photo Among those who shared their stories include a couple who answered an unexpected call later in life, a couple who are returning to Albania and to people they could not forget; and a couple who moved from welcoming the nations in Canada to going to Fiji. All of them shared their stories before the Sending Celebration. Unexpected invitation to go On Dec. 5, 2025, what seemed like an ordinary FaceTime call became a turning point for Rob Boss. As he spoke with his daughter, Hannah, during her IMB training, Rob sensed God speaking clearly to his heart: “You can do this too.” The impression was unexpected. After decades of writing, Christian education, seminary teaching and active support of missions, overseas service had never been part of Rob and Stephanie Boss’ plans. “It wasn’t an audible voice, but it was so clear,” Rob said. “It was Him. It was so kind and so gentle and so encouraging.” The moment drove him to his knees in surrender. When Stephanie came home later that day, he told her he believed God was calling them to the nations. Her response was immediate. “Thrilled is the right answer,” she said. The next day, the couple contacted the IMB and began the application process. Though missions had long been part of their family’s story, Rob and Stephanie Boss sensed God leading them to overseas service while encouraging their daughter, Hannah, during her missionary training. Sent by Wedgwood Baptist Church in Fort Worth, Texas, they are now headed to Colombia, where they will serve through theological education. IMB Photo Looking back, the Bosses see the Lord’s hand preparing them long before they realized where He was leading. “God brought us together in the summer of 1990 at Glorieta, New Mexico, where we met and married,” Stephanie said during the Sending Celebration. What followed was years of ministry, teaching, parenting and navigating life’s unexpected turns, which taught them to hold plans loosely and trust God completely. “We did not have a clue about what life held in front of us,” Stephanie said. “We just knew we wanted to follow the Lord.” Their calling also continues a family legacy. Rob’s mother served with the IMB in Africa after retirement, helping inspire Hannah’s service in South Korea. Now, three generations of the same family have answered God’s call to the nations. Rob and Stephanie expressed deep gratitude for their sending church, Wedgwood Baptist Church in Fort Worth, whose strong commitment to missions

featured.title_zh: 2名基督徒女孩在特伦甘纳邦遭到袭击
featured.content: A group of men who assaulted two Christian girls for attempting to convert Hindus to Christianity in Telangana, India, has sparked outrage throughout India. A video of the incident, which became public in early November, has raised concerns over Hindu nationalists taking the law into their hands and attacking Christians over allegations of conversion. The incident took place around two months ago in Almasguda, Maheshwaram mandal, under the Meerpet police station limits in Rangareddy district of Telangana state near Hyderabad, the capital city. Two of the attackers have been identified and arrested by the police after protests by the Christian community in front of the police station. Accusations and Assault In the video, a group of men is seen confronting the two young women — who appeared to be minors — accusing them of attempting to convert school children to Christianity by offering them chocolates. The two girls are heard denying the allegations, saying they were merely visiting relatives in the area. However, one of the men slaps them brutally and verbally abuses them in public. One woman is seen sitting nearby, but she does not make any attempt to stop the men from attacking the girls. While the girls’ agonized apologies are heard, the man is relentlessly hitting the two girls alternately without mercy, even as another man is making half-hearted attempts to restrain the attacker. One of the girls has her glasses shattered by a forceful blow to her face from the man, who is not done hitting before he assaults the other pleading girl. The attackers accused the young women of attempting forced religious conversions by allegedly distributing chocolates to schoolchildren — a frequent, unsubstantiated trope used by Hindu nationalists in India to justify street-level violence. Protests and Public Response Meanwhile, the video of the assault went viral, triggering immediate street protests by members of the Dalit Christian organizations on Nov. 4 to demand the arrest of the perpetrators. Dalit Christians (or Christian Dalits) are people in the Indian subcontinent who converted to Christianity from historically marginalized, low-caste or “untouchable” (Dalit) backgrounds. The protests by the Dalit Christians were met with aggressive counter-sloganeering by local Hindu outfits, forcing the Telangana state police to deploy additional forces and use force to prevent a full-scale riot. While the police swiftly arrested the primary perpetrators, the incident underscored a deeper systemic shift: the normalization of extrajudicial moral policing. Christian leaders, political figures and human rights advocates condemned the assault and called for an impartial investigation and protection. Sabitha Indra Reddy, former Telangana minister, condemned the brutality on X. Reddy stated that objections regarding religious freedom should be pursued legally rather than through violence against women. To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . For interviews, please email us . To support ICC’s work around the world, please give to our Where Most Needed Fund . 一群人因试图在印度特拉干纳将印度教皈依基督教而袭击了两名基督教女孩,这引起了整个印度的愤怒。 11月初公开的一则事件视频引起了印度民族主义者对印度教徒掌握法律并攻击基督教徒指控皈依的关注.

事件发生在两个月前,在首都海得拉巴附近的Telangana州Rangareddy区的Meheshwaram mandal的Almasguda, 两名袭击者在警察局门口基督教社区抗议后被警方指认并逮捕.

指控和攻击 在影片中,一群男子面对两名年轻女子——她们似乎是未成年人——指责他们试图通过提供巧克力来使在校儿童皈依基督教. 听到两名女孩否认这些指控,说她们只是去探访该地区的亲属。

然而,其中一人在公开场合粗暴地殴打他们并辱骂他们。 一名妇女被看见坐在附近,但没有试图阻止男子攻击女孩。 这名男子毫不留情地不择手段地殴打两名女孩,

同时,袭击的视频也传入了病毒,引发了达利特基督教组织成员于11月4日立即上街抗议,要求逮捕肇事者。 贱民基督徒(或称基督教贱民)是印度次大陆上从历史上被边缘化、低种姓或“不可接触”(达利特)背景皈依基督教的人。

达利特基督徒的抗议活动遭遇了当地印度教服饰的猛烈反攻,迫使泰兰加纳州警方增派了部队并使用武力来防止全面骚乱. 虽然警方迅速逮捕了主要肇事者,但这一事件突出表明了更深刻的系统转变:法外道德警察的正常化。

基督教领袖、政治人物和人权倡导者谴责这次袭击,并呼吁进行公正的调查和保护。 前特兰加纳部长萨比莎·因德拉·雷迪(Sabitha Indra Reddy)谴责了对X的残暴行为. 雷迪表示,对宗教自由的反对应该通过法律手段而不是通过对妇女的暴力行为来进行. 更多新闻报导,

featured.title: Beyond the Battlefield: Veteran Suicide and the Value of Life
featured.summary: On Veterans Day, we celebrate the willingness of those who have served and are serving to sacrifice for our country.
featured.summary_zh: 在退伍军人节，我们庆祝那些曾经和正在为我们的国家做出牺牲的人们的意愿。
featured.title_zh: 战场之外：退伍军人自杀与生命价值
featured.content: “We’ll teach you how to kill. When you get back, you’re the VA’s problem.” That’s what they told my old team sergeant before he deployed to Afghanistan with the 82nd Airborne Division. The risk of killing or being killed is an inescapable part of military service. In the Army, recruits go through a formation process in Basic Combat Training that turns them into soldiers. Part of this means learning that the mission always comes first, which in turn must mean they’re expendable. First aid is taught with the assumption that at some point, someone will need a tourniquet, chest seal, or body bag. After all, the enemy also learns to shoot, and sometimes the mission requires soldiers to get into harm’s way. That’s part of the tragic necessity of war. No one would have followed Washington across the Delaware or left the landing craft on D-Day if staying alive were the number-one goal. A commander’s ability to orchestrate force in combat would break down with a military unwilling to die. But this same dynamic that makes militaries potent threatens the lives of those who fight, through the tragedy of veteran suicide. Necessity of Sacrifice We must understand sacrifice as more than mere operational necessity: Something is lost when nothing is worth dying for. C. S. Lewis famously warned of the danger of making men without chests—of a people without an anchoring morality to mediate the carnal passions of the stomach and the cold calculations of the head. A society full of people consumed with their own survival doesn’t bode well for its moral character, to say nothing of its national defense. Americans ought to be thankful that thousands of young men and women regularly sign the dotted line to join the armed forces, volunteering to put their country’s well-being ahead of their own. A society full of people consumed with their own survival doesn’t bode well for its moral character. The willingness to sacrifice that makes a military effective can carry a hidden cost. What happens when a soldier learns to put his life second, then struggles to understand its value when the mission ends? A soldier who was prepared to take a bullet downrange may think little of a bottle of whiskey, a pack of cigarettes, or opening up his motorcycle on the highway. When the Mission Ends Those who make it back from combat alive aren’t entirely safe. Veterans take their own lives at roughly twice the rate of the general population. Veteran suicide stems from a number of factors, including post-traumatic stress, moral injury, difficulty transitioning to civilian life, loss of purpose and social connection, traumatic brain injury, pain, and proximity to firearms. Alongside these factors, we should consider what it means to spend years learning to put one’s life second and what happens when that lesson outlasts the mission. There’s an obvious tension when it comes to the value of life. Christians know that our lives in this world aren’t ultimate (Rev. 12:11). Christians can face death because we recognize this life’s limits, while still treating life as a gift worthy of protection. As Jesus taught, being willing to die for others is the highest form of love (John 15:13). This is why the second person of the Trinity stepped down from heaven, took on the form of a servant, and obediently followed the Father’s mission orders to death on the cross (Phil. 2:6–8). Yet Jesus didn’t throw his life away; he demonstrated perfect courage. Between the foolhardiness that leads to blood on the highway and the cowardice that keeps men in hiding when a wolf growls at the door, stands courage. As G. K. Chesterton observes, “Courage is almost a contradiction in terms. It means a strong desire to live taking the form of a readiness to die.” We see this in Christ’s agony in anticipation of the cross in the garden of Gethsemane (Luke 22:44). Yet he carried his cross anyway. Value of Life and Virtue of Sacrifice The Christian worldview ties together the value of both life and sacrifice,

“我们会教你如何杀人。 当你回来时,你就是退伍军人协会的问题。 他们告诉我的上士, 杀害或被害的风险是兵役不可回避的一部分。 在军队中,新兵在基本战斗训练中经过了编队过程,使他们变成了士兵.

这其中一部分意味着要学会,特派团总是先到,这反过来必然意味着特派团是消耗性的。 急救的教学假设是,在某个时候,有人需要止血带,胸口密封,或者身体包. 毕竟,敌人也学会了射击,有时任务需要士兵进入伤害的道路. 这是战争的悲惨必要性的一部分。

没有人会跟随华盛顿穿越特拉华州 或离开登陆艇 在D日,如果活着是头号入球。 指挥官在战斗中指挥武力的能力会同不愿牺牲的军队决裂. 但是,使军队强大起来的这种动态,通过老兵自杀的悲剧,威胁到那些战斗者的生命。

牺牲的必要性 我们必须将牺牲理解为不仅仅是行动上的必要:当没有什么值得牺牲的时候,就失去了某些东西。 C.S.Lewis曾著名地警告说,要让没有胸怀的人——一个没有固定道德的民族——来调解胃部的性欲和头部的冷淡计算。

一个充满自生自灭之人的社会, 美国人应该感谢成千上万的年轻男女经常在虚构的战线上签字加入武装部队,自愿将国家福祉置于自己首位。

一个充满自生自灭之人的社会, 使军事效力的牺牲意愿可以承担隐藏的代价。 当一个士兵学会把生命放在第二位,然后在任务结束时挣扎去理解其价值时,会发生什么?

准备取出一发子弹下行道的士兵可能会想出一瓶威士忌,一包香烟,或者在高速公路上打开他的摩托车. 当任务结束时, 退伍军人自杀率约为一般人口的两倍。

退伍军人自杀源于若干因素,包括创伤后压力、精神伤害、向平民生活过渡的困难、目的和社会联系的丧失、创伤性脑损伤、痛苦和接近火器。 除了这些因素之外,我们应该考虑用几年时间学习如何将一个人的生命置于第二位,以及这一教训超过任务时会发生什么。

在生命的价值方面, 基督徒知道,我们在这个世界上的生活并非是终极的(Rev.12:11)。 基督徒可以面对死亡,因为我们认识到生命的极限,同时仍将生命视为值得保护的礼物。 正如耶稣所教导的那样,愿意为他人而死是爱的最高形式(John 15:13).

在导致高速公路上出血的愚蠢和怯懦之间,当一头狼在门口咆哮时,使人躲藏起来,勇敢地站起. 正如G.K.切斯特顿所指出,“勇气几乎是矛盾的。 这意味着以准备去死的形式强烈地渴望生活。” 我们从基督的痛苦中看到这一点,

featured.title_zh: 随着马来西亚压制良心自由，绝望和恐惧与日俱增
featured.content: A wave of viral social media videos featuring Malaysian citizens publicly declaring their departure from state-sanctioned Sunni Islam has cast a harsh spotlight on the severe lack of religious freedom in the Southeast Asian nation. While state authorities have scrambled to investigate and suppress the footage, international religious freedom advocates warn that the phenomenon highlights a much deeper, systemic crisis: the complete criminalization of apostasy for ethnic Malays and the intense persecution faced by those who desire to follow other faiths, including Christianity. Under Article 160 of the Constitution of Malaysia, all ethnic Malays are legally defined as Muslims. This constitutional binding leaves no legal avenue for a Malay individual to officially change their religion. For those who experience a personal crisis of faith or choose to embrace Christianity, the path forward is fraught with state-sponsored surveillance, social ostracism, and severe legal penalties. Central to this machinery of suppression is the powerful federal agency JAKIM (Department of Islamic Development Malaysia) and state-level enforcers like JAIS (Selangor Islamic Religious Department). Together, they operate a rigid, dual-track legal system where Shariah courts hold near-absolute jurisdiction over Muslims. Requests by individuals to officially exit Islam are systematically rejected. Instead of granting freedom of conscience, JAIS and other state bodies actively weaponize mandatory detention in state-run Islamic rehabilitation centers (pusat pemurnian akidah). These centers function as forced re-education camps. Converts who are caught or who attempt to petition the courts for apostasy are routinely sentenced to months of involuntary confinement. Inside, they are subjected to intense psychological pressure, isolation, and compulsory doctrinal lectures designed to break their resolve and force a recantation. Recently, JAIS publicized a court-ordered Istitabah (forced repentance ritual) for a social media figure, signaling that the state will use its full administrative weight to enforce religious compliance. Recent landmark legal battles from 2025 and 2026 expose a devastating reality: born-Muslims face a structural wall of total rejections. In an Oct. 2, 2025 ruling, the Federal Court — Malaysia’s highest civil judiciary — completely shut down a final appeal from a 47-year-old Christian convert who spent years fighting the Shariah court system just to return to his original faith following a divorce. The apex court reaffirmed that civil courts have zero jurisdiction to override Shariah rejections, leaving the believer legally trapped. Similarly, on Jan. 6, 2025, a Selangor woman who was unilaterally converted to Islam as a child saw her final legal challenge collapse at the Federal Court, cementing the precedent that her state identity card (MyKad) must permanently brand her as a Muslim. Even elderly believers who have secretly practiced their faith for decades are being hunted through bureaucracy. In June 2026, a 58-year-old mother filed a prominent judicial review against the National Registration Department (JPN) after they flatly refused to remove the “Islam” label from her identification card — despite her having formally converted out of Islam via a deed poll more than 30 years ago. JPN continues to trap her under state custody, demanding a clearance letter from the Shariah court that officials refuse to grant. The statistics highlight how tightly the trap is wound. Historical data shows that out of 863 formal applications submitted nationwide to leave Islam during a 10-year period, only 168 were granted. Legal analysts emphasize that nearly 100% of those rare exceptions were administrative clerical corrections in East Malaysia — such as a Jan. 7 Kota Kinabalu High Court ruling where a father and three children successfully proved they were raised Christian and that an NRD officer had made a data-entry error. 虽然州当局纷纷调查并压制了这些镜头,但国际宗教自由倡导者警告说,这一现象凸显出一个更深层次的系统性危机:完全将叛教行为定为马来人的罪行,以及那些想追随其他信仰,包括基督教的人所面临的严重迫害.

对于经历个人信仰危机或选择信奉基督教的人来说,前进的道路充满了国家赞助的监视、社会排斥和严厉的法律惩罚。 这一镇压机制的核心是强大的联邦机构JAKIM(马来西亚伊斯兰发展部)和州一级的执行者,如JAIS(Selangor伊斯兰宗教部)。

它们共同实行僵硬的双轨法律制度,教法法院对穆斯林拥有几乎绝对的管辖权。 个人正式退出伊斯兰教的要求遭到系统的拒绝。 JAIS和其他国家机构没有给予良心自由,而是将强制拘留在国营伊斯兰康复中心(pusat pemournian akidah)的武器化。

这些中心作为强迫再教育营运作。 被捕或试图向法院申请叛教的皈依者通常被判处几个月的非自愿监禁。 在内部,他们受到强烈的心理压力、孤立和强制性的理论讲座,目的是打破他们的决心并强迫他们退位。

最近,JAIS为一名社交媒体人物公布了法院下令的Istitabah(强制忏悔仪式),表明国家将利用其全部行政权重强制宗教服从。 最近2025年和2026年的划时代的法律战暴露出一个毁灭性的现实:生来-穆斯林面临一堵彻底拒绝的结构性墙. 在十月一个。

2,2025 年的裁决,联邦法院——马来西亚最高民事司法机构——彻底关闭了对一位47岁的基督教皈依者的最后上诉,这位基督教皈依者花了多年与教法法院系统抗争,只是在离婚后恢复了原来的信仰. 最高法院重申,民事法院对推翻伊斯兰教法的拒绝没有管辖权,使信仰者在法律上受困。

featured.title_zh: 犹太难民成为副牧师
featured.content: Werner Simonson By Charles Gardner — At a time when Hitler aimed to harm us, here was a German who came to bless us! Holocaust survivor Werner Simonson escaped from Germany just before the outbreak of World War II, only to become a Church of England vicar. Of Jewish heritage, he was sacked as a judge by the Nazis and had to endure long years of separation from his non-Jewish wife and son before being reunited after the war. Like John Wesley who was rescued as a child from a rectory fire, Werner was also ‘a brand plucked from the burning’. He was about to be executed in a World War I battle with France when he and his colleagues were wrongly accused of shooting French prisoners. But just in time, one of the latter told the firing squad how Werner had treated him with kindness, even sharing his rations with him. The German soldier was thus spared but spent the next five years as a prisoner of the French, his POW status only ending in 1920 after being put to work restoring war damage in northern France. When finally released, it was a case of ‘from the frying pan into the fire’ as Germany was plunged into despair and division following their ignominious defeat. Despite this, however, Werner quickly rose to the status of high court judge before being dismissed from his post by the Nazis when they discovered his Jewish heritage. The fact that he had fought for Germany and had won the coveted Iron Cross for gallantry counted for nothing. And the increasing pressure of anticipating arrest led to a breakdown of his health. But while attending his niece’s confirmation at a Lutheran church, feeling at the end of his rope, it was as if the preacher was speaking directly into his desperate situation. He opened his heart to Christ and found new life and hope. “In the utter darkness which had engulfed my life I saw a new light,” he recalled.(1) He became associated with the Confessing Church opposing the Nazis’ antisemitic policies and was advised to escape which he managed to do with the help of the Bishop of Chichester Dr George Bell. Werner’s wife Leonie and son Juergen stayed behind but were able to join him after the war. Being German, he was initially interned with others on the Isle of Man where he led fellow Jews to faith in Christ. But tragic news followed, hearing of his father’s death, his mother being murdered in a concentration camp and his sister Ilse gassed in Auschwitz. Werner knew little English when he arrived on these shores but attracted much interest by being ordained at St Paul’s Cathedral when Britain was in the middle of a war with his fatherland. He was subsequently offered back the post of judge in the new West Germany along with a pension for the job from which he had been previously dismissed by the Nazis. But he turned down the generous offer. “I could not exchange service in the ministry of God for service in administering man-made law; accepting this offer would have meant abandoning God’s call to me, and this I could not do.” But this humble and self-effacing man was to make a significant impact in succeeding years as he proclaimed the gospel in three separate London parishes, ending up at St Luke’s, Hampstead, where (from 1956-1965) he helped yet more Jewish people to a knowledge of their Messiah. He continued passionately preaching Christ almost till his final breath in 1991, aged 101. 1 With grateful thanks to War and Grace by Don Stephens (Evangelical Press 2005), an imprint of 10Publishing. 维纳·西蒙森 查尔斯·加德纳 当希特勒想伤害我们的时候 有个德国人来祝福我们! 大屠杀幸存者维尔纳·西蒙森(Werner Simonson)在二战爆发前刚从德国逃出,只是成为英国牧师教堂.

由于犹太人的遗产,他被纳粹解雇为法官,不得不忍受与他非犹太妻子和儿子多年的分离,战争结束后才重新团聚. 就像小时候被救出来的约翰·卫斯理(John Wesley),

他在第一次世界大战与法国的战斗中即将被处决,当时他和他的同事被错误地指责射杀法国囚犯. 但就在时间上,后者之一告诉行刑队,沃纳如何以善意对待他,甚至与他分享他的口粮.

德国士兵因此幸免于难,但作为法国人的俘虏度过了接下来的五年,他的战俘身份直到1920年在法国北部被投入恢复战争破坏后才结束. 当德国在惨败之后陷入绝望和分裂。

尽管如此,维尔纳在发现他的犹太遗产后很快升格为高等法院法官,然后被纳粹解职. 他为德国而战 赢得了贪婪的铁十字勋章 他的英勇无足轻重 而预期被捕的压力越来越大,导致他的健康崩溃。

但当在路德会教堂出席侄女的确认仪式时,感觉他的绳索尽头,就像传教士直接谈到他的绝望处境一样. 他向基督敞开了心扉,找到了新的生命和希望.

" 在席卷我的生活的完全黑暗中,我看到了新的光芒, " 他回忆说。 (1) 他与反对纳粹反帝政策的忏悔教会有关联,并被劝告在奇切斯特主教乔治·贝尔博士的帮助下逃离。 维尔纳的妻子莱昂尼(Leonie)和儿子朱尔根(Juergen)留下,但战后得以加入他.

作为德国人,他最初在马恩岛和其他人一起被关押,在那里他带领犹太人同胞信仰基督. 但悲剧性的消息接踵而至,听到他父亲的死讯,他的母亲在集中营被谋杀,他的妹妹伊尔塞在奥斯威辛被毒气冲昏.

Werner在到达这些海岸时不懂英语, 随后他又被重新聘回新西德的法官职位,并同时获得先前被纳粹开除的职务养老金. 但他拒绝了慷慨的提议.

“我不能在上帝部交换服务,以服务于管理人造法律;

接受这个提议将意味着放弃上帝对我的召唤,我不能这样做。 但是,这位谦卑而自卑的人在接下来的岁月里,当他在三个独立的伦敦教区宣布福音时,将产生显著的影响,最后在汉普斯特德的圣卢克(St Luke),他在那里(从1956年到1965年)帮助了更多的犹太人民了解他们的弥赛亚。

featured.content: Presunto delincuente, herido en el abdomen Un hombre resultó herido de un disparo en el abdomen durante un procedimiento policial realizado este mediodía en Villa Santillán. Según pudo reconstruir LA ARENA,luego de que efectivos policiales fueran alertados por vecinos sobre la presencia de una persona que saltaba por los techos e ingresaba a los patios de distintas viviendas, se produjo una persecución, y ante reiteradas voces de alto de los efectivos que lo perseguían, el sospechoso habría sacado algo de su cintura, por lo que uno de los policías le disparó. A pesar de la herida, el hombre siguió la marcha y se escondió en su propia casa. A los pocos minutos, el personal policial llegó a detenerlo y algunos familiares intentaron impedirlo. Finalmente, el herido fue asistido por una ambulancia del SEM, y fue trasladado al Hospital Favaloro, donde quedó internado, fuera de peligro. Llamados al 101. Según pudo saber este diario, alrededor de las 11.30 comenzaron a recibirse llamados al servicio de emergencias 101. Algunos vecinos señalaron que el sospechoso era un hombre conocido en el ambiente delictivo, residente del mismo barrio. De acuerdo con los testimonios recogidos, también habría ingresado a patios de viviendas y sería habitual que circule armado, ya sea con arma de fuego o con armas blancas.Cuando llegó el personal policial, los efectivos comenzaron a recorrer el sector y buscar al sospechoso por los patios y los techos, hasta que finalmente lo encontraron en la vía pública. En ese momento, le dieron reiteradas voces de alto, le ordenaron que se detuviera y se arrojara al suelo. Sin embargo, siempre de acuerdo con la reconstrucción preliminar del episodio, el hombre habría desobedecido las indicaciones y amenazado a los policías con dispararles. Los efectivos advirtieron que llevaba un objeto en la cintura que parecía ser un arma de fuego. Amenaza. En medio de la persecución, el hombre habría llevado la mano hacia ese objeto y, ante lo que interpretó como una amenaza inminente, uno de los policías efectuó un disparo con su arma reglamentaria, que impactó en el abdomen del sospechoso. A pesar de la herida, el hombre continuó corriendo hasta ingresar a su vivienda.Una vez en el lugar, se convocó a una ambulancia. Sin embargo, familiares del herido habrían impedido inicialmente que el personal policial lo asistiera. Finalmente, fue trasladado al Hospital Favaloro, donde recibió atención médica. La lesión no requirió una intervención quirúrgica y, según la información conocida por este diario, se encuentra fuera de peligro. Investigación en marcha. Tras el episodio se desplegaron las actuaciones correspondientes, con peritajes y distintas medidas para reconstruir las circunstancias en las que se produjo el disparo. La investigación se encuentra en manos del Ministerio Público Fiscal, representado por Cristian Casais y Selva Paggi. También tomó intervención la Fiscalía de Investigaciones Administrativas, dado que se trata de un hecho en el que un efectivo policial utilizó su arma reglamentaria. Versión policial. El Ministerio de Seguridad y Justicia y la Jefatura de Policía emitieron un comunicado conjunto informando sobre el incidente. Afirmaron que la intervención inició a raíz de reiterados llamados al 101, por la presencia de una persona que caminaba por los techos. “Quienes realizaron los avisos también aportaron referencias sobre posibles antecedentes de conductas violentas del individuo”, dijeron. Agregaron que continúan desarrollándose las diligencias para esclarecer las circunstancias en que se produjo el incidente. Respecto al efectivo policial que habría realizado el disparo, señalaron que “recibió acompañamiento de personal especializado para el seguimiento psicosocial correspondiente. Asimismo, se iniciaron las actuaciones administrativas pertinentes, con intervención de la Fiscalía de Investigaciones Administrativas”. Por último, confirmaron que el herido recibió atención médica en el Hospital Favaloro. Artícu

featured.title_zh: 二战日本战俘在战俘营中找到“自由”
featured.content: By Charles Gardner — When a Japanese sailor’s destroyer was sunk by the Americans in a World War II South Pacific battle, most of his companions drowned. Amazingly, even though he was sucked underneath the waves with others as the ship went down, torpedo officer Michiharu Shinya somehow survived this 1942 disaster. (Only 18 of the 200-strong crew did). But he would rather have died at that point as his people had been indoctrinated to believe that it was shameful to be captured. Nevertheless, he was badly wounded but nursed back to health by medics. In time, he was picked up and eventually taken to a Prisoner-of-War camp at Featherston, near Wellington, in New Zealand, where he was to spend the next three years, as Don Stephens records in his inspirational book War and Grace (Evangelical Press, an imprint of 10Publishing). Shinya and his fellow inmates were treated with much kindness (in sharp contrast to the torture often experienced by Allied prisoners at the hands of the Japanese). Being showered with gifts at Christmas, a feast he knew nothing about, seemed especially strange. However, he was determined not to be ‘taken in’ by the Christian teaching offered after some of the prisoners requested spiritual help and a Japanese Bible was made available. That is until he chanced upon an article entitled ‘Sorrow in Victory’ in which the author quoted a ‘Hebrew prophet’ as saying: “Those who hope in the Lord will renew their strength. They shall soar on wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary; they will walk and not be faint.” It made a deep impression on him, and he was determined to find out where it came from. Assuming it was from the Old Testament, he began reading the Bible, starting at Genesis chapter 1. Eventually, to his joy, he discovered that the profound words were from the Book of the prophet Isaiah (chapter 40, verse 31). After flagging somewhat in his search, he found himself hospitalised with malaria when a friend brought him a booklet called The Reason Why explaining the way to salvation. It so happened that the camp’s chaplain, Pastor Hessell Troughton, had been a missionary to Japan and spoke the language. Shinya joined others in his Bible studies and came to know and love Jesus as his Saviour. So much did this “complete freedom” now rule his life that prison had morphed into what he described as “a unique paradise on earth”. He never looked back after that and became convinced that his post-war calling would be in service of his Lord. When he finally returned home, his family were shocked to see him alive for he had been reported as killed in action. He had also given a false name to his captors because of the supposed shame of falling into enemy hands. Shinya subsequently became a pastor and prolific writer and translator following years of theological study both in Tokyo and the US. The Old Testament, he came to believe, demonstrated that sin is “the ultimate problem of mankind” and clearly pointed to Christ as the answer. On seeking to understand why so few Japanese became Christians, he felt it was partly due to their pride borne of believing they were a superior race. As for those three Christmases he spent in New Zealand, author Don Stephens writes: “Of all the gifts he received, the one he valued most was ‘the boundless and deep grace and peace of God in the Lord Jesus Christ’.” The post WWII Japanese POW found ‘freedom’ in camp first appeared on God Reports .

查尔斯·加德纳编著: 当一艘日本水手的驱逐舰在二战南太平洋战役中被美国人击沉时,大部分同伴溺毙. 令人惊奇的是,尽管随着船只的下沉,他与其他人一起被吸在海浪下,但鱼雷军官Michiharu Shinya却不知何故幸免于1942年的灾难。 (200人的船员中只有18人这样做).

但他宁愿死在那个时候,因为他的族人被灌输相信被俘虏是可耻的. 然而,他受了重伤,但被医护人员喂养。

在时间上,他被接了起来,最终被带到新西兰惠灵顿附近的费瑟斯顿(Featherston)的战俘营,在那里他将度过接下来的三年,正如唐·斯蒂芬斯在他的励志书"战争与格蕾丝"(福音出版社,10Publishing的印记)中记载的那样.

信也和同狱囚犯受到很大程度的善待(与盟军囚犯经常在日本人手中遭受的酷刑形成鲜明对比). 在圣诞节用礼物淋浴 一个他一无所知的宴会 看起来特别奇怪

然而,在一些囚犯要求精神帮助和提供日本圣经后,他决心不再接受基督教教义的 " 接纳 " 。 直到他看到一篇题为“为胜利而悲伤”的文章,作者在文章中引用了一位“赫布鲁先知”的话:“那些希望主复活的人。 他们将像鹰一样飞翔,

他们将奔驰,而不会疲倦,他们将走路,而不会晕倒。 这给他留下了深刻的印象,他下定决心要找出它来自何处. 假设它来自旧约,他开始阅读圣经,从创世纪第一章开始. 最终,在他的喜悦中,他发现深刻的文字来自先知以赛亚的经典(第40章第31节).

在搜索中略微浮出水面后,他发现自己患上了疟疾,一位朋友给他带了一本小册子,名为《原因》,解释救世之路。 难民营的牧师Hessell Troughton牧师曾是日本的传教士, 信也加入了其他人的圣经研究,来到了了解和热爱耶稣作为他的救世主.

这种“完全自由”现在统治了他的生活,监狱变成了他所称的“地球上独一无二的天堂”。 他从此之后再也没有回头看,并且确信他的战后召唤将会为他的主服务. 当他最终回家时,家人震惊地看到他活着,因为他被报道为阵亡.

他还给抓捕者取了一个假名,因为被假定是落入敌人手中的耻辱。 在东京和美国多年的神学研究之后,信也后来成为一名牧师和多产作家和翻译。 他逐渐相信,《旧约》表明了罪恶是“人类的最终问题”,并明确指出基督是答案。

在试图理解为什么如此少的日本人成为基督徒时,他感到部分是由于他们的自豪感,因为他们相信他们是优越的种族。

featured.title_zh: 两只卡车轮胎和一只白鸽教会了我信靠上帝
featured.content: By Mike Shreve — Tent meeting in the 80s Evangelism has been my focus for 55 years, ministering throughout the United States and in 14 other nations. God mercifully saved me during the Jesus Revolution (1970), out of a hippie lifestyle and a passionate, though misguided pursuit of truth through far eastern religious practices (yoga and meditation). Shortly after encountering Jesus and being delivered, along with another brother in the Lord, I began hitchhiking around the country, preaching the Gospel on street corners and college campuses. That developed through the years into ministry in churches, auditoriums, conferences, and tent crusades. Supernatural provision and divine intervention has always carried me, through every phase of this five-and-a-half-decade-long adventure. However, the following story is a classic. For about 25 years I carried big Gospel tents around the country. At the time of this “miracle,” I was transporting a 60’ x 90’ tent from one city to the next in an old, dilapidated bus that kept introducing new challenges to our amateur mechanic skills (putting it mildly). One day, on our way to Tampa, Florida—unfortunately—we hit a large pothole in the road that put a serious dent in the rear left rim on which a large truck tire was mounted. From that point, the inner tube would not retain air, making it necessary to stop every thirty miles or so to fill it up again . . . and again . . . and again . . . making the trip painfully slow. Adding to the problem, the other rear tire was bald, and we had no spare (couldn’t afford one). So, a flat would have brought us to a complete standstill. Sometimes, I think back on those days (when our zeal for the Kingdom outran any wisdom we might have possessed), and I marvel at the many times God took care of us anyway (like the loving heavenly Father that He is). Thousands of pounds of equipment were packed into that groaning, creaking, rusty, decrepit bus — heavy canvas tent sections, metal poles, stakes, platform, and 300 chairs—and only a few days allowed in between cities for transit and setup. No, we really could not afford any setbacks. And yes, a lot of “faith prayers” were uttered during every trip (or were they “presumptive proclamations”—not sure—maybe a mix of the two). An old split rim tire mounted on an old bus Once we got to Tampa, attempting to be frugal, I visited the junkyards hoping to find a used replacement rim. As if they had conspired to dissuade me, every junkyard owner/manager shot down my hopes with a similar assessment, “Fella, you won’t find one of them old split-rims anywhere. They’re dangerous. When you try to mount a tire on one, they can snap open and injure somebody real bad, cutting off a hand, even killing a person. We melted ‘em all down as scrap metal.” (Go ahead, look them up online—they were even called “widow-makers.”) It was the same story everywhere I went. Nobody could help. Then three weeks passed and we had to pack the bus and head to our next location—Bessemer City, North Carolina. It was a college-level, biblically-sound course on developing long-suffering and patience: stopping every thirty miles or so to air up that unpredictable tire, pleading with God to somehow supernaturally assist us in our journey by making sure none of the tires blew. Somehow, we made it—around 600 miles—stopping about 25 times. Then an incredible miracle happened! God did it and I still feel awestruck, just writing about it. As we turned into the fairgrounds area, right in the middle of the entrance were two brand new, neatly-stacked truck tires (unclaimed), exactly the size we used on the bus—mounted (you guessed it!) on the very same split rims our bus required. Talk about worshiping God—we launched into a praise session right then and there! What were the odds? We all knew it had to be God. 超自然的供给和神的干预 总是让我在五年半的历险历程中 然而,以下的故事是一个经典的故事. 大约25年来,我在全国各地搭载着大型福音帐篷。

在这个“奇迹”发生时,我正用一辆老旧、破旧的公交车将60×90的帐篷从一个城市运送到另一个城市,这辆公交车不断给我们的业余技工技能带来新的挑战(轻轻地推开)。 有一天,在前往佛罗里达州坦帕的路上——不幸地——我们撞上了路边的一个大坑洞,在后左侧竖起一个大型卡车轮胎,后侧有严重的凹痕。

从此,内管不会保留空气,使得每30英里左右必须停一次才能再次填充. . . 再加上问题, 另一台后轮胎是秃头, 因此,一个公寓会 使我们完全停顿。

有时,我想起那些时候(那时我们对王国的热情超越了我们可能拥有的任何智慧),我惊讶地看到,无论怎样,上帝总是照顾我们(就像他那慈爱的天父)。

数千磅的设备被装进那辆呻吟、颤抖、生锈、破烂的巴士——重型帆布帐篷路段、金属杆、木桩、平台和300张椅子——而且只有几天时间允许在城市之间过境和布置。 不,我们真的无法承受任何挫折。

在每次旅行中都发表了许多“信仰祷告”(或它们是否“假定的宣告”——不确定——可能是两者的混合)。 一辆旧公共汽车上挂着一个旧的分叉轮圈轮胎 一旦我们到了坦帕, 试图节俭, 我参观了垃圾场 希望找到一个旧的替代轮圈。

就像他们密谋劝阻我一样, 每个垃圾场老板/经理都用类似的评估来击落我的希望, “伙计, 他们很危险。 当你试图安装一个轮胎, 他们可以撕开和伤害一个人 真正的坏,切断一只手,甚至杀死一个人。

我们把它们都融化成废金属。” 他们甚至被称为“寡妇制造者”。 我去过的地方都一样 没人能帮上忙 然后三个星期过去了,我们不得不收拾公交车 并前往下一个地点——北卡罗莱纳州的贝瑟默市。

featured.title_zh: 利奥十四世捍卫宗教间对话，视其为人类尊严的守护者——梵蒂冈
featured.content: Em seu penúltimo compromisso público desta segunda-feira (9) na Argentina, o papa Leão XIV liderou um encontro com representantes de diversas comunidades cristãs e tradições religiosas no Palácio San Martín, em Buenos Aires. Em seu pronunciamento no Palácio San Martín, o pontífice americano homenageou seu antecessor, o papa Francisco, e destacou que o evento se realizou "nos pilares do diálogo e da amizade", elementos descritos como "fundamentais" na trajetória do antigo chefe da Igreja Católica. "Nosso encontro, de fato, se assenta nos pilares do diálogo e da amizade, que foram fundamentais na vida do Papa Francisco e que agora desejamos fortalecer, construindo novas pontes e novos caminhos de colaboração na sociedade em que vivemos", afirmou. Robert Francis Prevost ressaltou que a identidade nacional argentina "evoluiu como um caldeirão de diversas etnias, culturas e religiões, formada por povos originários e imigrantes de várias partes do mundo, que trouxeram consigo seus sonhos e sua fé: a princípio, católicos, evangélicos e judeus, e posteriormente muitos outros". "Todos eles, em sua diversidade, aprenderam a trabalhar juntos, a formar famílias e comunidades e a construir cidades em admirável simbiose com as tradições locais. Uniram a nação e perseguiram projetos comuns sem que as religiões jamais fossem fonte de divisão, mas sim ponto de convergência e compromisso compartilhado com a sociedade", observou. O pontífice estruturou sua reflexão a partir de três pilares centrais que emergem da oração sincera: "as religiões como guardiãs da dignidade humana, como expressões de nossa liberdade e como espaços para cultivar a esperança". "As religiões nos lembram que não somos feitos apenas de matéria: nossa carne contém um excedente de vida e significado. Esse mesmo desejo, que se transforma em grito e súplica, atesta que não viemos do nada e não fomos feitos para a morte. Dessa forma, as religiões salvaguardam a dignidade humana. Portanto, cada vez que orarmos, devemos cuidar daqueles que vivem ao nosso redor, traduzindo nossas palavras em fraternidade renovada", analisou. Ao fazer um apelo pela preservação ambiental e moral, Leão XIV exortou os líderes a defender o planeta: "Não destruamos com nossas próprias mãos o 'jardim' que o Criador nos confiou". O papa enfatizou ainda que a fé atua na construção da sociedade ao "educar as consciências e nos libertar dos ídolos", funcionando como um elo vivo entre gerações. "A própria palavra religião é eloquente a esse respeito: refere-se a religare, isto é, conectar, unir as pessoas. Essa relação sustenta nossa jornada através da história. Ao louvarmos a Deus pelo dom da esperança, devemos compartilhá-la com aqueles que sofrem na pobreza, que perderam o sentido da vida e com aqueles que desejam se comprometer com a renovação do mundo segundo a justiça", declarou. Ao encerrar o evento, Leão XIV recitou a oração deixada por Francisco "que compromete todos a fazer o bem". Após acender uma vela entregue por uma criança, o pontífice e as autoridades presentes observaram um minuto de silêncio em favor da paz mundial. TODOS OS DIREITOS RESERVADOS © Copyright ANSA
