featured.title_zh: 从迫害到毕业的旅程
featured.content: On Nov. 6, Titus Hassan Malika stood with his classmates and received his diploma — a quiet but powerful moment marking the end of a long, difficult road. The Sudanese Christian, who fled violence and persecution in his homeland, had received support from International Christian Concern (ICC). With God’s help, what once seemed impossible had become reality. “The support I received from ICC is a dream come true,” Malika said. “I never imagined that someone would stand with me for so many years, believing in my future when I could barely see it myself. This graduation is not only my achievement — it is the fruit of their faithfulness and God’s provision.” Titus grew up in Sudan, where following Jesus grew increasingly dangerous . As pressure on Christian communities intensified amid conflict and targeted hostility, he was forced to leave everything behind. With little more than his faith, he crossed into Kenya as a refugee, carrying the weight of loss, uncertainty, and the hope that God still had a future for him. By His Side In 2023, ICC stepped into that uncertainty. Through consistent support, practical help, encouragement, and the means to continue his studies, we walked with Titus through years of hardship. The path was not easy. He faced the daily challenges of life, the lingering trauma of persecution, and the enduring discipline of education while far from home. Yet he pressed on. “Jesus Christ has been the center of my life from the day I fled Sudan until this moment,” he said. “When I had no home, he was my shelter. When fear tried to silence me, he gave me courage. Every step of this journey has been possible only because he walked with me and never left me alone.” As he steps into his next chapter, Titus carries both a Bachelor’s degree in business administration and management, as well as a testimony that God can bring beauty from ashes, and that the Body of Christ, when it stands with the persecuted, can help rewrite a life marked by suffering into one marked by grace. “I give thanks to God for ICC, for they have been the hands and feet of Christ to me,” he said. “As it is written, ‘And my God will meet all your needs according to the riches of his glory in Christ Jesus’ (Philippians 4:19). Truly, the Lord has done this. May he continue to bless those who have poured out their lives so that I could stand here today.” To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . For interviews, please email us . To support ICC’s work around the world, please give to our Where Most Needed Fund . The post The Journey Through Persecution to Graduation first appeared on International Christian Concern .
featured.content_zh:
11月6日,蒂图斯·哈桑·马利卡与同学们站在一起,获得了他的文凭——一个静悄悄但强大的时刻,标志着漫长,艰难的道路的结束. 苏丹基督教徒在家乡躲避暴力和迫害,得到了国际基督教关注组织的支持。 在上帝的帮助下,过去似乎不可能实现的事情变成了现实。

Malika说,“我从国际刑事法院得到的支持是梦想成真”。 “我从未想到有人会和我站在一起这么多年,相信我的未来,而我几乎看不到未来。 这一毕业不仅是我的成就——这是他们忠心耿耿和上帝供给的成果。” Titus在苏丹长大,

由于在冲突和有目标的敌意中,对基督教社区的压力加剧,他被迫留下一切。 他带着微乎其微的信仰,以难民身份越境进入肯尼亚,背负着损失,不确定性的重担,希望上帝仍然有他的未来. 在他的身边 2023年,国际商会介入了这种不确定性。

通过始终如一的支持,实际帮助,鼓励,以及继续他学习的手段,我们和蒂图斯一起经历了多年的艰苦生活. 这条道路并不容易。 他每天都面临生活挑战、迫害造成的长期创伤以及远离家的持久教育纪律。 然而,他坚持着。

他说,“从我逃离苏丹到现在,耶稣基督一直是我生命的中心。” “当我没有家的时候,他是我的避难所。 当恐惧试图让我沉默时,他给了我勇气.

这段旅程的每一步都有可能,只是因为他与我同行,从未离开我。” 在他进入下一章时,Titus同时持有工商管理学士学位, 以及证明上帝能从灰烬中带来美丽, 以及基督的身体,当它与受迫害者站在一起时, 能够帮助重写以痛苦为标志的生活,

被恩典冲动 他说,“我为国际刑事法院感谢上帝,因为他们是基督的手脚。” " 上面写道: " 我 的 神 、 也 必 照 他 在 基督 耶穌 中 的 丰盛 、 满足 你 一切 的 需要 " ( 菲利浦 4: 19) 。 真的,上帝已经这样做了。

愿他继续保佑那些倾注生命的人,以便我今天能够站在这里。” 阅读更多新闻, 请给我们发电子邮件 支持电算中心在世界各地的工作, 文章《透过迫害到毕业的旅程》首次出现在国际基督教关注上。

featured.title_zh: 非洲花园中的新蛇
featured.content: ABSTRACT: Just as the serpent led Adam and Eve into idolatry by reinterpreting God’s good word, so prosperity and word-of-faith preachers are today proclaiming a false and idolatrous gospel. But unlike Adam, African preachers are refusing to stay mute. Recognizing the need for faithful interpretation of Scripture, they have drawn up a statement to help pastors stand against the idolatrous assumptions and teachings of the prosperity gospel and word-of-faith theology. For our ongoing series of feature articles for pastors and Christian leaders, we asked Dieudonné Tamfu (PhD, Southern Baptist Theological Seminary), pastor of Église Baptiste Bethléem and Assistant Professor of Bible and Theology and Director of the Cameroon Extension Site of Bethlehem College and Seminary, to introduce readers to the recently published Africa Statement on the Prosperity Gospel and Word of Faith Theology . Christian leadership is war. When God calls a man to shepherd his flock, he calls him to war against wolves. Satan, the father of lies, and his minions hate the spiritual health of God’s people, wanting nothing more than to lead the people of God from truth to idolatry. The spiritual leaders of God’s flock are called to fight against Satan’s counterfeit gospels by proclaiming the word of God (Ephesians 6:17). In God’s good garden, the enemy came preaching lies: If God truly loves you, he will give you the fruit from the tree in the middle of the garden. Eve paid close attention while Adam idly stood by, mute. Thus he, his wife, and all his descendants died of the poison of Satan. The world is under the curse of sin because of a failure of leadership. 2 One of Satan’s most deceptive counterfeits plaguing both American and African churches is the prosperity gospel, a false teaching that elevates the idols of health, wealth, and power. David Oyedepo, a strong proponent of the prosperity gospel and word-of-faith theology, says, “Healing is the covenant right of every child of God . . . sickness has no right to feast on your life.” He goes on to proclaim healing over his congregation: “In the name of Jesus, I decree an end to every toil with sickness and disease.” He assures them that faith in Jesus means the end of sickness. 3 As I’ve written elsewhere, this “idolatrous perversion of the gospel” turns Jesus into “a means to God’s full blessings, primarily of health, wealth, and might” in the present life. 4 Its widespread success indicates a failure on the part of so-called shepherds to engage in spiritual warfare by speaking the whole testimony of God’s word. featured.title_zh: 穆斯林枪手在高原袭击中杀死6人后没有逮捕
featured.content: Suspected Muslim Gunmen killed at least six people, including a Nigerian soldier, in separate attacks on communities in Plateau state, Nigeria. The attacks occurred on Sunday night, Nov. 8, in Bel village, Sho community, Barkin Ladi Local Government Area (LGA), and Lakas community in Panyam, near the Mangu-Pankshin border in Mangu LGA. Four people, including three civilians and a soldier, were reportedly killed when gunmen stormed Bel village at about 9 p.m. and opened fire. A resident of Bel village, Bulus Bot, who confirmed the attack to International Christian Concern (ICC), said several people also sustained gunshot injuries. The attack forced residents to seek safety as gunfire rang through the community. He said the attackers are Islamic Fulani herders who want to take over their land. Rwang Tengwong, publicity secretary of the Berom Youth Moulders Association (BYM), confirmed the killings and identified three of the civilian victims as Emmanuel Pam Dachung, 15; Joseph Gyang, 28; and Emmanuel Yohanna, 32. The soldier has not been publicly identified. According to a six-year study conducted by the Observatory for Religious Freedom in Africa (ORFA), Islamic Fulani militias are by far the deadliest persecutors of Christians in Nigeria. The network of militias is responsible for four times more civilian deaths than the two prominent Islamic terror organizations, Boko Haram and Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP), combined. The study’s findings challenge the commonly held belief that the two organized terror groups kill the larger number of Christians, highlighting the Fulani network’s expanded efforts to target Christians. A Second Attack Two additional people were reportedly killed in a separate attack on the Lakas community in Panyam, bringing the reported death toll from the two incidents to at least six. “Muslim Fulani stopped us from going to the farm to harvest our crops, and we are now afraid to go to the church to worship,” Mathias said. “Nigerian authorities failed to protect us.” Tengwong told ICC that no arrests had been made following either attack. He specifically accused the Nigerian Army of failing to apprehend any of the suspected Fulani attackers. Tengwong condemned the killings and called on security agencies to identify and arrest those responsible, warning that the failure to apprehend attackers could leave surrounding communities exposed to further violence. Residents and eyewitnesses alleged that Fulani extremists carried out the attacks, targeting predominantly Christian communities. Some residents described the assaults as part of a pattern of violence aimed at taking over ancestral lands and forcing indigenous populations from their communities. These allegations could not be independently verified. The latest attacks add to continuing reports of armed assaults against rural communities in Plateau, particularly in Barkin Ladi, Bassa, Riyom, and Mangu local government areas, where Christian farming communities have repeatedly reported killings, destruction of property, displacement, and threats to their livelihoods. 研究结论质疑人们的普遍看法,即两个有组织的恐怖集团杀害了更多的基督徒,突出了富拉尼网络扩大针对基督徒的努力。 第二次攻击 据报告,在对Panyam的Lakas社区进行的另一次袭击中,又有两人丧生,据报这两起事件的死亡人数至少达6人。

featured.title_zh: 在最近的ADF攻击中超过30人死亡
featured.content: Fear, bloodshed, and devastation have once again descended upon communities in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). The Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) stormed Cantine in the Madiwe sector of Beni territory, in the North Kivu Province during the night of Thursday, Nov. 5, into the early hours of Nov. 6, leaving civilians dead, homes burning, and an already vulnerable population gripped by terror. Justin Paluku, president of the Civil Society Forces Vives of Madiwe, confirmed that the provisional death toll stood at more than 30 civilians. “For families that went to bed hoping to wake up to another ordinary morning, the night turned into a nightmare of unimaginable suffering,” Paluku said. “We are deeply concerned about the safety of our population. Christian Civilians cannot continue living like prisoners in their own communities, constantly wondering when armed men will strike again. Our people deserve protection, peace and the freedom to live without fear.” Seeking Safety As news of the attack spread, residents began fleeing Cantine toward neighboring areas considered relatively safer. Children, women, and the elderly are among those facing the uncertainty of displacement, leaving behind homes, livelihoods, and personal belongings. For Christian survivors, the immediate concern is no longer what tomorrow will bring, but whether they will survive another attack . “We heard the sounds of violence, and fear immediately took control of us,” a survivor of the attack said. “We had no time to collect our belongings. All we wanted was to escape with our lives. We have lost our sense of security, and we do not know whether we will ever return to our homes again.” The reported burning of homes and looting of property represent more than material destruction. They strip Christian families of their dignity, deepen their vulnerability, and leave children exposed to hunger, insecurity, and psychological trauma. The wider Beni region has endured years of repeated attacks, killings, abductions, and displacement attributed to armed groups, particularly the ADF. Each new incident adds another painful chapter to the suffering of communities that continue to demand protection and justice. To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . featured.content: A Senegalese Christian shares the gospel with event volunteers during the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar. IMB Photo As athletes and spectators from around the world fill the streets of Senegal for the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games, missionaries and local believers are praying the event will leave behind more than medals and memories. For Carson West, an International Mission Board missionary serving in Senegal, the Games represent a unique opportunity not only to engage visitors with the gospel but also to mobilize local churches to take a more active role in evangelism long after the Olympic flame is extinguished. “This is the first Olympic event ever held on the continent of Africa,” West said. “For us, it was an opportunity to ask, ‘What are we going to do with this?’” The Youth Olympic Games, which began Oct. 31 and end Nov. 13, are taking place across three host cities: Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly. Event organizers expect nearly 2,700 athletes, ages 14-17, to participate in 35 sports and represent more than 200 delegations. The Games have drawn a million spectators, and West reported more than 6,000 event volunteers are staffing all the venues. With so many people gathering in Senegal, West and his team concentrated on preparing Senegalese churches for evangelistic opportunities. “We could run and hide, or we could do this thing,” West said, recalling an early conversation with teammates. “We decided we were going to do this thing.” The 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal, is the first Olympic event held on the continent of Africa. IMB Photo West serves as team leader for IMB work in Senegal, where ministry efforts focus on three areas: gospel engagement, church advancement and community development. The Youth Olympic outreach naturally aligns with the first two priorities. “Our approach has been to mobilize the local church,” he said. “This is their backyard.” Instead of relying on a large influx of international volunteers, though there is one volunteer team from the United States serving, the strategy has centered on equipping local believers. Senegal has four Baptist churches in the greater Dakar area. Many leaders representing the congregations, as well as other ministry partners, participated in evangelism training designed specifically for the Games. Church leaders and ministry partners in Senegal participate in an evangelism training session specifically designed to share the gospel during the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar. IMB Photo A key outreach method involves trading commemorative pins, a familiar Olympic tradition. Volunteers use the exchange as a natural conversation starter before offering gospel-centered materials. Each pin is accompanied by a card featuring a QR code connected to a digital engagement platform adapted from previous Olympic and World Cup outreaches. Visitors who scan the code are directed to online resources and can connect with trained digital responders. Experienced volunteers in the U.S. are helping provide follow-up conversations. “We’re building on strategies that have been used effectively in previous Olympic Games,” West said. “It’s an easy, non-intimidating way to start gospel conversations.” Trading commemorative pins is an Olympic tradition. Volunteers use these pins to start gospel-driven conversations during the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar. Each pin is accompanied by a card featuring a QR code that connects people to trained digital responders. IMB Photo The effort extends beyond Dakar. IMB teams and church partners are positioned in each of the three host cities. An IMB team, which includes three global missionary partners, is helping coordinate outreach efforts in Diamniadio, and an IMB team along with a Baptist church is organizing efforts in Saly. West believes the greatest potential impact may be felt not among international visitors but among Senegalese believers themselves. Senegal is approximately 95% Muslim and 0.2% evangelical. featured.title_zh: 刚果民主共和国曼巴萨地区在埃博拉疫情期间至少有26人死亡
featured.content: Twenty-six people have reportedly been killed and several others abducted in a new attack carried out by the Islamist rebels of Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) on Nov. 10, during the night, in Mambasa territory, Ituri province, northeastern DR Congo, a country where nearly 93% of the population is Christian. According to a local association coordinator, Malikidogo, more than six villages were affected, including Kangwayi, Misele, Mingazi, and Mambaka. “The situation is very serious; we identified 26 people killed, several others abducted, and many families are still searching for their missing loved ones,” Malikidogo said. “Aside from the death of many people, five houses were burnt alongside some motorcycles. We are calling on the authorities to take urgent action to protect the population.” Left With Nothing Survivors who succeeded in escaping reported that many families had to run for their lives, leaving their homes and belongings behind. “We were very afraid when we realized that the enemies were already in the village when we heard people crying and others running in every direction,” one survivor said. “We just fled without having time to collect our belongings, just to save our lives. We do not know what will happen next, and we are afraid that they might come and reach Mambasa city where we are today.” The attack comes at a difficult time for local communities, which are already facing the threat of Ebola . Residents are now dealing with both the fear of the disease and the danger of further attacks. There are concerns that the violence could also make it harder to control the Ebola outbreak. People fleeing their villages may spread the disease to other communities, while insecurity could prevent health workers from reaching those who need medical help. A local leader also expressed concern about the situation and called for stronger protection of civilians. “We have suffered for many years because of the atrocities committed by ADF Islamist terrorists,” he said. “We are already struggling with Ebola, and now we are facing these attacks again. We cannot continue living like this. We are calling on the government and security forces to protect our communities before more innocent lives are lost.” To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . featured.title_zh: 民主同盟军重返卢贝罗，在埃博拉危机中散布恐惧
featured.content: After nearly half a year away, fighters from the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) have returned to Lubero territory in North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). On Tuesday morning, Nov. 3, the Islamic extremist ADF attacked Maikengu village, terrorizing the community. According to local authorities, “the attackers looted homes and businesses before setting fire to houses, shops, and pharmacies. As news of the attack spread, residents began fleeing for safety. Some are heading toward Kambau and Nziapanda, leaving behind their homes and everything they worked hard to build. In this attack, one Christian was found killed with a machete alongside many others who remain untraceable.” For many families, this is another painful reminder that nowhere feels truly safe. While people are already worried about Ebola and the loss of loved ones due to this disease, they are now once again facing the fear of being killed, kidnapped, or forced to flee by Islamist terrorists. “We have already lost so much to Ebola disease, and now we are afraid of losing even more,” a woman named Jannette said. “Doctors, church leaders and local leaders are advising us to avoid crowded places, or avoid unnecessary visits, but today, with the new ADF attack, we were obliged to run for our lives. Every day, we worry about our families; we just want to live in peace and feel safe in our villages.” Renewed Trauma Maikengu is no stranger to this suffering because during the ADF’s first invasion of Bapere in June 2024, the ADF Islamist killed 42 people in many villages around it. The group’s return has reopened painful memories and renewed fears among residents who had hoped to rebuild their lives and worship God peacefully in their churches. The Congolese army has begun deploying troops to the area to stop the militants’ advance. However, for local Christians and other vulnerable civilians, the urgent need is for lasting protection, peace, and the chance to live without fear. The ADF’s return comes amid growing concerns over its activities in the region, including allegations that the group is exploiting local gold resources to finance its violence. According to a report by The Sentry , “the ADF generates approximately $1 million to $1.6 million annually from gold mines it controls in the Manguredjipa area alone, and it controls several other gold-rich territories. Abduction remains the backbone of the ADF’s manpower, supplying labor, recruits, and dependents, while reinforcing control through systematic violence.” To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . 据地方当局称,“袭击者在放火焚烧房屋、商店和药店之前,抢劫了房屋和企业。 随着袭击消息的传出,居民开始为安全而出逃. 有些人正向坎包和恩齐阿潘达行进,留下了他们的家园和他们努力建造的一切。

在这次袭击中,一名基督教徒被砍刀打死,还有许多人至今下落不明。” 对许多家庭来说,这是另一个痛苦的提醒,没有任何地方真正感到安全。 虽然人们已经担心埃博拉和由于这一疾病而失去亲人,但他们现在再次面临被伊斯兰恐怖分子杀害、绑架或被强迫逃离的恐惧。

“我们已经因埃博拉疾病而损失了这么多,现在我们害怕失去更多,”一位叫Jannette的妇女说。 “医生、教会领导人和地方领导人建议我们避免拥挤的地方,或避免不必要的探访,但今天,随着民主同盟军的新袭击,我们不得不奔跑。 我们每天都在担心家人;

我们只想和平地生活,在我们村庄中感到安全。” 由于民主同盟军于2024年6月第一次入侵巴佩尔,民主同盟军的伊斯兰教徒在附近许多村庄杀害了42人,所以再次遭受创伤的Maikengu并不陌生。

该团体的返回使那些希望重建自己生活并和平地在教堂中崇拜上帝的居民重燃了痛苦的记忆和恐惧。 刚果军队已开始在该地区部署部队来阻止好战分子的前进。

然而,对于当地基督徒和其他弱势平民来说,迫切需要持久的保护、和平和无所畏惧地生活的机会。 民主同盟军的返回正值人们对其在该地区的活动日益关切之时,包括据称该团体正在利用当地黄金资源来资助其暴力。

featured.title_zh: 为子孙后代带来改变
featured.content: How old were you when you first learned that Jesus loves you? Perhaps you’ve always known it and can’t remember a day when you didn’t know the song “Jesus Loves Me” or couldn’t recite John 3:16 by heart. Maybe you were a teenager and learned about Jesus’ love through a friend or church summer camp. Or were in college and went to a concert where the gospel was clearly articulated. Maybe you were in the trenches of the workforce, and a coworker boldly shared with you about the God who radically changed their life. Regardless of how old you were, each of us who has chosen to follow Jesus has an origin story — a moment in our lives when the knowledge that “Jesus loves me, this I know, for the Bible tells me so” moved from head knowledge to heart belief. And from then on, our lives were transformed forever. This is the truth of the gospel and the power of understanding that Jesus loves you. People around the world are discovering the personal truth of John 3:16 for themselves in a language and format they clearly understand. Explore why understanding that “God so loved the world” transforms entire communities → A Changing Reality Throughout Christian history, the gospel has spread from one community to the next. Stories were told and retold, Scripture was translated, churches were planted, and discipleship deepened as people learned more about Jesus. Bible translation is foundational to all ministries of the church. It fuels evangelism, church planting, discipleship and more. It equips people to move from a blurry picture of who God is to a clear understanding and personal encounter with Jesus as Lord. Through Scripture, people are able to read, hear or see the love of God on display. Just two decades ago, most of the world’s language communities still needed Bible translation work to begin , let alone be completed. But praise God, in the last few years, we’ve seen tremendous progress made, with Bible translation underway in more languages than ever before . While the change in numbers is exciting, what’s more important is what they signify: Every number represents a person who has a story that matters to God. For these communities, the stories of future generations are being completely rewritten as children will now grow up never remembering a day when they didn’t have access to God’s Word in a language and format they clearly understand. That statement bears repeating: There will now be people who never remember a day when they didn’t have access to God’s Word in a language and format they clearly understand. From the first word of Genesis to the last word of Revelation, the Bible tells one incredible story: God’s love for the world and His invitation for people from every nation and language to know Him. Get a glimpse of how God continues writing this story today as more and more people are experiencing the power of His Word. Watch the video → A New Generation Growing Up With God’s Word Let’s take a look at some of the recent communities that are experiencing not only life transformation but generational transformation as they encounter Jesus personally through Scripture. Jakalteko | Guatemala The Jakalteko Bible was dedicated in July 2026 in Guatemala! During the celebration, John 1:1-18 was read aloud — a passage that focuses on Christ, the eternal Word and our Redeemer. Early on, many women in the community memorized Job 19 . Like Job, they had faced various hardships in their lives and identified with his suffering. The book reminded them that God remains in control and that, in the midst of difficult circumstances, their Redeemer will deliver them and comfort them in their pain. Today, they have the full counsel of God’s Word and can now see this Redeemer fulfilled in Jesus in the New Testament. They are overjoyed that the Bible has arrived in the language they were born into! featured.title: He prayed for his mother's infected leg. Then his Muslim neighbours started coming
featured.summary: 🇸🇩El Hasahisa· 2022
featured.summary_zh: 🇸🇩哈萨希萨·2022年
featured.title_zh: 他为母亲感染的腿祈祷。然后，他的穆斯林邻居开始前来
featured.content: Pastor Abdalla Haron Sulieman gathered his small church in El Hasahisa, Sudan, to pray for his mother. Aisha Adam was sixty, and a leg infection had worn her down. They prayed, and she recovered. What looked like a private family mercy did not stay private for long. Word of the healing moved through the town, which is mostly Muslim. And people started showing up at the church. Not to argue. To ask if the God who healed Aisha might heal them too. When a healing becomes a door That is exactly the kind of thing that makes some people afraid. Local extremists pressed the police to arrest Sulieman, and they did, charging him under an old law with claiming to be a witch doctor, as if the love of Jesus were a kind of sorcery. Believers across Sudan shared his name and called for his release. "This is a serious violation against Christians in Sudan," said one, an evangelist named Francis Ismail. But notice what the fear could not undo. A mother was well. A Muslim town had seen the name of Jesus do something real, and neighbours who had never entered a church walked in looking for Him. God still heals, and He still uses one ordinary answered prayer to open a door no one can shut. He can open one where you are too.
featured.content_zh:
Abdalla Haron Sulieman牧师在苏丹El Hasahisa聚集了他的小教堂,为其母亲祈祷。 艾莎·亚当六十岁 腿部感染使她疲惫不堪 他们祈祷,她恢复了。 看起来像一个私人家庭的怜悯 并没有长期保持私人。 关于治愈的传言传遍了大部分是穆斯林的城镇。 人们开始出现在教堂。 不为辩才.

问治愈艾莎的神能否治愈他们 当治愈变成一扇门 这正是那种让人害怕的东西。 当地的极端分子逼迫警察逮捕苏利曼,他们确实如此,根据旧法指控他自称巫医,仿佛对耶稣的爱是一种巫术.

苏丹各地的信徒都认同他的名字,要求释放他。 "这是对苏丹基督徒的严重侵犯",一位名叫弗朗西斯·伊斯梅尔的福音者说. 但请注意恐惧无法消除 一个母亲很好 一个穆斯林城镇看到了耶稣的名字做一些真实的事情,从未进入教堂的邻居走进教堂寻找他.

上帝仍然痊愈,他仍然使用一个普通的应答祷告来打开一个没人能关闭的门. 他可以打开一个你的地方。

featured.title_zh: 食堂大屠杀4天后遇害
featured.content: Just days after the deadly massacre in Cantine, where at least 33 civilians were reportedly killed, suspected Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) fighters have struck again in Beni Territory, claiming four more lives and burning several houses in Mabalako, in the Democratic Republic of Congo. At about 12:20 a.m. on Thursday, Nov. 12, Mabalako once again faced ADF violence , with a fresh overnight attack in the Kamahume neighborhood. According to local civil society representatives, the death toll rose from an initial three to four, while more than seven houses were also set ablaze during the deadly incursion. The attack has renewed fears among civilians already traumatized by the violence that struck Cantine-Aloya less than a week earlier. The proximity of these two attacks in time and location has heightened concerns about the continuing threat posed by the ADF to civilian populations across Beni. “We are living in constant fear,” said Mulwahali, a survivor. “We have not yet recovered from the pain of what happened in Cantine, where innocent people were brutally killed and homes reduced to ashes. Now the violence has reached Mabalako, and once again we are mourning our loved ones and watching our homes burn. We do not know who will be next or where these attackers will strike again. We are even tired of burying our people without heads. All we want is to live in peace and sleep in our homes without fearing that we may never see another morning.” A Need for Security Local civil society representatives have appealed to security services to take full responsibility for protecting civilians, strengthen security operations, and prevent further attacks. Residents of Runzayi, Malondo, Ngazi, and Kibunamaru have also been urged to remain vigilant, maintain calm, and cooperate with security forces by reporting suspicious movements. “We cannot continue living at the mercy of armed attackers,” a local Catholic bishop said. “Although the intervention of the FARDC helped limit the destruction in Mabalako, the fact that the attackers could strike and disappear without their direction being known leaves us deeply frightened. We want security, not another massacre.” To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . For interviews, please email us . 马巴拉科再次面临民主同盟军的暴力, 据当地民间社会代表说,死亡人数从最初的3人增加到4人,而在致命的入侵中,还有七座房屋被点燃。

袭击使已经因不到一周前袭击Cantine-Aloya的暴力而受到创伤的平民再次感到恐惧。 这两起袭击在时间和地点上接近,使人们更加担心民主同盟军对贝尼各地平民继续构成威胁。 幸存者穆尔瓦哈利说:“我们生活在持续的恐惧之中”。

“我们尚未从坎廷发生的痛苦中恢复过来,在那里,无辜者惨遭杀害,家园沦为灰烬。 现在,暴力已蔓延到马巴拉科,我们再次哀悼我们的亲人,并观看我们的家园被烧毁。 我们不知道下一个是谁,也不知道这些袭击者将在哪里再次袭击。 我们甚至厌倦了无头埋葬我们的人民。

我们只想在家中过上和平的生活和睡觉,而不必担心再有早晨。” 地方民间社会代表呼吁安全部门全面负责保护平民,加强安全行动,防止进一步的袭击。

还敦促Runzayi、Malondo、Ngazi和Kibunamaru的居民保持警惕,保持平静,并与安全部队合作,报告可疑行动。 一位当地天主教主教说,“我们不能继续受武装袭击者的摆布”。

“虽然刚果(金)武装部队的干预有助于限制对马巴拉科的破坏,但袭击者可能袭击并消失而不了解他们的方向这一事实使我们深感恐惧。 我们要的是安全,而不是另一次屠杀。” 阅读更多新闻, 请给我们发电子邮件

featured.title: 我在這裡，請差遣我｜2026 台中場萬軍宣教年會回顧
featured.source: 中華宣教聯盟 · 宣教故事1001（中）
featured.summary: 2026 年 9 月 20 日，萬軍宣教年會在台中思恩堂美福教會舉行。這不只是一場禾場近況的分享，更是一個邀請：讓門徒訓練不只改變生命，也使人活出使命；從聽見遠方，到願意把自己放進神正在工作的地方。
featured.content: 2026 WANJUN MISSION・TAICHUNG 我在這裡， 請差遣我 這不只是一場禾場報告，而是一個回應的邀請：從聽見遠方，到願意把生命放進神正在工作的地方。 2026 台中場萬軍宣教年會回顧 讓門徒訓練，不只改變生命，也使人活出使命 2026 年 9 月 20 日，我們在台中思恩堂美福教會相聚。從非洲、中東、黑海到南島，講台上的每一段分享，都不是遙遠的故事，而是正在發生的生命現場。 有人在艱難的環境裡長久陪伴，有人用教育與生活技能扶持一個家庭重新站起；也有人在受裝備之後，預備回到自己的家鄉建立教會。宣教因此不只是一趟旅程，而是一種被福音更新後的生活。 「我在這裡，請差遣我。」 宣教不是只把消息帶回來，而是讓台灣的教會看見：生命如何在長久陪伴中被建立。 從難民青年到返鄉的門徒 在生活裡接受裝備，也在生活裡預備被差遣 年會影片分享了難民青年接受一年裝備的過程：聖經、音樂、電腦、體育與生活技能一起進入每天的學習。訓練不是把信仰留在課堂，而是讓人學習承擔、服事，並在帳篷教會中實習。 當第一批學生預備回到家鄉，他們帶回去的不只是一份知識，更是一個建立教會、陪伴社區的使命。福音在這裡成為能夠走進家庭，也能夠走回故鄉的力量。 一張地圖讓遠方不再只是地名，也讓每一個禱告有了方向。 移動中的世代，也能成為被差遣的世代 把離開家鄉的路，轉化為帶著使命前行的路 在尼泊爾的分享中，青年大量前往海外工作，是家庭的盼望，也是當地教會長期面對的挑戰。好不容易建立的年輕門徒，可能很快就離開熟悉的土地。 但年會提出另一個眼光：如果門徒被健康地建立，他們不只是外出工作的人，也能在所到之處成為宣教士。流動不再只是失去，也可能成為福音跨越文化、進入新群體的道路。 ONE BODY・MANY FIELDS 四個區域，一個彼此承接的宣教身體 年會把非洲、中東、黑海與南島的工作放在同一個視野中。不同禾場有不同的語言、需要與節奏，但都指向同一件事：教會要在真實生活裡陪伴人，也要預備下一代接續前行。 非洲 難民青年裝備、社區陪伴與返鄉開拓 中東 在艱難之地以生活、產業與福音長久同行 黑海 面對變動與流離，建立能承擔使命的門徒 南島 跨越島嶼與文化，承接福音最後一棒 從聽見，到一起回應 敬拜、禱告，也讓每一個人說出自己的下一步 聚會的最後，不是停在「知道更多」。會眾一起敬拜、禱告，並在小組中分享與聆聽。有人重新看見自己的位置，有人開始為禾場守望，也有人思考：我能如何參與神已經開始的工作？ THE NEXT STEP 宣教從一個願意的回應開始 不是每一個人都立刻走到遠方，但每一個人都能開始聆聽、禱告、關心，並在神所託付的位置上踏出下一步。 認識萬軍宣教禾場 加入禱告與守望

김승환 이사장은 “성경을 읽고 들을 때 어떠한 자세와 마음으로 들어야 할지 수많은 사람들이 이야기하고 있다. 유진 피터슨 목사는 내게 필요한 말씀을 선택하고 소비하는 성향을 지적하기도 했다. 이런 ‘성경 소비자들’을 향해, 느헤미야 선지자는 백성들이 말씀에 귀를 기울였다고 전한다”며 “공동체 성경읽기는 디모데전서 4장 13절 말씀 ‘the Public Reading of Scripture’에서 왔다”고 소개했다.

김 이사장은 “말씀이 우리를 깨우치게 하신다. 요한계시록 1장 3절 말씀에서 ‘읽는 자’는 단수형, ‘듣는 자’는 복수형으로 기록돼 있다. 훈련된 사람이 읽고, 청중들이 함께 듣는 것”이라며 “읽고 듣는 데서 끝내지 않고, 행함이 따라와야 한다. 저희 재단은 하나님께서 자라나게 하심을 믿고, 6년 전부터 교회와 신학교를 섬기기로 했다. 지금은 서울과 도쿄를 중심으로, 아시아 41개 도시에서 PRS가 진행되고 있다”고 말했다.

그는 “현재 PRS는 한국에서 서울신대가 가장 밀접하게 함께하고 있다. 고신대와 한동대, 명지학원 등 많은 단체들과 교회들이 함께하고 있다”며 “세계로도 확산되고 있다. 뉴욕을 중심으로 북미와 남미, 유럽과 중동, 아프리카 대학에서도 함께 성경을 읽고 있다. 그리고 하버드 로스쿨에서 몇 년째 모임이 이뤄지고 있다”고 소개했다.

김 이사장은 “읽는 것과 듣는 것이 뭐가 다르냐고 하신다. 그러나 성경을 연구하듯 읽기보다(Reading), 말씀의 현재성에 주목하고자 한다”며 “지나간 글이 아니라 살아있는 말씀을 관계적으로 듣는 행위로서(Listening) 풍성함으로 초대하는 것이다. 이를 위해서는 경청의 자세와 청종이 필요하다”고 덧붙였다.

하나님 말씀과 인간의 들음 들음의 능력, 말씀으로 회복

2부 패널토의에서 ‘믿음은 들음에서 나고’라는 제목으로 오희천 교수(호서대)는 “들음은 행함을 내포한다. 한국어에서 ‘들으라’는 말에는 행하라는 의미도 함축돼 있다. 성경을 왜 들어야 하는가? 들어야 믿음이 생기기 때문”이라며 “하나님 말씀은 살아있고 생명력이 있기 때문에(히 4:12), 그리스도의 말씀(비유)은 지금 여기 생생한 삶의 현장에서 해석돼야 한다”고 말했다.

오희천 교수는 “본래 하나님 말씀과 인간의 들음은 불가분적으로 종속적이었다. 그러나 인간은 보암직도 먹음직도 한 것에 유혹돼, 들음의 능력을 상실했다. 들음의 능력을 상실한 시대는 궁핍한 시대”라며 “설교자는 시인이자 사상가로서 이런 궁핍한 시대의 전도자여야 한다. 상실된 들음의 능력은 그리스도의 말씀(레마)을 통해, 그리스도의 말씀으로 말미암아 회복된다”고 설명했다.

오 교수는 “인간이 하나님을 직접 볼 수 없듯, 하나님 말씀도 직접 들을 수 없다. 기록된 말씀을 읽어야 하나님을 볼(알) 수 있고, 기록된 말씀을 들어야 하나님 말씀(음성)을 들을 수 있다”며 “색과 소리가 너무 강하면, 영적 상상력이 약해진다. ‘무엇을 먹을까 무엇을 마실까’에 대한 관심의 색과 소리가 너무 과하면 하나님 나라와 의를 보기 어렵다. AI의 색과 소리에 너무 집착하면, 소리를 듣지 못하고 자발적으로 문명과 인공지능의 노예가 되기 쉽다”고 우려했다.

예배학적 관점 공동체 성경읽기 신·구약, 공동체 성경 읽기 증언

‘공동체 성경읽기에 대한 예배학적 관점’이라는 주제로 조기연 교수(서울신대)는 “구약 느헤미야 8장 1-10절은 이스라엘 공동체가 ‘공동체 성경읽기’를 통해 모든 백성들이 하나님 말씀을 듣고 깨달으며 하나님을 예배했다고 증언한다”며 “신약 누가복음 4장 16절 이하는 예수께서 공생애 기간 정기적으로 회당에 가셔서 예배에 참여하셨음을 증언한다. 예수께서 ‘이 글이 오늘날 너희 귀에 응했다’고 해석하신 것은 랍비의 자격을 갖추셨음을 의미한다”고 풀이했다.

조기연 교수는 “사도 시대 예배는 크게 성경봉독과 설교, 성찬으로 이뤄져 있었다. 4세기 말까지는 ‘예배의 부름’ 직후 성경봉독으로 예배가 시작됐는데, 이는 동방·서방 교회의 공통적 방식이었다”며 “4세기 안디옥 예배 전통에서는 율법서와 예언서를 읽은 후 신약의 서신서와 사도행전을 읽고, 마지막으로 복음서를 읽었다. 7세기부터는 구약과 신약 한 곳씩 읽었고, 9세기 이후 비잔틴 예전에서는 주일에 신약만 두 곳을 읽었다”고 소개했다.

조 교수는 “초대교회의 성경읽기 방식은 주로 ‘연속 읽기(lectio continua)’였으나, 점차 특정 절기에 읽어야 할 특정 본문들을 결정해서 읽는 ‘선택 읽기(lectio selecta)’로 바뀌었고, 동방·서방 교회 모두 부활절에는 사도행전을 봉독했다”며 “성 주간(Holy Week)에는 예수 그리스도의 수난을 공동체 성경읽기 형식으로 재현하고 묵상했다. 이러한 방식은 예수의 수난을 오늘 예배 공동체가 참여하고 묵상한다는 의미”라고 설명했다.

성서적 토대와 학원 사례 PRS 후 식사, 환대의 표현

‘읽어주는 사람과 듣고 지키는 사람들은 복되도다: PRS/JSU의 성서적 토대와 학원 사례를 중심으로’라는 제목으로 이승문 교수(명지전문대 교목실장)는 “공동체 성경읽기(PRS)는 초대교회 공적 낭독 구조를 현대적으로 회복하려는 실천”이라며 “PRS에서 성경을 함께 들은 직후 즉각적 해석이나 감상 나눔을 유보하는 것은 생각을 금지하기 위해서가 아니라, 본문 자체가 공동체 안에서 충분히 들리도록 시간을 확보하기 위해서”라고 전했다.

이승문 교수는 “‘Just Show Up(JSU)’은 성경이 아닌 일반 도서를 함께 읽는 실천이라는 점에서 PRS와 구별된다. PRS가 말씀의 공적 청취에 초점을 둔다면, JSU는 독서 뒤 자기표현과 상호 경청을 훈련한다”며 “PRS와 식사 제공 후 JSU를 진행하는 것은 처음 온 사람에게도 자리를 내어주고 참여 자격을 묻지 않는 환대의 표현”이라고 밝혔다.

이 교수는 “명지중학교는 청소년 PRS/JSU 그룹 모델을 이루고, 명지전문대학은 대규모 채플(PRS)과 소규모 채플(JSU), 오픈 PRS/JSU, 학과 비전모임 등 기존 교육·신앙 활동에 PRS와 JSU를 정기적으로 진행하고 있다”며 “공동체 성경읽기의 성패는 얼마나 많이 읽고 들었는가보다, 그 말씀이 삶으로 발현되는 것이 얼마나 중요한가를 알게 한다. 한 사람이 읽어주고, 공동체가 함께 듣고, 말씀을 삶에서 지킨다는 원리를 각 기관 상황에 맞게 구현해야 할 것”이라고 제언했다.

기독교 상담의 관점에서 성경 속 ‘나의 이야기’ 듣기

‘들음과 멈춤과 나눔의 미학: 기독교 상담의 관점에서 바라본 공동체 성경읽기(PRS)와 독서모임(JSU)’을 제목으로 홍정택 목사(솔트기독상담센터 대표)는 “PRS와 JSU에서 가장 주목한 것은 공동체 안에서 함께 성경을 읽고 공동체 앞에서 느낀 바를 자유롭게 이야기할 수 있도록 분위기를 제공하는 나눔의 기능”이라고 전했다.

홍정택 목사는 “JSU 독서모임이 ‘읽기→ 멈춤→ 자기언어→ 경청’의 핵심 리듬을 지향하는 점은 기존 주입식 성경공부와 다른 장점을 제공할 수 있다”며 “권위자에게 받는 일방향 교육에서 확장해 성경 이야기에 머물러 있으므로, 성경 이야기 속에서 ‘나의 이야기’를

第47届新村论坛在首尔麻浦区新村圣洁教会（主任牧师朴鲁勋）举行，主题为“聆听、阅读、践行”。本次论坛以“一起阅读、一起聆听、在信仰的旅程中再次长久停留”为副标题，安排了正在开展团体圣经阅读运动的G&M ASIA and Japan理事长金胜焕的主题演讲以及教授们的专题讨论。朴鲁勋牧师表示：“新村论坛始于1997年，如今已走过了30个年头。每年通过至少两次论坛，我们一直致力于在教会与社会、神学与牧会之间搭建桥梁，并提出新的替代方案。”他还表示：“本次论坛旨在倡导将信仰融入生活，并探索学校与教会的实际应用模式。我相信，天上宝贵的祝福将临到我们所有参与者。” 阅读和聆听有什么不同吗？

PRS在亚洲41个城市举办

在由吴熙千博士主持、新村论坛理事长李相直介绍论坛之后，金承焕理事长发表了题为“Listening the Scripture, Doing the Scripture（聆听圣经，践行圣经）”的主旨演讲。金胜焕理事长表示：“有很多人在谈论阅读和聆听圣经时应该以怎样的态度和心态来聆听。尤金·彼得森牧师也指出了人们倾向于选择和消费自己需要的话语。针对这些‘圣经消费者’，先知尼希米说，百姓们聆听了神的话语。”他还介绍说，“集体读经源于提摩太前书4章13节的‘the Public Reading of Scripture’（圣经的公开宣读）。”

金理事长表示：“神的话语使我们得到启迪。在启示录第1章第3节中，“念”是单数，“听”是复数。受过训练的人来朗读，听众们一起聆听。”他还表示：“不能止步于阅读和聆听，而是要付诸行动。我们基金会相信上帝会使我们成长，因此从6年前开始就决定要服侍教会和神学院。目前，PRS正在以首尔和东京为中心，在亚洲的41个城市开展。” 他说：“目前在韩国，首尔神学大学与PRS的合作最为紧密。高神大学、汉东大学、明知学园等许多团体和教会都在参与其中。”他还表示：“PRS也在向全世界传播。以纽约为中心，北美、南美、欧洲、中东和非洲的大学也在共同阅读圣经。

此外，在哈佛法学院，这样的聚会已经持续了好几年。” 金理事长表示：“有人会问，阅读和聆听有什么区别。然而，我们希望关注的是话语的当下性，而不是像研读圣经那样去阅读（Reading）。”他还补充道：“这是一种以关系性的方式聆听（Listening）活生生的话语，而不是过去的文章，从而被邀请进入丰盛的境界。为此，我们需要有倾听的态度和顺服的行动。” 神的话语与人的聆听 聆听的能力，藉着话语得着恢复

在第二部分的专题讨论中，以“信心是因听道而生”为题，湖西大学的吴熙千教授表示：“听道包含了行道。在韩语中，“听”这个词也隐含着“行”的意思。为什么我们要聆听圣经？

因为只有听了才能产生信心。”他还说：“由于神的话语是活泼有力的（来4:12），基督的话语（比喻）必须在当下、在鲜活的生活场景中得到诠释。” 吴熙千教授表示：“本来，神的话语和人的聆听是不可分割地相互依存的。然而，人类被好看又好吃的东西所诱惑，失去了聆听的能力。丧失聆听能力的时代是一个贫乏的时代。”他还表示：“传道人作为诗人兼思想家，应当成为这样一个贫乏时代的传道者。失去的聆听能力将通过基督的话语（rhema），藉着基督的话语得到恢复。” 吴教授表示：“正如人无法直接看见神一样，人也无法直接听见神的话。

只有阅读记录下来的话语，才能看见（认识）神；只有聆听记录下来的话语，才能听到神的话语（声音）。”他还表示：“如果色彩和声音过于强烈，灵性的想象力就会变弱。如果对“吃什么、喝什么”的关注所产生的色彩和声音过于强烈，就很难看到神的国和神的义。如果过于沉迷于人工智能的色彩和声音，就容易听不到声音，从而自愿成为文明和人工智能的奴隶。”

从礼拜学的角度看共同体读经 新约与旧约、共同体读经的见证

以“从礼拜学角度看待团体读经”为主题，赵基妍教授（首尔神学大学）表示：“旧约《尼希米记》第8章1-10节见证了以色列团体通过‘团体读经’让所有百姓聆听并领悟神的话语，并敬拜神。”他还表示：“新约《路加福音》第4章16节以下见证了耶稣在传道期间定期前往会堂并参与礼拜。耶稣解释说‘这段经文今天在你们耳中应验了’，这意味着他具备了拉比的资格。” 赵基妍教授表示：“使徒时代的礼拜主要由圣经朗读、讲道和圣餐组成。

直到4世纪末，“礼拜的呼召”之后，礼拜都以圣经朗读开始，这是东方和西方教会的共同做法。”他还介绍说：“在4世纪安提阿的礼拜传统中，先读律法书和先知书，然后读新约的书信和使徒行传，最后读福音书。从7世纪开始，人们分别读一段旧约和一段新约；9世纪以后，拜占庭礼仪在主日只读两段新约。”

赵教授表示：“早期教会的圣经阅读方式主要是‘连续阅读（lectio continua）’，但后来逐渐转变为‘选择阅读（lectio selecta）’，即确定在特定节期应阅读的特定经文并进行阅读。东方和西方教会都在复活节诵读《使徒行传》。这种方式意味着今天的礼拜群体参与并默想耶稣的受难。”

圣经基础和学校案例 PRS PRS 用餐后、热情好客的表达

李承文教授（明知学院牧师主任）在题为“阅读者、倾听者和坚持者有福：聚焦 PRS/JSU 的圣经基础和学院案例”的标题下说，“社区圣经阅读（PRS）是一种寻求以现代方式恢复早期教会公共阅读结构的实践。”他补充说，“在 PRS 中一起听完圣经后，不立即解释或分享欣赏的原因并不是为了禁止思考，而是因为文本本身是在社区中使用的。“这是为了确保有足够的时间让人们听到。李升文教授表示：“‘Just Show Up (JSU)’与PRS不同，它是阅读一般书籍而不是圣经的做法。

“如果说 PRS 专注于公众聆听神的话语，那么 JSU 则训练阅读后的自我表达和相互聆听，”他说。 “在 PRS 和用餐后举办 JSU 是一种热情好客的表现，为首次来访者提供空间，并且不询问参与资格。”李教授表示：“明知中学形成了青年PRS/JSU团体模式，明知学院设有大礼拜堂（PRS）和小礼拜堂（JSU），开放PRS/JSU，并举办部门愿景会议。” “除了现有的教育和宗教活动之外，PRS 和 JSU 也是定期开展的，”他说。 “社区读经的成功或失败，比读或听多少圣经更重要，而更重要的是在一个人的生活中表达出来的话语有多重要。”

他建议，要根据各机构的情况，落实一个人读、社区共同听、生活中守信用的原则。从基督徒辅导的角度聆听圣经中的“我的故事”

洪正泽牧师（Salt基督教咨询中心代表）在题为“倾听、暂停、分享的美学：从基督徒咨询的角度看社区读经（PRS）和阅读俱乐部（JSU）”的主题中说：“在PRS和JSU，我最关注的是分享功能，它提供了一种氛围，让人们可以在社区中一起阅读圣经，并在社区面前自由地谈论自己的感受。”

featured.content: Pope Leo XIV waves to faithful from the popemobile upon his arrival for a prayer vigil at the Centenario Stadium in Montevideo on November 7, 2026. (AFP Photo) Pope Leo XIV warned students on Nov. 7 of “dehumanization” through the use of AI in education, and urged schools and university to place the “person before the algorithm.” “The process of dehumanization we are experiencing poses a challenge,” the pope, who has warned repeatedly about the need to ensure AI is used ethically, said in a speech at the Catholic University of Uruguay. Just three weeks after undergoing surgery for lung cancer, the 71-year-old pontiff is on a 12-day tour of South Africa where he served nearly two decades as a missionary. On Nov. 7, he visited the crime-blighted Montevideo neighborhood of Casavalle. The murder rate in the impoverished district is four times the national average and residents spoke movingly of the dangers they faced, like commonplace gun violence. Katherine Silva’s voice cracked with emotion as she told the pope about the violence and abuse she had suffered as a child. After ending up homeless at 15, the young mother said she “went through very dark times” and “nearly died.” “There are children in Uruguay who do not go to school for fear of never returning home,” Leo said. “In a country as rich in resources as this, children should never have to go to bed hungry... Much less should they have to suffer violence to the point of losing their lives,” he added. As police helicopters flew overhead, locals waved and cheered to welcome the head of the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics, who blessed 12 new low-income houses financed by the Church.

featured.title_zh: 世界各地的地标建筑将在2026年红色周期间亮灯
featured.content: About 130 cathedrals, thousands of churches, and over 125,000 people around the world are expected to take part in Red Week this month, with the European Parliament in Strasbourg, France, honoring the occasion by lighting up in red on Nov. 23. Red Week 2026 will take place from Nov. 15–22, with Red Wednesday falling on Nov. 18 in most regions, although it will be observed on Nov. 25 in the Philippines. The observance began in 2016 by Aid to the Church in Need (ACN), an international Catholic aid organization and Pontifical Foundation of the Church that supports Christians who are persecuted, oppressed, or in material need. The week includes illuminating monuments in red, prayer vigils, testimonies, and seminars on Christian persecution around the world. Designed to raise awareness of the ongoing Christian persecution in countries particularly in Africa and Asia, Red Week brings together those who are persecuted and those who are working to end violence and hatred against people of faith. At various events, testimonials from survivors of religious persecution will provide powerful moments of reflection about the suffering and human rights violations happening around us that go unnoticed. According to the latest figures provided by ACN, 413 million Christians live in countries where serious violations of religious freedom occur, and around 220 million Christians worldwide are directly exposed to persecution. "Faced with this reality, the pontifical foundation is once again promoting the Red Week this November, an international mobilization of prayer, witness, and awareness-raising to draw attention to the deterioration of religious freedom and remember the millions of Christians who suffer discrimination and persecution because of their faith," said Regina Lynch, executive president of ACN International. Red is more than a color According to ACN's "Religious Freedom in the World Report 2025," more than 5.4 billion people — almost two-thirds of humanity — live in countries where religious freedom is not fully guaranteed. The color red is used to symbolize the blood of martyrs and all those who suffer for their faith. In 33 countries Christians have been forced to leave their homes because of their faith while in 57 countries Christians suffer physical violence or even detention because of their faith. Each church and monument taking part in Red Week serves as a reminder of Christians who cannot freely practice their religion. In line with article 18 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, every individual has the freedom of thought, religion, and conscience with the right to practice their beliefs, free from persecution and violence. Through this weeklong initiative, ACN aims to promote one shared goal of making visible the shared suffering of the Christian people and defend everyone's fundamental rights to religious freedom.

" 红色周 " 旨在提高人们对特别是在非洲和亚洲国家正在进行的基督教迫害的认识,将受迫害者和致力于结束对信仰者暴力和仇恨的人聚集在一起。

在各种事件中,宗教迫害幸存者的证词将有力地反思我们周围发生的、无人注意的痛苦和侵犯人权行为。

根据澳大利亚基督教联合会提供的最新数字,有4.13亿基督徒生活在严重侵犯宗教自由的国家,全世界约有2.2亿基督徒直接受到迫害。

“面对这一现实, 浮雕基金会今年11月再次推动红色周, 在国际上动员祈祷、见证、提高认识,

阿尔。 根据ACN的"2025年世界报道中的宗教自由",红色不止一种颜色,超过54亿人——几乎占人类的三分之二——生活在宗教自由得不到充分保障的国家. 颜色红色用来象征烈士和所有因信仰而受苦的人的鲜血.

在33个国家,基督教徒因信仰而被迫离开家园,而在57个国家,基督教徒因信仰而遭受暴力甚至拘留。 每个参加红周的教堂和纪念碑都提醒不能自由信奉其宗教的基督徒。

根据《世界人权宣言》第18条,每个人都有思想、宗教和良心自由,有权信奉自己的信仰,不受迫害和暴力。

通过这一为期一周的倡议,基督教大会旨在促进一个共同目标,即使基督教人民共同遭受苦难,并捍卫人人享有宗教自由的基本权利。

featured.content: Dense fog blanketed our landscape on Nov. 1. The old timers say to expect some kind of precipitation 90 days from fog. That will be Feb. 1, 2027. Former pastor of the Lustre EMB Church, John Skillman, called to let our community know of the passing of Melody Nickel – Sharon's sister and wife of Missionary Dan Nickel – this morning in Ireland. Our deepest sympathies are extended to their families. Dan and Melody had been here in August as speakers of the recent Harvest Festival. They were long term missionaries in Ireland. Former LCHS teacher, Sarel Matthyser, passed away peacefully on Oct. 30, having lost his battle with cancer. He and his son, Josua had returned to South Africa to be with family. LCHS Foundation President Keith Unger emceed the Annual Foundation dinner. The LCHS Choir members served the meal of baked potatoes, brisket or barbecued pulled pork. Prizes were drawn and reports given. Keith introduced the speaker, Andy Shewey. He said the MB Foundation philosophy "is based on two principles: 1) God owns it all. (Ps 24:1) and 2) Therefore we are His stewards, seeking be rich in good works. (II Cor. 9:6-7, I Tim 6:17-19, Matthew 25)." He defined "heritage" as "something passed down from previous generations including cultural traditions, historical values, physical property and spiritual faith." Quoting David Green, CEO of Hobby Lobby, Mr. Shewey said "Legacy is what we set in motion." "Legacy is a last act of stewardship, reflecting your values, makes a statement and is a way to give past your own lifetime." He gave several family stories as examples of how generations were affected by how these people (in Kansas and Oklahoma) were "giving meaning to money." The girls played Nashua at home Saturday evening, Frazer on Tuesday with Lustre Junior High girls winning in overtime by four, and on Friday travelled to Dodson to play the coyotes. featured.summary: 2026 年六個禾場的可公開近況：尼泊爾工程收尾、寮國落腳評估、烏干達生活技能，以及伊拉克、緬甸、東馬的長期陪伴。
featured.content: WANJUN FIELD UPDATE · AUGUST 2026 把進度寫清楚，也把前線安全守住 2026 年的禾場工作，不只是在地圖上增加一個點，而是讓基地、教育、生計與社區關係逐步成形。以下整理尼泊爾、寮國、烏干達、伊拉克、緬甸與東馬來西亞可公開的近況；人名、行程、證件、醫療與敏感位置不列入網站。 黑海區 尼泊爾｜工程進入收尾 道路依在地條件改採鋼筋混凝土，地下管線溝完成；大型聚會與接待空間依施工紀錄逐步整理。工程進度以現場紀錄為準，不把規劃寫成成果。 閱讀尼泊爾禾場 → 南島區 寮國｜先安頓，再發展 團隊先完成生活落腳，再評估土地、水源、雨季條件與小型農業方向。先學習文化、建立關係，才決定後續基地與生計規模。 閱讀寮國禾場 → 非洲區 烏干達｜培育連結生活技能 HOST 宣教學校持續陪伴青年，並把信仰培育、水資源、農業及小型養殖連結成可實踐的生活路徑，幫助所學能回到家庭與社區。 閱讀烏干達禾場 → 中東區 伊拉克｜基地走向長期陪伴 供水、圍護與種植條件逐步改善，團隊持續以家庭、社區及生活需要為起點，建立可長久同行、可被信任的服事。 閱讀伊拉克禾場 → 南島區 緬甸｜以教育連結家庭 學校持續以基礎教育、生活陪伴與家庭連結服事兒童；新的服務方向仍按安全、需要與在地承擔能力審慎推進。 閱讀緬甸禾場 → 南島區 東馬｜多點教育與社區陪伴 多個社區學習與陪伴據點持續運作；兒童教育、災後陪伴、家庭關懷與在地人才培育，正逐步連成一條長期路徑。 閱讀東馬禾場 → PRAY · PARTICIPATE · SUPPORT 你可以怎麼參與？ 禱告： 為在地同工、社區關係、教育與工程安全守望。 專業參與： 以教育、農業、建築、媒體或行政經驗成為長期夥伴。 奉獻支持： 讓基地、教育與生計計畫能按需要穩健推進。 資料整理至 2026 年 8 月。本文只公開可安全說明的事工方向與階段進度；未公開人名、精確位置、行程、證件、醫療、財務路線及未定案資訊。

featured.content: El papa León XIV nombró a monseñor Pierre Jubinville como nuevo obispo de la diócesis de San Lorenzo en reemplazo de monseñor Joaquín Robledo, quien presentó renuncia al cargo. La Nunciatura Apostólica en Paraguay comunicó el sábado 7 de noviembre que el santo padre aceptó la renuncia de Robledo y designó en su reemplazo a monseñor Pierre Laurent Jubinville, quien se desempeñaba como obispo de San Pedro y es el actual presidente de la Conferencia Episcopal Paraguaya (CEP). La decisión fue anunciada por la CEP, conforme a lo establecido en el Código de Derecho Canónico, que contempla la renuncia de los obispos al alcanzar los 75 años de edad. No obstante, monseñor Robledo continuará al frente de la diócesis como administrador apostólico hasta la toma de posesión canónica de su sucesor. La Conferencia Episcopal Paraguaya agradeció a monseñor Robledo por su servicio pastoral y dedicación a la Iglesia, al tiempo que encomendó en oración al nuevo obispo, deseándole un fecundo ministerio episcopal en su nueva misión. El nuevo obispo Monseñor Pierre Laurent Jubinville nació el 5 de agosto de 1960 en Ottawa, Canadá. Tras algunas experiencias laborales, ingresó en la Congregación del Espíritu Santo y estudió Teología en la Universidad de Montreal. Emitió los votos solemnes en 1988 y fue ordenado presbítero el 17 de setiembre de 1988. Tras algunas experiencias misioneras en África, realizó estudios académicos en Montreal y París. Llegó a Paraguay en 1991, desarrolló diversas tareas pastorales y formativas; entre ellas, se desempeñó en la pastoral indígena de la parroquia San José Obrero, en la Diócesis de San Pedro; fue párroco de San Francisco de Asís y formador de la Congregación del Espíritu Santo en Asunción. En 2013 fue nombrado obispo de San Pedro y recibió la ordenación episcopal el 21 de diciembre de ese mismo año. Además, ejerció la vicepresidencia de la Conferencia Episcopal Paraguaya entre 2018 y 2024 y, desde noviembre de 2024, ocupa la presidencia de dicha institución. La Diócesis de San Lorenzo comprende varias localidades del departamento Central, entre ellas Capiatá, San Lorenzo, Ñemby, Itá, Ypané, Guarambaré, Villeta, Nueva Italia, San Antonio, J. Augusto Saldívar, Ypacaraí y Thompson.

featured.title_zh: 邮政父母：传教士儿童的经历
featured.content: Faith Cook’s Troubled Journey narrates her early experiences as the daughter of OMF missionaries to China. Honouring the faith, courage, and self-sacrifice of her parents, she also shines a compassionate light on the family deprivations brought about by long periods of separation from them. The excerpt below is Chapter 11 of the book in question, which cover Faith’s childhood between the ages of fourteen and eighteen. A passage on the P & O Carthage was booked for Stanley and Norah [Faith’s parents—Ed.] in early January 1952, only eight months after our family had first arrived back from China. It was a subdued Christmas we spent together that year, the last for some years to come. Frantic packing followed, purchasing school uniform and preparing for the long outward journey back to the Far East, this time by sea. A round of speaking engagements filled the days for my parents and seemingly eased the ache of the forthcoming separation. As the day of parting drew ever nearer, I noticed a new tenderness in their attitude towards me – a tenderness that only added to my distress. And at last came the day of departure. It would be four years before we would see them again. Photographs were taken on the steps of the mission headquarters, as all joined to wish the departing missionaries well. Norah’s expression told a story, as did fifteen-year-old Christopher’s forced smile, for in reality, the boy’s spirit was at breaking point. On we went to the station where our parents would board a train to Southampton. A large contingent of missionary personnel followed, for this departure was highly significant for the entire future of the mission, urgently seeking a new role for its operations now the door to China was closed. I found myself thrust to the back of the crowd as the train slowly moved off. Suddenly one more thoughtful friend spotted the irony of the situation and pushed me to the front to catch the last glimpse of my parents as they stood waving at the window of the train, my mother looking tense and tearful, and my father strained. Back at the mission home once more, we were at a loose end. No guardian had yet been appointed to care for us, although one or two kindly adults helped out if I asked for assistance. The Spring term would soon begin and I was glad. Some of my new clothes were too long and needed altering, and I discovered with alarm that the shoe repairer considered my school shoes beyond his skills to patch up. Never handy with a needle, I tried my best to turn up the hems myself. At last the third week of January arrived and I was on the train back to my well-loved school – a place I now regarded as home. Although soon immersed once more in all the trivia of boarding school life, I found time each week to write a letter to my parents. The first few letters were addressed to ports en route for Malaysia where the P & O Carthage would call: Aden, Penang and then to Singapore to await their arrival. Stanley and Norah treasured these schoolgirl epistles, storing them all up, until at last my father would present his married daughter with a shoe box crammed with letters dating from January 1952 until the time that he and my mother finally retired from missionary service in Malaysia more than twenty years later. These letters form a unique commentary on the development of a postal relationship with my parents that would form the bedrock of my security and development from a young teenager to womanhood and beyond. Faithfully my parents replied to each letter, commenting on my progress, chiding when they could sense my behaviour was becoming erratic, and offering advice as well as they were able. Not long after arriving back at the mission headquarters in London at the end of the spring school term, I discovered that a middle-aged couple had been appointed as guardians for the children of the missionaries: Louis and Nancy Gaussen. Understanding and kindly, they were well-suited to care for the children. ‘Mr and Mrs Gaussen
featured.content_zh: Faith Cook的"麻烦之旅"讲述了她作为OMF传教士去中国的女儿的早期经历. 她以对父母的信仰、勇气和自我牺牲的敬意,也为长期与父母分离所带来的家庭贫困而发出同情之光。 下面的节录是该书第11章,其中涵盖了费斯14至18岁的童年. 1952年1月初,我们一家刚从中国回来才八个月,为斯坦利和诺拉(Faith的父母——Ed.)预订了P & O迦太基号上的一段。 那年是我们一起度过的圣诞 几年来的最后一天 紧随其后的弗朗克包装,购买了校服并准备了远东的漫长出行旅程,这次是海上出行. 一轮的演讲为我父母提供了时间,似乎缓解了即将到来的分居的痛苦。 随着离别日的临近,我注意到他们对我的态度出现了新的温柔,这种温柔只会使我更加痛苦。 终于到了出发之日 四年后我们才能再见到他们 对特派团总部的步骤进行了拍照,因为所有人都希望离开的传教士们一切顺利。 Norah的言论讲述了一个故事,15岁的Christopher被迫微笑也讲述了一个故事,因为实际上,这名男孩的精神正在崩溃。 我们去了车站 在那里,我们的父母 会登上火车到南安普顿。 随即派出了大批传教人员,因为这次出走对传教团的整个未来都具有重大意义,因此紧急寻求为传教团的行动起新的作用,现在中国的大门已经关闭了。 我发现自己被推倒 在人群的后部 当火车慢慢地离开。 突然又有一位深思熟虑的朋友发现情况具有讽刺意味,把我推到前面,以抓住我父母站在火车窗前挥手的最后一眼,我母亲看起来紧张而泪流满面,而我父亲也感到紧张. 回到了任务之家, 我们处在一个松散的结局。 目前还没有指定监护人来照顾我们,不过,如果我想得到帮助,一两个成年人会帮助我们。 春季学期即将开始 我很高兴 一些我的新衣服太长,需要更换,我惊恐地发现,修鞋者认为我的校鞋超出了他的能力来补补补. 我从不用针指手画脚,我尽力自己把螺丝弄大 终于在一月的第三个星期抵达, 我坐上火车回到我深爱的学校, 虽然我很快再次沉浸在寄宿学校生活的三难之中,但我发现每周都有时间写信给我的父母。 最初的几封信是寄给前往马来西亚的港口,P&O迦太基会称这些港口为:亚丁,槟城,再到新加坡等他们到达. 斯坦利和诺拉珍藏了这些女学生的表皮, 把它们全部储存起来, 直到最后我父亲会向他的已婚女儿展示一个鞋盒, 里面塞有1952年1月的信件, 直到他和我妈妈20多年后终于从马来西亚的传教士退休。 这些信件构成了关于与我父母发展邮政关系的独特评论,这将构成我从青少年到妇女时代及以后的安全和发展的基石。 诚然,我的父母每一封信都回信,评论我的进展,当他们能感觉到我的行为变得不规则时,他们就会发号施令,并尽可能地提供建议。 在春季学期结束回到伦敦的使团总部不久后,我发现一对中年夫妇被指定为传教士子女监护人:路易和南希·高森. 理解和友善,他们很适合照顾孩子。 高森夫妇

featured.title: Batalha do Salado ( figuraes na historiografia medieval )
featured.summary: A celebração dos novecentos anos de Portugal convoca uma reflexão sobre os momentos inaugurais em que o registo histórico se funde não só com o imaginário lendário, como com o cruzamento de presciênci
featured.content: A celebração dos novecentos anos de Portugal convoca uma reflexão sobre os momentos inaugurais em que o registo histórico se funde não só com o imaginário lendário, como com o cruzamento de presciências tornando-se alicerce da identidade coletiva também através de matrizes simbólicas. Este cruzamento corrobora dimensões factuais essenciais para a compreensão do percurso civilizacional, evidenciando, segundo Mircea Eliade (1907-1986), que a dimensão racional do logos não extingue relatos míticos e emocionais, antes os absorve e valida enquanto testemunhos antropológicos. A Batalha do Salado Travada a 30 de outubro de 1340, junto ao Rio Salado, nas proximidades de Tarifa, Espanha, constitui um dos marcos mais decisivos da geopolítica ibérica do século XIV. O confronto colocou lado a lado os reinos cristãos de Castela e Portugal (com apoio de Aragão) contra as forças muçulmanas do Sultanato Merínida de Marrocos e do Emirado de Granada, traduzindo-se no confronto direto entre a coligação cristã, liderada por Afonso XI de Castela e D. Afonso IV de Portugal, e a contraofensiva islâmica encabeçada pelo referido Sultanato Merínida de Abu al-Hassan, em aliança com o Reino Nacérida de Granada. Do ponto de vista estritamente militar, a intervenção do contingente português revelou-se um elemento de crucial importância estratégica. A coordenação tática entre as forças peninsulares permitiu neutralizar a superioridade numérica adversária e estancar a última grande tentativa de expansão magrebina no ocidente europeu, fixando de forma definitiva o controlo cristão sobre as margens do Estreito de Gibraltar. Dimensões Em termos historiográficos e simbólicos, o desfecho da Batalha transcendeu a imediata vitória territorial, assumindo uma profunda dimensão de legitimação política e dinástica para a Coroa de Portugal. Numa época marcada por tensões intermonárquicas latentes, a solidariedade militar prestada por D. Afonso IV consolidou a soberania portuguesa face ao expansionismo castelhano, ao mesmo tempo que elevou o prestígio internacional do monarca, doravante cognominado “o Bravo”. Adicionalmente, o conflito foi instrumentalizado através duma retórica de cruzada fortemente enraizada na mentalidade medieval. A cronística coeva e a tratadística posterior sacralizaram o acontecimento, convertendo-o num pilar da identidade nacional fundado na defesa da Cristandade, o que conferiu à dinastia de Borgonha uma renovada autoridade moral e um papel central no xadrez diplomático europeu. Cronística medieval A cronística medieval portuguesa – cronicões, crónicas e nobiliários – enquanto género literário-historiográfico, não atua apenas como um mero registo de factos, mas como um poderoso instrumento de legitimação política e de construção da memória dinástica. No século XIV, a escrita da História servia de palco à afirmação da soberania de Portugal no complexo tabuleiro geopolítico peninsular. O tratamento textual da Batalha do Salado nas letras revela uma intencionalidade clara: monumentalizar a intervenção de D. Afonso IV e fixar um modelo de realeza fundado na valentia militar e na piedade cristã. Destarte, abandona a frieza do relato factual para adotar uma retórica de teor épico, contrariando a natural tendência da cronística castelhana em menorizar o papel dos contingentes lusos. D. Afonso IV presentifica-se sob o prisma da necessitas – o rei não age por ambição territorial, mas sim para acudir à Cristandade e responder ao apelo de auxílio do seu genro, Afonso XI de Castela. Tal construção projeta no imaginário a imagem de um Portugal autónomo, cuja força militar é indispensável para a sobrevivência dos restantes reinos hispânicos. featured.title: Adiós Leon XIV : la miniserie de 4 caps sobre los misterios de la fe que conquista Netflix
featured.summary: (BUENOS AIRES).- Netflix tiene disponible Misterios de la fe, una miniserie documental de cuatro episodios sobre algunas de las reliquias más sagradas del cristianismo. La producción recorre las histo
featured.content: (BUENOS AIRES).- Netflix tiene disponible Misterios de la fe, una miniserie documental de cuatro episodios sobre algunas de las reliquias más sagradas del cristianismo. La producción recorre las historias, creencias y controversias que rodean a esos objetos. Las piezas que aparecen en la serie estuvieron vinculadas con Jesús y con momentos importantes de la historia cristiana, según la tradición religiosa. El recorrido muestra cómo atravesaron los siglos y se convirtieron en símbolos de devoción para millones de creyentes. Para reconstruir esas historias, la miniserie combina investigaciones, testimonios y reconstrucciones. Uno de los episodios aborda la Corona de Espinas, que, según la tradición, fue colocada sobre la cabeza de Jesús durante la crucifixión. El documental también recuerda el incendio de la catedral de Notre Dame, en París, ocurrido en 2019. En ese contexto, repasa el operativo que permitió rescatar la reliquia de las llamas. El Santo Grial, la copa asociada con la Última Cena, aparece entre los grandes interrogantes de la producción. La serie explora distintas teorías sobre su posible paradero y presenta las versiones que rodean a esa reliquia. El objeto forma parte de un recorrido que combina la historia con las creencias vinculadas a los símbolos cristianos. La miniserie también se detiene en el Velo de Manoppello, una tela conservada en Italia. Algunos fieles le atribuyen una representación del rostro de Cristo. La producción incorpora esa creencia a su recorrido por objetos venerados y por las historias que se formaron alrededor de ellos. Otro tramo sigue la Vera Cruz, vinculada con la crucifixión de Jesús, y llega hasta Río de Janeiro, donde se conserva un fragmento de la reliquia. Las historias presentadas abren preguntas sobre la autenticidad de esos objetos y el lugar que ocupan dentro de la fe. La propuesta combina historia, investigación y espiritualidad para abordar esas cuestiones. La llegada del papa León XIV a Argentina el 8 de noviembre de 2026 volvió a poner a la Iglesia Católica y sus tradiciones en el centro de la atención. El pontífice tenía una agenda de encuentros y celebraciones hasta el miércoles 11. En ese marco, la miniserie aparece como una propuesta para quienes buscan profundizar en los símbolos y las historias del cristianismo, incluso fuera de las comunidades religiosas.

featured.title_zh: 教宗利奥十四世回到秘鲁进行为期六天的访问，他一生中大部分的宗教生活都是在这个国家度过的。
featured.content: El papa León XIV llegó este miércoles a Perú para iniciar la última etapa de su gira por América Latina, en un viaje cargado de significado personal y religioso, debido al estrecho vínculo que mantiene con esta nación sudamericana, donde vivió durante más de dos décadas y desarrolló gran parte de su trayectoria dentro de la Iglesia católica. La visita representa un reencuentro del pontífice con el país que considera parte fundamental de su historia personal y espiritual. En territorio peruano comenzó su labor como misionero, asumió posteriormente responsabilidades eclesiásticas de mayor importancia, llegó a convertirse en obispo y obtuvo la nacionalidad peruana. Después de cumplir compromisos en Uruguay y Argentina, León XIV permanecerá seis días en Perú, convirtiendo esta etapa en la más extensa de su recorrido sudamericano. Durante su estadía tiene previsto visitar Lima, Cusco, Pucallpa y Chiclayo, ciudades que forman parte de una agenda orientada a los encuentros religiosos, las actividades institucionales y el acercamiento con diferentes comunidades. Uno de los momentos más significativos del recorrido será su regreso a Chiclayo, donde ejerció como obispo durante ocho años, entre 2015 y 2023. En esa diócesis construyó importantes vínculos con la población y desarrolló una labor pastoral que dejó una huella en su trayectoria religiosa. UNA BIENVENIDA CON HONORES Y MUESTRAS DE CARIÑO El avión que trasladaba al Santo Padre desde Buenos Aires aterrizó a las 17:00 horas locales (22:00 GMT) en el aeropuerto internacional Jorge Chávez, ubicado en la provincia constitucional del Callao, que sirve a la capital peruana. A su llegada, el pontífice fue recibido por la presidenta de Perú, Keiko Fujimori, acompañada por el ministro de Relaciones Exteriores, Carlos Espá, quienes participaron en el acto oficial de bienvenida. La recepción estuvo acompañada de gestos de afecto y muestras de cercanía por parte de la población. Una pareja de niños entregó un ramo de flores al papa, mientras el coro infantil de Sinfonía por el Perú interpretaba una canción para darle la bienvenida. Este proyecto musical, impulsado por el tenor peruano Juan Diego Flórez, promueve la educación artística de niños y jóvenes, especialmente de aquellos que proceden de familias con recursos económicos limitados. En otro momento emotivo de la ceremonia, León XIV se apartó brevemente de la alfombra roja para acercarse a un grupo de menores huérfanos que viven en albergues estatales. El gesto permitió observar la cercanía del pontífice con los niños y su interés por saludar personalmente a quienes participaron en el recibimiento. AGENDA OFICIAL Y PRIMER MENSAJE A LOS PERUANOS Tras concluir las actividades en el aeropuerto, el papa se trasladará al centro histórico de Lima para sostener un encuentro con la presidenta Keiko Fujimori en el Palacio de Gobierno, donde también tendrá una breve audiencia con integrantes del gabinete ministerial. El recorrido hacia el centro de la capital incluirá un desplazamiento en el papamóvil por algunas de las principales calles del casco antiguo, permitiendo que los ciudadanos puedan observar y saludar al líder de la Iglesia católica durante su paso por la ciudad. La llegada a la Plaza Mayor de Lima será otro de los momentos destacados de la jornada, debido al significado histórico y político de este espacio, donde se encuentra la sede del Ejecutivo peruano.

featured.title_zh: 犹太军医在目睹病人的勇气后归信耶稣
featured.content: Pastor Peter Colon portraying Major Rossvally in the movie of his story By Charles Gardner — A Jewish army surgeon was amazed by the courage of a young soldier badly wounded in the Battle of Gettysburg during the American Civil War (1861-65). Dr Max Rossvally was forced to amputate both a leg and arm in a bid to save the boy’s life. But it changed his own life. For the 17-year-old Drummer Boy – too young for frontline duty – refused chloroform or brandy to dull the pain. Charlie Coulson chose instead to trust in Jesus, his Lord and Saviour. The doctor – an army major and Orthodox Jew – was understandably stunned by the boy’s bravery, as well as his boldness in declaring his faith in Christ and imploring the officer (whom he knew to be Jewish) to put his own trust in Jesus, since he was also the Jewish Messiah. Max, however, was shaken rigid, and in a great dilemma, as he had always been taught to hate Jesus. For his people had largely rejected him as an ‘impostor’ and false Messiah. Charlie died just days later, apparently more concerned for the doctor’s eternal destiny than for his own painful exit from this life. Ten years later, Max found himself in a barber’s chair in New York once more being urged to trust in Jesus. Having explained the gospel, the barber promised to pray for him and said that, whenever he came in contact with a Jew, he felt it his duty to introduce him to the one who came for “the lost sheep of Israel” (Matthew 10:6). The surgeon subsequently boarded a train for a business meeting in Washington, where a newspaper advertisement drew him to a ‘revival’ service where the preacher echoed the messages he had heard from the barber and the boy soldier, leaving him in tears. He agonised at home in prayer for some time afterwards, struggling most of all with the thought that, if he accepted Christ, he would be going against all the advice and teaching he had known, not to mention the Jewish community as a whole. But he finally became convinced that Jesus was indeed the fulfilment of Old Testament prophecies (in particular, Genesis 49:10, Micah 5:2 and Isaiah 7:14). So he prayed: “O Lord God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. You know I am sincere in this thing. If Jesus Christ is the Son of God, reveal him to me this night, and I will accept him as my Messiah.” A long battle ensued, but his doubts were eventually replaced by joy and happiness as he praised God that he had found the true Shiloh, Ruler of Israel and Emmanuel. He was to pay a high price, however, as do all who follow Christ. His wife walked out on him; his parents disowned him. But he never gave up hope as he constantly prayed and reached out to his family. After 54 days, his wife joined him as a disciple of Jesus and, in time, his daughter also became a believer. But his son disowned him for many years until he was eventually reconciled both with his earthly and heavenly Father. In an extraordinary sequel some 18 months after he came to Christ, Max met up with Mrs Coulson, the mother of his dying young patient all those years earlier on the battlefield. With great joy, he was able to share how her son had set him on the path to a glorious future in Christ, which was to touch lives across the world, including my home county of Yorkshire in England. In fact, he came to live in Leeds to reach out to the Jewish community there and is buried at Lawnswood Cemetery in the city. An Irish friend of mine, Colin Nevin, has visited the grave, which includes an excerpt from one of the doctor’s hymns, I am Coming Soon, and was able to give a copy of Max’s story to a caretaker, so continuing the evangelist’s legacy more than a century after his death in 1892, aged 64. A 54-minute movie – Rossvally: From the Synagogue to the Saviour – has been produced on DVD and can apparently be ordered online. featured.content_zh:
牧师彼得·科隆在他的故事电影"查尔斯·加德纳"(By Charles Gardner)中描绘了罗斯瓦利少校——一位犹太军队外科医生对美国内战期间格底斯堡战役(1861-65)中一名年轻士兵严重受伤的勇气感到惊讶. Max Rossvally医生被迫截肢, 但这改变了他自己的生活。

对于17岁的Drummer Boy — — 年龄太小,无法承担前线任务 — — 拒绝氯仿或白兰地来消磨疼痛。 查理·科尔森选择了信任耶稣,他的主和救世主.

这位医生是一名陆军少校和正统犹太人,对男孩的勇敢以及他大胆地宣布对基督的信仰,恳求军官(他知道是犹太人)相信耶稣是可以理解的,因为他也是犹太弥赛亚。 然而,马克思被动摇僵硬,陷入了巨大的困境,因为他一直被教导要憎恨耶稣.

他的宗族曾否认他是一个 " 骗子 " 和假的弥赛亚。 Charlie在几天后就去世了,显然更关心医生的永恒命运,而不是他自己痛苦地离开这一生。 10年后,马克思发现自己在纽约的理发师座椅上再次被敦促信任耶稣.

在解释了福音之后,理发师答应为他祈祷,并说每当他与一个犹太人接触时,他觉得有义务将他介绍给前来寻找“迷失的以色列羊”的人(Matthew 10:6)。

外科医生随后登上火车在华盛顿举行商务会议,报纸的广告将他引向 " 复活 " 服务,传教士重复了他从理发师和男孩士兵那里听到的信息,使他流泪。

他在家里苦苦地祈祷了一段时间,他首先想到,如果他接受基督,他将反对他所知道的所有建议和教导,更不用说整个犹太社区了。 但他最终确信耶稣确实是"旧约预言"的实现(特别是创世纪49:10,米迦5:2和以赛亚7:14).

他就祈祷说:易卜拉欣、易司哈格、叶尔孤白的主啊! 你知道我对这件事很真诚 如果耶稣基督是上帝之子,那么今晚把他告诉我,我将接受他为我的弥赛亚。” 一场漫长的战斗随之而来,但他的疑虑最终被欢乐和幸福所取代,因为他称赞上帝找到了真正的希洛,以色列统治者和埃马纽埃尔.

但他要付出高昂的代价,跟随基督的所有人一样。 他的妻子抛弃了他;他的父母抛弃了他。 但是,他从未放弃过希望,因为他不断祈祷和联系家人。 在54天后,他的妻子作为耶稣的门徒加入了他,在时间上,他的女儿也成为了信徒.

但他的儿子与他断绝关系多年,直到他最终与他的大地父和天父都和解. 在他来到基督的大约18个月之后的一段非凡续集中,马克思在战场上遇见了那些年前他死去的年轻病人的母亲科尔森夫人.

他怀着极大的喜悦,得以分享她儿子如何使他踏上基督辉煌未来的道路,这就是触摸世界各地的生活,包括我的家乡英格兰约克郡. 事实上,他来到利兹居住,向那里的犹太社区伸出援手,并被埋在城内的草坪林墓地.

我的一个爱尔兰朋友科林·内文参观了这个坟墓,其中包括医生颂歌"I am Coming Soon"的节录,并且能够把马克思的故事复制给看守人,因此在1892年去世后一个多世纪的福音派传承下来,享年64岁.

一部54分钟的电影 — — Rossvally: 从Synagogue到救世主 — 已经在DVD上制作,显然可以在网上订购. 在目睹病人的勇气首次出现在上帝的报告之后,

featured.content: 2026 WANJUN MISSION · KAOHSIUNG RECAP 教會・差會 本為一家 2026 高雄武昌教會萬軍宣教年會回顧｜在敬拜、分享與禱告中，再次回應走向萬民的呼召。 OCTOBER 7 · KAOHSIUNG 同心聚集，看見教會與禾場彼此相連 10 月 7 日晚間，弟兄姊妹在高雄武昌教會相聚。從敬拜、信息到禾場分享，整場聚會不只是一次事工報告，更是一個彼此提醒的時刻： 宣教不是少數人的遠方故事，而是教會一同領受、一同承擔的使命。 當眾人舉手回應、安靜禱告，也聆聽不同禾場仍在發生的故事，我們再次看見：每一份守望、每一次同行、每一個願意踏出的腳步，都能成為福音繼續向前的力量。 「教會與差會彼此連結，才能把所領受的使命，走成一條長久的路。」 DATE 2026 年 10 月 7 日 PLACE 高雄武昌教會 PHOTO STORY 精選影像紀實 — 一同敬拜，也一同回應 — 從信息出發，再次思想教會與宣教彼此同行的關係。 會眾在聚會中舉手回應，一同守望禾場。 不同年齡的弟兄姊妹一同投入敬拜與分享。 透過地圖與現場分享，看見宣教足跡彼此相連。 生命見證讓遠方的故事，成為眼底真實的同行。 從長期陪伴與生活扎根，看見禾場一步一步向前。 NEXT GATHERING 下一場，10 月 18 日新竹見 延續這份感動，邀請您走進第 4 場年會，一同聆聽、禱告並回應呼召。 前往【新竹場】聚會資訊

featured.title: 從硬土到盼望｜伊拉克、尼泊爾與衣索比亞的生活宣教
featured.source: 中華宣教聯盟 · 宣教故事1001（中）
featured.summary: 從伊拉克滴灌果樹、尼泊爾摩西計畫，到衣索比亞 JOY 農場的拓荒記憶，看見萬軍如何在生活中學習、同行，使福音在硬土扎根。
featured.content: WANJUN FIELD NOTES · 2026 在硬土上，把福音活成看得見的盼望 從伊拉克的滴灌果樹、尼泊爾摩西計畫的基地建設，到衣索比亞 JOY 農場留下的拓荒經驗；三片土地，見證同一個方向：進入生活、長久同行，使福音在當地扎根。 萬軍走進的禾場，常是環境艱難、資源有限，也少有人願意長期留下的地方。近期資料讓我們再次看見：宣教並不只發生在講台上，也發生在一條水管、一棵樹苗、一棟正在成形的建築，以及一次次不放棄的學習裡。 IRAQ · 伊拉克 讓乾旱土地重新長出盼望 近期農場以滴灌方式照顧近萬棵橄欖、葡萄等樹苗，整體存活率約七成五。下一階段將持續面對施肥、病蟲害與果實保護。這不只是農業成果，更是與社區建立信任、陪伴家庭走向穩定生活的一條路。 NEPAL · 尼泊爾 基地不是終點，而是承接生命的空間 奇旺約七公頃的摩西計畫基地持續推進，道路與地下管線等基礎工程已逐步完成，主要接待空間進入結構與細部施工階段；Golden Himal Palace 與多功能聚會空間則依現場條件分期規劃。工程的目的，是預備接待、培訓、退修與在地生計的平台。 ETHIOPIA · 衣索比亞 從一顆雞蛋開始的生活宣教 早年萬軍在衣索比亞建立 JOY 農場，引進生態養雞與發酵床技術，高峰期飼養逾三千隻雞，並由同工一家一家拜訪商店與餐廳，建立穩定的銷售關係。農場留下的不只是產業紀錄，更是一段學習在陌生文化中誠實工作、與人同行的拓荒歷史。 MISSION DNA · 萬軍的核心 生活就是宣教：不會的就學，會的彼此配搭 王老師常提醒同工，盡心盡力不是抽象口號。禾場需要農業，就學農業；需要水電與工程，就進到現場跟著專業師傅學。宣教士不是只把一篇信息帶到遠方，而是願意與當地人同吃、同住、同勞動，在最平凡的生活裡把基督的愛活出來。 「不會的就趕快去學；會的帶著不會的，彼此配搭。」 農場、建築、生計與慈善都很重要，但它們不是事工的終點。萬軍始終要問：這份投入是否真正承接生命、建立門徒，並使福音在當地成為能夠繼續傳承的根基？這也是衣索比亞的經驗，留給今天每一個禾場最深的提醒。 PRAY · PARTICIPATE · SUPPORT 請與我們一起守望 為伊拉克禱告 求主保守樹苗、農作與社區關係，使乾旱之地持續長出生命。 為尼泊爾禱告 求主賜下施工安全、智慧與合一，讓每個空間按真正需要成形。 為禾場同工禱告 求主使眾人忠心學習、彼此配搭，在生活中成為福音的見證。 認識伊拉克禾場 認識尼泊爾摩西計畫 認識衣索比亞禾場 資料整理至2026年9月30日。為保護前線安全，本文不公開同工姓名、精確位置、行程、醫療、財務及未定案資訊；工程進度以現場最新紀錄為準。

featured.title_zh: Patrick Nagatani：通过色彩、摄影和艺术进行的精神探索
featured.content: Arriving in Albuquerque, New Mexico, in 2009, I was fortunate to catch the final chapter of artist and photographer Patrick Nagatani’ s remarkable career before his death from cancer in 2017. As one of my favorite modern photographers, Nagatani fascinated me with his unique artistic vision, his imaginative compositions, and his ability to transform his photography into extraordinary works of art. Watching him at gallery openings was a pleasure. He was cordial, kind, and genuinely responsive to those who engaged him. There was something refreshing about an artist of his stature who remained approachable, thoughtful, and seemingly delighted to discuss his work. An Artist Shaped by History Photo credit: Grahm Howe, 1979. Patrick Ryoichi Nagatani was born on August 19, 1945, in Chicago, Illinois, only days after the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki. His Japanese American parents had experienced incarceration during World War II, and the legacy of displacement, cultural identity, and nuclear destruction would profoundly influence his artistic imagination. Raised Catholic, Nagatani eventually moved with his family to Los Angeles. He studied at UCLA, earning his Master of Fine Arts in 1980. His early professional experience included model-making for Hollywood productions, helping establish the theatrical techniques that later distinguished his photography. In 1987, he moved to Albuquerque to teach at the University of New Mexico , where he became an influential professor and internationally recognized artist. His celebrated Nuclear Enchantment series examined the disturbing relationship between New Mexico’s landscapes and the nuclear industry. Other projects investigated Japanese American incarceration, archaeology, cultural memory, and the uncertainty of photographic truth. ‘Generation to Generation’, Strategic Defense Initiative (SDI) Nuclear Powered Vehicles, West Mesa, Albuquerque, New Mexico, 1991 & 1993, Chromogenic print (Ilfocolor Deluxe), 17 X 22 and 27 3/4 X 34 1/4 My interest in Nagatani extends beyond the artistry of his photographs—the theatrical tableaux, vibrant colors, and beautifully constructed compositions—to what I perceive as an underlying spiritual search. Throughout his career, questions of identity, mortality, healing, and transcendence surfaced repeatedly. Though not every work was explicitly religious, I suggest that there’s a longing to discover meaning beyond the material world. One early example is his series Colorful Cathedrals (1980–1983), which invites consideration of the relationship between artistic creation and spiritual imagination. Colorful Cathedrals: Light and the Sacred Nagatani’s Colorful Cathedrals emerged during his early experimentation with color photography and constructed imagery. The series was exhibited in Los Angeles and elsewhere, including a 1983 exhibition at the Arco Center for Visual Arts. His artistic practice during this period involved manipulating photographic environments rather than merely documenting existing scenes. Using constructed arrangements, controlled lighting, and photographic experimentation, he explored how color could transform visual experience. Canterbury #1, Kent, England, 1981, 36 X 33 X 2 1/2, nine P-12 Cibachrome prints from original SX-70’s with mixed media (oils, enamels, watercolors, sprayed and selectively hand colored) For me, the title of the series suggests something spiritually evocative. Cathedrals have historically served as architectural expressions of Christian theology, with light and color—particularly through stained glass—symbolizing divine illumination. Having graduated at Canterbury Christchurch University, with an Evensong service at Canterbury Cathedral, I’m drawn to his “Canterbury #1” work. Patrick Nagatani juxtaposes the grandeur of a Gothic cathedral with human hands holding yellow cards, suggesting a tension between sacred architecture and humanity’s search for spiritual meaning. 2009年抵达新墨西哥州阿尔布开克, 我有幸在2017年因癌症去世前, 作为我最喜欢的现代摄影师之一,那加塔尼用他独特的艺术眼光,想象力的构思,以及把他的摄影改造为非凡的艺术作品的能力,让我着迷.

在画廊的开幕式上看着他真是荣幸 他对雇用他的人是真诚、善良和真诚的。 有一些令人振奋的东西 关于他的地位 艺术家保持接触, 深思熟虑, 似乎很高兴讨论他的作品。 An Artist shaped by History Photo credit: Grahm Howe, 1979 (英语).

帕特里克·里约伊奇·纳加塔尼于1945年8月19日出生于伊利诺伊州芝加哥,距广岛和长崎原子弹爆炸仅几天后. 他的日本裔美国父母在二战期间曾遭受过监禁,流离失所,文化认同和核毁灭的遗留影响将深刻影响他的艺术想象.

养成天主教徒,那加塔尼最终随家人移居洛杉矶. 他在加州大学洛杉矶分校学习,1980年挣得他的美术硕士. 他早期的专业经验包括为好莱坞的制作制作模特,帮助建立后来将他的摄影区分开的戏剧技术.

1987年,他搬到阿尔伯克基,在新墨西哥大学任教,在那里他成为了一位有影响力的教授和国际知名的艺术家. 他的著名的"核魅力"系列研究了新墨西哥州地貌与核工业之间的令人不安的关系.

其他项目调查了日本裔美国人的监禁,考古,文化记忆,以及照片真相的不确定性.

" 代代相传 " ,战略防卫倡议核动力车辆,西梅萨,阿尔布克尔克,新墨西哥,1991年和1993年,Chromogenic print(Ifocolor Deluxe),17 X 22和27 3/4 X 34 1/4 我对那加塔尼的兴趣 超越了他的照片的艺术性 戏剧桌布 充满活力的色彩 和美丽的构思

一个早期的例子就是他的系列"彩色大教堂"(1980年-1983年),这请人们考虑艺术创作与精神想象之间的关系. 彩色大教堂:光明与圣洁的那加塔尼的彩色大教堂在他早期的彩色摄影和构筑图像实验中出现.

该系列在洛杉矶和其他地方展出,包括1983年在Arco视觉艺术中心展出. 他在此期间的艺术实践涉及操纵摄影环境,而不仅仅是记录现有的场景. 他利用构建的安排,受控的照明,以及摄影实验,探索了色彩如何转化视觉体验.

featured.summary_zh:
